grupos.texto:
WHAT: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently does nothing when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`.
WHY: For a COLLECTIVE event where neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, the evt field is set to `null` (lines 1063-1067), so the collected `teamDestinationCalendars` of the other hosts are dropped and those hosts are never invited — defeating the multi-host support this PR adds.
HOW: Initialize to an array (e.g. `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` before pushing, or default the field to `[]` instead of `null`) so team destination calendars are always appended.

WHAT: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` drops the previous non-calendar fallback `result.credentialId`.
WHY: For non-calendar results (video events) `referencesToCreate` now stores `credentialId: undefined` where it previously stored `result.credentialId`, so the persisted video reference loses its credentialId; later code that looks the reference up by credentialId (e.g. handleCancelBooking.ts:491-502 deleting the video meeting, or EventManager.updateLocation) can no longer resolve the credential and the meeting is not cleaned up.
HOW: Keep the fallback for non-calendar results: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : result.credentialId` (i.e. just `result.credentialId` for both branches).

WHAT: The new `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` loop performs a `prisma.credential.findUnique` on every destination whose credential is not found in the cached `this.calendarCredentials` (line 344); the same per-reference DB lookup was added in updateAllCalendarEvents at line 517.
WHY: For collective bookings with multiple hosts this turns one in-memory lookup into up to N sequential database round-trips added to the booking-creation hot path, scaling with host count.
HOW: Resolve all missing credential ids in a single batched query (`prisma.credential.findMany({ where: { id: { in: missingIds } } })`) before the loop and build a lookup map.

The Meet-location fallback destructures `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. When `destinationCalendar` is an empty array (which this PR now produces in many callers, e.g. handleCancelBooking.ts, the payment webhooks, confirm/editLocation/deleteCredential/requestReschedule handlers all set `[]` when there is no destination calendar), the destructured value is `undefined` and `.integration` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`, aborting event creation. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration` to preserve the previous optional-chained behavior.
outros:
WHAT: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is dereferenced without optional chaining after destructuring `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`.
WHY: The previous code was `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`, which was null-safe; now when `destinationCalendar` is null/empty (e.g. handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067 sets it to `null` when neither eventType nor organizer has one) and `evt.location === MeetLocationType`, destructuring yields `undefined` and `.integration` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`, crashing the booking creation flow.
HOW: Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

`mainHostDestinationCalendar` can be `undefined` because `evt.destinationCalendar` may now be null or an empty array (callers such as handleNewBooking pass `: null` / `: []`). The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, but the new line dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining, throwing `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` whenever `evt.location === MeetLocationType`. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` to preserve the null-safe fallback.

handleNewBooking.ts (lines 1063-1067) can produce `destinationCalendar: null` (and other callers pass `[]`), but here `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields `undefined` for both, and line 119 then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining, throwing `TypeError` on every booking without a destination calendar. The previous code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which was null-safe; guard it (e.g. `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`) so the Google-Meet fallback does not crash.

Destructuring `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields undefined when destinationCalendar is an empty array (which this PR now produces in many callers, e.g. handleCancelBooking:255, webhook:119, paypal-webhook:156, confirm.handler:179). The subsequent `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` then throws TypeError, aborting event creation whenever location is Google Meet and destinationCalendar is empty. Guard the access: `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

The comment still describes a graceful fallback ("as a fallback we will only check the first one"), but the code no longer guards the absent case: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is the first element of `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and is `undefined` when the event has no destination calendar, so `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws a TypeError before the Cal Video fallback can run. The previous `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` was safe and let the fallback apply. Either restore optional chaining (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`) so the comment holds, or update the comment to state that a missing destination calendar is not handled.
Undefined dereference at EventManager.ts:119.

grupos.texto:
WHAT: The fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it compares `cal.externalId` against `null`/`undefined` and matches nothing (the same wrong pattern is duplicated in deleteEvent at lines 315-317).
WHY: When `updateEvent`/`deleteEvent` are called without an externalCalendarId, `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` now resolves to `undefined` instead of the host's destination calendar externalId (old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`), so the Google API is invoked with an undefined calendarId and the update/delete targets the wrong (or default) calendar or errors.
HOW: Find the destination calendar for the current credential (e.g. by credentialId) rather than comparing `externalId` to the already-falsy `externalCalendarId`, or restore the single fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`.
outros: Dead computation in the fallback: the else branch runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, yet it calls `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`, comparing every cal.externalId to undefined. Nothing can match, so selectedCalendar is always undefined and the fallback that previously returned `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` is lost. Match the intended criterion (destination calendar's own externalId/credentialId), not the already-falsy externalCalendarId.

Same dead-computation defect in deleteEvent: the else branch executes only when externalCalendarId is falsy, yet the predicate `(cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` compares against undefined and can never match, so calendarId falls through to "primary" and the event is deleted from the wrong calendar instead of the booking's destination calendar. Fix the predicate to use the destination calendar's externalId (or credentialId) rather than the falsy externalCalendarId.

In updateEvent (and the identical pattern at lines 315-317 in deleteEvent), the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` compares each element's externalId to the same `externalCalendarId` the ternary already found falsy, so it can never match and always returns undefined. The intended fallback to the destination calendar's externalId is lost, sending the update/delete to the wrong calendar ("primary"). Select the relevant destination calendar by credential instead, as done in createEvent.

grupos.texto: Null vs [] inconsistency.

The fallback searches for a destination whose externalId equals the absent externalCalendarId. When a booking reference lacks that field, this yields undefined instead of the configured calendar and the update request has no calendarId; the analogous deletion fallback targets primary rather than the configured calendar. Restore a valid destination fallback when the reference has no externalCalendarId.

updateLocation now reads externalId and credentialId exclusively from results, but CalendarManager.updateEvent returns neither field. Calendar references produced by location editing consequently lose their calendar and credential routing information, breaking subsequent updates or cancellation, particularly for secondary collective hosts. Return those fields from updateEvent or preserve them from the corresponding booking reference.

Organization creation no longer assigns a slug when team billing is disabled, while requestedSlug is also omitted in that mode. New self-hosted organizations therefore have neither publication field, and publish.handler rejects them because requestedSlug is missing. Restore the non-billing slug assignment.

Keep the first destination access optional in the Google Meet fallback. The changed handleNewBooking producer explicitly sets destinationCalendar to null when neither the event type nor organizer has a destination, and other changed callers produce an empty array. Destructuring either yields no first destination, so selecting Google Meet now throws at mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration instead of falling back to Cal Video as before. Use mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration.
outros: The Google Meet fallback dereferences mainHostDestinationCalendar without checking whether the destination array is empty. Bookings with Google Meet and no configured destination now throw instead of falling back to Cal Video. Use mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration in the condition.

Preserve the optional guard when checking the first destination (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`). When Google Meet is selected and destinationCalendar is null or empty (both explicitly produced by booking handlers), destructuring yields undefined and this condition throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.

Preserve the missing-destination fallback by using mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration here. handleNewBooking explicitly supplies null when neither the event type nor organizer has a destination calendar, and other callers supply []. With a Google Meet location, destructuring yields undefined and this property access throws instead of falling back to Cal Video as the previous optional access did.

Guard mainHostDestinationCalendar before reading integration. When destinationCalendar is null or [], destructuring produces undefined; a booking with MeetLocationType then throws a TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video. handleNewBooking explicitly still produces null when neither the event type nor organizer has a destination, so this is reachable in precisely the no-calendar case this fallback handles.

grupos.texto: Retain result.credentialId for non-calendar references as well. The previous mapping saved the dedicated video integration's credential ID; this change unconditionally replaces it with undefined for video results, losing the association needed to identify the account that created the meeting during subsequent lifecycle operations.
outros: The reference mapping discards credentialId for every video result. createMeeting returns the video credential ID, and handleCancelBooking only deletes a video meeting when its reference has that ID, so newly created video meetings are left behind on cancellation. Preserve result.credentialId for video results as well.

grupos.texto: Select the destination matching the credential used for this creation rather than always taking the first element. handleNewBooking now appends collective hosts' calendars, and EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents calls CalendarManager.createEvent separately for each host's credential with the entire event array. On the second Office365 host, this code therefore requests the organizer's calendar ID using the second host's token, typically failing with a calendar-not-found error instead of creating the event on that host's calendar. Accept the credentialId passed by CalendarManager and use it to select the appropriate destination.
outros: Office365 creation always selects the first host's destination despite being invoked separately with each host's credential. A collective booking with distinct Office365 calendars sends the second host's token to the first host's calendar ID, causing failed or incorrectly targeted creation. Accept the credentialId supplied by CalendarManager and select the matching destination.

Select the destination belonging to the current credential rather than always taking the first array entry. EventManager now calls createEvent once per destination with that destination's credential, while passing the full event array each time. In a collective booking with two Outlook hosts, the second host therefore attempts to insert into the first host's calendar using the second host's token, typically failing instead of creating the second calendar event. Accept the credentialId passed by CalendarManager and match the destination by that ID (or pass a destination-specific event).

Select the destination belonging to the credential passed by CalendarManager, rather than always selecting the first array element. EventManager now invokes creation for each collective host with the full destination array. A second Office365 host therefore attempts to write to the first host's calendar using its own token, causing creation to fail or target the wrong calendar; meanwhile the saved reference records the second host's externalId.

Select the destination matching the credentialId passed by CalendarManager rather than always taking the first destination. EventManager now invokes createEvent once per collective host using that host's credential but passes the entire destination array each time. For two Office365 hosts, the second host therefore attempts to create an event in the first host's calendar under /me/calendars, normally failing because that calendar does not belong to the second account. Accept the credentialId argument and resolve the corresponding destination, as the Google implementation does.

Select the destination belonging to the credential used for this creation, rather than always taking the first destination. createAllCalendarEvents now invokes this service for each collective host's credential but passes the full destination array each time. The second Office365 host consequently posts to the first host's calendar ID under the second host's token, normally failing because that calendar is inaccessible; if accessible, it writes to the wrong calendar while the booking reference records the second host's destination.

grupos.texto: Initialize destinationCalendar to an array before appending collective hosts' destinations. When neither the event type nor organizer has a destination, it is set to null above, so optional push silently discards all the computed teamDestinationCalendars. Hosts with configured destination calendars consequently receive no calendar events.
outros: The optional push discards all collected team destinations when the organizer has no destination calendar. A collective booking with configured secondary hosts therefore creates none of their calendar events even though teamDestinationCalendars contains them. Initialize the array before appending the team destinations.

grupos.texto: For cancel-all-remaining recurring collective bookings, delete each updated booking's reference matching the current outer reference/credential. The new outer loop iterates all calendar references, but this inner block still iterates only the organizer's credentials and takes the first calendar reference of each booking. Every outer iteration therefore repeats deletion of the first host's event, while the additional hosts' recurring events remain on their calendars after cancellation.
outros: The new per-reference loop runs the recurring-series deletion branch for every host, but that branch still iterates only bookingToDelete.user.credentials and selects the first calendar reference in each occurrence. Canceling all remaining collective occurrences repeatedly deletes the owner's events while leaving secondary hosts' events untouched. For each occurrence, delete the reference matching the current host credential using the resolved calendarCredential.

grupos.texto: createEvent now picks the target calendar only by matching credentialId. Destination calendars without a credentialId (handled by EventManager's integration-based branch) never match, so events are inserted into "primary" instead of the configured destination externalId as before.

destinationCalendar is now an array that can be null/empty (the diff itself produces [] and null), so `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined and `.integration` throws a TypeError for Google Meet bookings without a destination calendar. The old code used `?.`; use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration` so the fallback to Cal Video still applies.
outros: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty, so `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws a TypeError. Every booking with no destination calendar (the existing `[]` or null fallbacks) crashes in `create`. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined when destinationCalendar is empty or null (many callers now pass []), so `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws a TypeError for Google Meet locations. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields undefined when the array is empty or null. `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` then throws a TypeError for any Google Meet booking with no destination calendar, because the optional chaining was dropped. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

`mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty, so `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws a TypeError. This breaks booking creation for Google Meet locations with no destination calendar. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

grupos.texto: In the fallback branch `externalCalendarId` is already falsy, so `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can only match a calendar whose externalId is also falsy. The destination calendar's externalId is never selected, so updateEvent falls back to the default calendar. Use the first destination calendar's externalId (`event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`) instead. The same flawed lookup is in deleteEvent at lines 315-317.
outros: In the fallback branch, `externalCalendarId` is already falsy, so `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can never match and `selectedCalendar` is always undefined. The same defect is in `deleteEvent` at lines 315-317. The previous fallback to the destination calendar's externalId is lost. Fall back to `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`, or to the entry matching the credential.

The fallback runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, yet it looks for a destination calendar with externalId === externalCalendarId. That can never match the intended calendar, so the fallback is dead. Use the first destination calendar's externalId (e.g. mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId). The same bug is in deleteEvent.

In deleteEvent the fallback `find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is only evaluated when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it never yields a usable id and the event is deleted from 'primary' instead of the destination calendar. Fall back to the first destination calendar's externalId.

The fallback runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, but it then looks for a destination calendar whose externalId equals that falsy value. This always yields undefined, so the destination calendar is never used on update. The same pattern is in deleteEvent (lines 315-317). Fall back to the first destination calendar's externalId instead, e.g. `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`.

In the fallback branch externalCalendarId is falsy, so `find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can never match a real calendar and always yields undefined. The previous fallback to the event's destination calendar externalId is lost; use the first destinationCalendar's externalId instead. The same pattern in deleteEvent has the same problem.

grupos.texto: In the branch for destinations without a credentialId, `createEvent(c, event)` is called without the externalId argument. CalendarManager.createEvent only returns `externalId` when it is passed in, and EventManager now stores `result.externalId` as externalCalendarId, so these booking references are saved with an undefined externalCalendarId. Pass `destination.externalId` as the third argument, so the producer returns what the consumer stores.
outros: In the no-credentialId branch createEvent(c, event) is called without externalId, so EventResult.externalId is undefined. The booking reference's externalCalendarId, which used to come from evt.destinationCalendar.externalId, is now not stored, which breaks later update/delete targeting. Pass destination.externalId.

grupos.texto: WHAT: evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when no organizer calendar exists, then evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) silently no-ops. WHY: collective team destination calendars are dropped for exactly the organizer-without-calendar case, so secondary hosts never get events. HOW: initialize to [] instead of null when collecting team calendars.

WHAT: slug spread condition was inverted from ...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && {slug}) to ...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? {slug} : {}). WHY: organizations get slug when billing enabled and lose it when disabled, opposite of prior contract and breaking slug/requestedSlug pairing. HOW: restore negation for slug branch.

Destructured `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` assumes index 0 exists, then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. When destinationCalendar is null/undefined/[] (allowed by type `DestinationCalendar[] | null` and produced as null in handleNewBooking and [] in handleCancelBooking), this throws TypeError. Old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` which was safe. Guard with `?.` and handle undefined, e.g. `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== 'google_calendar'` only when present or default correctly.
outros: WHAT: mainHostDestinationCalendar can be undefined when destinationCalendar is null/empty but code unconditionally reads .integration. WHY: throws TypeError on bookings/reminders with no destination calendar, breaking Meet fallback that old optional-chaining handled. HOW: guard with ?. and fallback, e.g. mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== google_calendar.
Missing optional chain on mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration throws when array null/empty

Guard against missing destinationCalendar: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`. Currently `?? []` destructure can yield undefined when producer supplies null, so unconditional `.integration` throws.
Null dereference: mainHostDestinationCalendar can be undefined when destinationCalendar is null/empty; accessing .integration throws. Use optional chaining.

New code does const [mainHostDestinationCalendar]=evt.destinationCalendar ?? [] then mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chain. Old code was evt.destinationCalendar?.integration (null-safe). When destinationCalendar is null/undefined/empty, this throws TypeError. Use mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar" or explicit guard.

grupos.texto: Fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` in the `externalCalendarId ? ... : ...` else-branch compares against externalCalendarId which is guaranteed falsy there, so it can never match and yields undefined instead of the old `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback. Fall back to first/credential-matched calendar instead of searching for the absent value.
outros: WHAT: updateEvent fallback event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) is evaluated only when externalCalendarId is falsy so it can never match. WHY: selectedCalendar becomes undefined and update targets undefined calendarId instead of the stored destination calendar. HOW: fall back to first entry or credential-matched entry, not a find against the falsy value.
Dead fallback in updateEvent else-branch can never match
Dead fallback in updateEvent: else-branch find on falsy externalCalendarId never matches, yielding undefined calendarId. Fall back to main host calendar.

grupos.texto: Same inverted-lookup in deleteEvent: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` can never match when externalCalendarId is falsy, losing the previous destinationCalendar fallback and passing undefined calendarId to delete. Use a fallback that does not depend on the absent externalCalendarId.
outros: WHAT: deleteEvent has the same impossible fallback find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) in the else branch. WHY: delete without explicit externalCalendarId resolves to undefined then defaults to primary, deleting from the wrong calendar or failing. HOW: use destinationCalendar[0]?.externalId as fallback.
Dead fallback in deleteEvent else-branch can never match

grupos.texto: Interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId) and destinationCalendar is array. Implementation kept createEvent(event) and always uses first element, ignoring credentialId, while GoogleCalendarService selects via find(cal=>cal.credentialId===credentialId). For collective bookings with multiple destinations all Office365 writes go to first calendar. Add credentialId param and select matching entry.
outros: WHAT: createEvent always uses destinationCalendar[0] even though EventManager now loops per-host credentials sharing the same evt array. WHY: secondary collective hosts create their Office365 event in the main host calendarId (or wrong /me context) instead of their own destination. HOW: thread credentialId/externalId like Google service and select matching entry.

Same contract miss as Office365: createEvent(event) not updated to createEvent(event, credentialId). Always uses destinationCalendar[0], ignoring per-credential selection that Google implements. Add credentialId param and pick matching destinationCalendar entry, falling back to first.

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

grupos.texto: Inconsistent email normalization for identity checks. Both the authorization check `attendee.email === user.email` (line 52) and the existing-attendee dedup `guest === attendee.email` (line 76) use strict case-sensitive equality, while emails are treated as case-insensitive everywhere else in this handler (the blacklist block directly below lowercases). Consequence: a legitimate attendee whose stored casing differs from their session email is wrongly FORBIDDEN, and a guest differing from an existing attendee only by case is duplicated rather than filtered. Compare on a normalized form (both sides `.toLowerCase()`), consistent with the blacklist normalization.

Case-sensitive identity comparison misroutes emails. `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` compares the freshly-added guest list against stored attendee emails with strict case-sensitive matching. A newly added guest whose casing differs from the stored value falls into the `else` branch and receives the AttendeeAddGuestsEmail template intended for pre-existing attendees, while existing attendees can receive the wrong one. Normalize both sides (e.g. compare `attendee.email.toLowerCase()` against a lowercased newGuests set).

`Tooltip content="Remove email"` is a hard-coded English user-facing string, while the surrounding code in this same component routes user text through `t()` (e.g. `t("add_another")` on line 69). This string bypasses the translation mechanism and will never be localised; it should use a translation key.

In `onError`, `message` is always a non-empty template string (`"${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}"`), so the fallback `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` is unreachable and the newly added `unable_to_add_guests` translation is never shown. The user is instead shown a raw error code prefix like `BAD_REQUEST: ...` rather than the translated message; the fallback and code prefix handling should be corrected so the intended translated text reaches the user.

The handler never deduplicates within the incoming `guests` array. `uniqueGuests` only excludes emails that are already attendees or blacklisted, so a request containing the same email twice (or two equivalent emails) yields two identical `guestsFullDetails` entries. Since the wire schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` has no uniqueness refine (the uniqueness check lives only in the client's AddGuestsDialog), the server cannot rely on the UI: either duplicate attendee rows are persisted (state corruption of the booking's attendee list) or, if a DB unique constraint on (bookingId,email) exists, `createMany` throws an unhandled Prisma error. Deduplicate the input server-side (e.g. `[...new Set(guests)]`) and/or add the uniqueness refinement to `ZAddGuestsInputSchema`.

Check-then-insert race: the handler reads `booking.attendees` at the start, filters against it, then inserts in a separate `prisma.booking.update ... createMany` with no transaction or unique guard. Two concurrent addGuests calls for the same guest both see it as absent and both insert, producing duplicate attendees. Wrap the read+filter+insert in a transaction (or rely on a unique constraint on (bookingId, email) and handle the conflict) so concurrent requests cannot both succeed.

WHAT: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && instead of ||. WHY: isTeamAdmin returns truthy for role ADMIN or OWNER while isTeamOwner returns true only for OWNER, so the && expression is only true for OWNERs; team ADMINs are treated as unauthorized and get FORBIDDEN when adding guests, contradicting the variable's intent. HOW: use `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) || (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0))`.
outros: The flag is named `isTeamAdminOrOwner` but is computed with `&&` (both admin AND owner). A team admin who is not the owner, or the owner who is not flagged admin, will fail this check, so the guard at line 54 wrongly throws FORBIDDEN for legitimate admins/owners. Use `||` between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner.

The variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` names an OR condition, but the code combines `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)` with `&&`, so it is true only when the user is both admin AND owner. Either the name is wrong or the operator is; as written the permission check at line 54 denies a plain team admin, contradicting what the identifier promises. Use `||` to match the name (or rename if AND is intended).

`isTeamAdminOrOwner` is built with `&&`, so it is true only when the caller is BOTH a team admin AND the team owner — it should be `||`. As written, a team admin who is not the owner (and vice versa) evaluates to false and is denied by the `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)` throw at line 54, so admins/owners cannot add guests to team bookings. Replace `&&` with `||` between the `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` calls.
ANDed isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner check

grupos.texto: Case-sensitivity bypass of the guest blacklist. `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased on the list side (line 71) but the input side is compared raw: `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` (line 77). A guest email submitted with any different casing (e.g. `Foo@Bar.com` when the blacklist holds `foo@bar.com`) passes the filter and is persisted, defeating BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS. Normalize the input before comparison, e.g. filter on `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest.toLowerCase())` (and likewise lowercase `guest` for the attendee dedup check).
outros: WHAT: The blacklist is compared case-sensitively against guest input while blacklistedGuestEmails are lowercased. WHY: blacklistedGuestEmails entries are lowercased but the filter compares `guest` verbatim (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`); an authenticated user can add a blacklisted address simply by changing its case (e.g. `Foo@bar.com` vs `foo@bar.com`), bypassing the configured BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restriction. HOW: normalize the guest before comparison, e.g. `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest.toLowerCase())`.

grupos.texto: The handler passes the raw input `guests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails`, but the email manager's `newGuests` parameter is documented/used as the set of guests that were actually added (`newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` selects who gets the full `AttendeeScheduledEmail`). Since the handler filters the added guests into `uniqueGuests` (dropping addresses that already belong to an attendee or are blacklisted) before creating attendees, any submitted address that was not actually added is still treated as a new guest here — an existing attendee re-submitted by the requester receives a duplicate booking-confirmation email with a new ICS REQUEST. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead of `guests`.
outros: WHAT: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw `guests` input instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`. WHY: any submitted email that was already an attendee (or is blacklisted) is dropped by uniqueGuests for the DB write but still appears in the `guests` array, so in email-manager.ts the `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` branch marks that existing attendee as a new guest and sends them a full AttendeeScheduledEmail re-confirmation instead of the add-guests notification. HOW: pass `uniqueGuests` (or the newly-created attendee emails) to sendAddGuestsEmails.

`uniqueGuests` is computed (line 74) to exclude already-invited and blacklisted emails and is the value actually inserted into the booking, but `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is called with the raw input `guests`. The untransformed value is used where the filtered one was intended, so the email-manager's `newGuests.includes(...)` classification operates on the wrong list; pass `uniqueGuests`.

The callee `sendAddGuestsEmails(calEvent, newGuests)` expects the array of *new* guests: it uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to send AttendeeScheduledEmail (a fresh invitation) to new guests and AttendeeAddGuestsEmail (notification) to everyone else. The caller passes `guests` — the raw input — instead of the deduplicated `uniqueGuests` computed at lines 74-90. Any email in `guests` that was filtered out as already-an-attendee (or blacklisted) is therefore treated as a new guest, causing that existing attendee to be re-sent a full invitation. Pass `uniqueGuests` here.
Using `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests` when sending emails

grupos.texto: The admin-or-owner authorization check requires both isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner to succeed. Since isTeamAdmin accepts ADMIN and OWNER but isTeamOwner accepts only OWNER, a team admin who is not the organizer or an attendee receives FORBIDDEN. Use isTeamAdmin alone, or combine the checks with OR.

EventManager is initialized with the requesting user's credentials rather than the booking organizer's credentials. When an attendee or team owner adds guests to a booking whose calendar reference lacks credentialId, updateAllCalendarEvents selects credentials by type from the caller's calendars, so the organizer's event is not updated or the update targets the wrong account. Load credentials for booking.userId and initialize the manager with the booking owner.

The mutation accepts an unbounded guest array that is persisted and immediately expanded into concurrent emails to every attendee. For non-seated bookings each email's ICS serializes the full attendee list, so adding N guests creates O(N) concurrent sends and O(N²) aggregate attachment work; repeated additions also resend to all existing attendees. Enforce a server-side guest-count and total-attendee limit before insertion and bound notification concurrency.

The new removal tooltip hard-codes `Remove email`, so users in non-English locales see English text even though the neighbouring controls use `t(...)` and this component already obtains `t` from useLocale. Route this tooltip through a translation key (and supply its English translation) rather than using the literal.

Enforce guest uniqueness on the server, including atomically against existing attendees. This filter checks each submitted address only against the original booking snapshot, so a request with guests ["new@example.com", "new@example.com"] retains both and passes both entries to createMany, despite the dialog's explicit uniqueness requirement. Two concurrent requests for the same new address can likewise both pass this check before insertion. Deduplicate/validate the input and enforce booking/email uniqueness transactionally or with a database constraint so duplicate requests cannot create duplicate attendees (or surface a database constraint error after validation).
outros: uniqueGuests filters against existing attendees but does not deduplicate addresses within the incoming guests array. A direct mutation with the same new address twice inserts two Attendee records and sends duplicate invitations because the server schema permits duplicates and the Attendee model has no unique booking/email constraint. Deduplicate normalized input before filtering and inserting.

uniqueGuests does not deduplicate the submitted guests: it only filters against attendees already in the booking. The server schema accepts duplicates, so submitting ["new@example.com", "new@example.com"] passes this filter and creates two attendee records (and sends duplicate invitations). Deduplicate the input on the server before creating attendees rather than relying on the dialog's uniqueness check.

grupos.texto: The blacklist entries are lowercased at line 71, but `guest` is not normalized before `includes`. Both the UI and server schemas accept mixed-case emails without lowercasing, so a caller can submit `Blocked@Example.com` to bypass a configured `blocked@example.com` blacklist and have that address added and emailed. Normalize the incoming address to the same lowercase representation before checking the blacklist (preferably normalize guest inputs once before identity comparisons).
outros: The blacklist comparison uses the raw guest address against lowercase blacklist entries instead of the canonical address used by handleNewBooking. An authorized attendee can invite a blocked address using uppercase characters or a plus-address alias, bypassing the guest-email block and triggering an invitation. Compare extractBaseEmail(guest).toLowerCase() against normalized blacklist entries, as the existing booking flow does.

Blacklist entries are lowercased at lines 70–72, but guest input is compared without lowercasing. An address such as Blocked@example.com therefore bypasses a blacklist entry blocked@example.com and is added and emailed. Normalize both sides of the comparison consistently.

grupos.texto: Pass `uniqueGuests` rather than `guests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails`. The new email-manager implementation interprets this argument as the attendees newly added and sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` to every attendee whose email it contains. If the request contains an existing attendee and a new guest, the existing attendee is filtered out of the database insertion but remains in `guests`, so they receive a new-booking notification rather than `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Using the filtered insertion list preserves the email manager's distinction between existing and new attendees.
outros: Pass uniqueGuests rather than guests to sendAddGuestsEmails. If the submitted list contains an existing attendee plus a new address, the existing attendee is filtered out of creation but remains in guests. The email manager uses this argument to classify new attendees, so that existing attendee receives a fresh scheduled invitation instead of the guests-added notification.

grupos.texto: Any attendee, matched only by email, is allowed to add arbitrary guests to a booking, and the handler then sends emails and calendar invites on the organizer's behalf. Any attendee can use this to send invites to arbitrary addresses. Restrict the action to the organizer and team admins, or verify that the attendee's email is confirmed.

The tooltip text "Remove email" is hard-coded English and bypasses the translation mechanism. The component already calls useLocale (t), and the neighbouring label uses t("add_another"). Add a locale key and use t(...) here.

The error message is built as a template string, so it is always truthy. The `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is therefore dead code, and the user can see "undefined: ..." or an untranslated raw message. Use `err.message ? t(err.message) : t("unable_to_add_guests")`.

isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so it is true only if the user is both. Team admins who are not owners are denied. Use || (or a single admin-or-owner check) to match the variable name's intent.
outros: The team permission check combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with `&&`, so only users who are both admin and owner pass. Team admins who are not owners are therefore denied. Use `||` instead.

The variable is named isTeamAdminOrOwner, but the code joins the two checks with `&&`, so it only passes if the user is both admin and owner. The name states OR and the code does AND. Change it to `||`, or rename the variable.

grupos.texto: The server does not enforce that guest emails are unique. It dedupes only against existing attendees, and it does so case-sensitively. Duplicates inside the `guests` input, or the same address in different case, pass the filter and createMany inserts duplicate attendee rows. The blacklist check is also case-sensitive against a lowercased list. Normalise guests to lowercase and dedupe them with a Set before filtering, and compare against existing attendees in lowercase.
outros: Duplicate and blacklist checks compare guest emails case-sensitively against attendee emails, and the blacklist is lowercased while the guest is not. Case variants such as `Foo@x.com` bypass both checks. Lowercase the guest before comparing, and also lowercase the attendee email.

The blacklist is lowercased but the guest email is compared without normalisation, so a blacklisted address can be added by changing its case (e.g. Blocked@x.com). Compare guest.toLowerCase() against the blacklist. Compare existing attendee emails case-insensitively too, so the same address in a different case is not added as a new attendee.

grupos.texto: The calendar update uses the credentials of the acting user (ctx.user), not the booking organizer's, so an admin or attendee acting on someone else's booking updates the wrong calendar or none. Also, sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw `guests` list, including filtered duplicates and blacklisted emails. Use the organizer's credentials and pass `uniqueGuests`.
outros: sendAddGuestsEmails treats its `newGuests` argument as the set of newly added attendees. The handler passes the raw `guests` input, which still contains existing attendees and blacklisted addresses that were filtered out into `uniqueGuests`. Those existing attendees get a full 'scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' notice. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead.

sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw `guests` input instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`. A guest who was already an attendee (and was filtered out) is still treated as new, so they get the 'scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' notification. Pass `uniqueGuests`.

sendAddGuestsEmails treats its second argument as the list of newly added guests, but the handler passes the raw `guests` input. Guests that were filtered out (already attendees or blacklisted) are still in that list, so existing attendees get the 'scheduled' email again and blacklisted addresses may be emailed. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead.

grupos.texto: The attendees are written to the database at line 92, but `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` at line 165 runs outside the try/catch. If it throws, the mutation returns an error even though the guests are already persisted, so the DB and the calendar are out of sync. No emails are sent, and a retry then fails with 'emails_must_be_unique_valid'. Catch and handle the calendar update failure after the DB write.
outros: The attendees are already committed to the DB when `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` is awaited without a try/catch. If the calendar sync throws, the mutation returns an error and skips the emails, although the guests were added. The caller sees a failure for a partly applied change and may retry. Handle calendar sync failure as best-effort, as the email send is, or run it before the DB write.

grupos.texto: WHAT: addGuestsMutation onSuccess resets multiEmailValue and closes the dialog but never resets isInvalidEmail. WHY: after one failed validation the red emails_must_be_unique_valid error persists on the next open/successful add.

WHAT: guests is an unbounded z.array(z.string().email()) with no max length. WHY: any authorized caller (including a mere attendee) can submit thousands of emails causing unbounded createMany inserts plus unbounded Promise.all email fanout in sendAddGuestsEmails.

Tooltip content="Remove email" is hard-coded English user-facing text bypassing i18n while surrounding strings in the same file/PR use t(). Wrap it in t() e.g. content={t("remove_email")} and add the key to locales.

Race condition: findFirst check for existing attendees then booking.update+createMany is not atomic. Two concurrent addGuests calls with the same new email both see it as absent and both insert, creating duplicates. Guard with a unique constraint and handle conflict or run in a transaction/serializable check.

Unreachable fallback: `message` is a template string `${code}: ${...}` which is always truthy, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never takes the fallback. Build message conditionally or test the underlying parts for emptiness.

WHAT: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner. WHY: isTeamAdmin already returns truthy for ADMIN or OWNER (verified in queries/teams), so && reduces the check to OWNER-only and wrongfully denies team ADMINs.
outros: Name declares OR but code uses AND: `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. A team admin who is not owner (or owner who is not admin) fails the check and gets FORBIDDEN. Change && to ||.

grupos.texto: Case-sensitivity bypass: blacklisted emails are lowercased (line 71) but incoming `guest` is compared raw at line 77 (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). Normalize guest (e.g. `guest.toLowerCase()` / trim) before both the duplicate and blacklist checks so `Evil@Example.com` cannot bypass a `evil@example.com` blacklist entry.
outros: WHAT: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased but the incoming guest string is compared without lowercasing/normalizing. WHY: an attacker bypasses the blocklist with case variation (e.g. Spam@Example.com) and gets added/emailed.

Case disagreement: blacklist entries are lowercased at build but compared as `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without lowercasing `guest`, and existing-attendee check uses exact `guest === attendee.email`. Mixed-case blacklisted/existing emails bypass the filter. Lowercase both sides before compare.

grupos.texto: uniqueGuests filters only against existing attendees/blacklist but never dedupes guests[] itself and schema has no uniqueness check. A request like guests=[a@x.com,a@x.com] passes the filter twice and createMany inserts duplicate attendee rows or throws an unhandled DB unique-constraint exception. Dedupe/normalize input (and reject intra-request duplicates) before createMany.
outros: WHAT: uniqueGuests filter only dedupes against existing booking.attendees with case-sensitive === and never dedupes duplicates within the input guests array itself (server schema has no uniqueness refine unlike the client). WHY: a request with the same new email twice creates duplicate attendee rows via createMany.

grupos.texto: Dead-transform / wrong input: `uniqueGuests` is computed (dedup vs existing attendees + blacklist) and written to DB, but `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the original `guests`. Existing attendees re-submitted are then `includes()`-matched as new and get AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. Pass `uniqueGuests`.
outros: WHAT: sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) passes the raw input guests instead of the filtered uniqueGuests. WHY: already-existing attendees included in the request are misclassified as newGuests in email-manager and receive AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail (wrong notification).

Pass `uniqueGuests` (the filtered set written to DB) to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of raw `guests`; the email layer assumes newGuests exactly equals newly created attendees for its Scheduled vs AddGuests branch.

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.prTitle: Add guest management functionality to existing bookings

grupos.texto:
WHAT: The new block fetches and persists a fresh access token (`accessTokenParsed.data`) but then creates the `jsforce.Connection` with the stale `credentialKey.access_token` (line 106) instead of the just-refreshed token.
WHY: The refreshed token is written to the DB but never used for the connection; if the old token was expired, jsforce must refresh again (extra round trip) or fail, and the DB/connection state diverge.
HOW: Pass the new access token (`accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`) to the `jsforce.Connection`.

The webhook secret is compared with the `!==` operator, which short-circuits on the first differing byte and leaks the secret via response timing (timing attack). An attacker can iteratively recover CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and then forge requests that create/update arbitrary user credential keys (decrypted with the AES key) via this endpoint. Use a constant-time comparison, e.g. crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers, guarding for length mismatch first.

The JSDoc documents two different parameters with the same text: both `@param appData.type` and `@param appData.appId` are described as "the app slug". The body uses `appData.type` as the credential `type` and only `appData.appId` as the app slug, so the `type` doc contradicts the code and misleads callers. Document `type` as the credential type.

WHAT: The 3rd argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is `credentialId` (= `credential.id`, line 53), but the function's parameter is `userId` (`refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId)`).
WHY: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, the sync endpoint is sent `calcomUserId: <credential id>` instead of the user id, so Bigin credentials are synced against the wrong/non-existent user (all other apps correctly pass `credential.userId`).
HOW: Pass `credential.userId` instead of `credentialId` as the third argument.
outros: refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter is the Cal.com userId (used as `calcomUserId` in the sync request and to decide whether sharing runs), but this call passes `credentialId`. Every other caller passes `credential.userId`, so the credential-sync endpoint receives a credential row id as the user id and shared credentials are fetched/updated for the wrong identity. Pass `credential.userId` here.

refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter is `userId` (declared in refreshOAuthTokens.ts line 3 and used as `calcomUserId: userId.toString()`), but this call passes `credentialId` (the Credential row id, line 53) instead of the user id. When credential sharing is enabled the customer's sync endpoint receives a credential id labelled as calcomUserId and cannot resolve the correct Cal.com user. Pass `credential.userId` (the BiginToken/credential payload carries it) or plumb the user id through refreshAccessToken.

refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter is `userId: number | null` (used as calcomUserId in the credential-sync request), but this call passes `credentialId` (a credential id), unlike every other call site which passes `credential.userId`. The sync endpoint will receive a credential id where a Cal.com user id is expected. Pass `credential.userId`.

The third parameter is named/documented as `userId` (comment: "the credential belongs to a user"), but the new zoho-bigin call site passes `credentialId`, so the request sends `calcomUserId: <credentialId>` — a credential row id where a Cal.com user id is expected. Pass `credential.userId` or rename/document the parameter if a credential id is intended.

grupos.texto:
WHAT: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` assigns the zod `safeParse` result object `{ success, data }` (see parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:29), not the parsed credential data, and this wrapper is persisted directly as `credential.key`.
WHY: The stored key no longer matches `googleCredentialSchema`, so the next time the credential is loaded `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75) throws and Google Calendar is broken until the credential is re-created. Every other caller (office365/zoom/salesforce) unwraps `.data`; only google stores the raw return value.
HOW: Use `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data` (or restore `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)`) when writing the key.
outros: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the SafeParseReturnType wrapper (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed value the old `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` returned. Assigning it to `key` and persisting `data: { key }` stores the wrapper as the credential key; the next read does `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` and throws, making the credential unusable. Use the `.data` result.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the whole safeParse result object `{ success, data }` (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts line 29), not the parsed value. The previous code was `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`, which returned the token object directly. Other callers (office365calendar, salesforce) read `tokenResponse.success`/`.data`, confirming the wrapper contract. Here the wrapper is stored verbatim as the credential key, so the persisted key becomes `{ success: true, data: {...} }` and is later unparseable by googleCredentialSchema. Use `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data;`.

parseRefreshTokenResponse now returns the whole zod safeParse result ({success, data}), not the parsed credential data (the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` returned data directly). This caller assigns that wrapper to `key` and persists `data: { key }`, so the stored Google credential becomes `{success:true,data:{...}}` instead of the credentials object, breaking subsequent reads of the key. Unwrap the result, e.g. `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema).data`.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParse result (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed credentials. Assigning it straight to `key` and persisting `data: { key }` stores the wrapper object instead of the credential, corrupting the user's stored key. Use `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data` (as office365/salesforce/zoom already do) — or make the helper return the parsed data.

grupos.texto:
WHAT: In the credential-sharing branch `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` `Response` object instead of a parsed token payload, yet several callers treat the result as an already-parsed token object.
WHY: Callers such as hubspot (`hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn`), zoho-bigin (`tokenInfo.data.error`), zohocrm (`zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`) and googlecalendar (`res?.data`) read `.data`/token fields off the return value; a `Response` has neither, so the sync path yields `undefined`/`NaN` or throws a TypeError — the feature's primary code path is broken for those apps.
HOW: Parse the response (e.g. `const data = await response.json(); return data;`) before returning, or make every caller await the appropriate response handler.
outros: In sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response (no `.data`), but the google caller reads `res?.data` and then `token.access_token`, throwing a TypeError swallowed by the catch, so the token is never refreshed.

`res?.data` assumes the value returned by refreshOAuthTokens has a `.data` field (true for the `fetchTokens.res` branch), but when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED the helper returns a raw `fetch()` Response, which has no `.data`. Then `token.access_token` throws. Either parse the shared-mode Response here or have refreshOAuthTokens return a normalized `{ data }` shape.

grupos.texto: The new credential update references prisma without importing or declaring it; searching this file finds only the new usage. This fails TypeScript checking and raises ReferenceError after a successful token exchange at runtime. Import prisma from @calcom/prisma before using it.

getClient now unconditionally exchanges the Salesforce refresh token on every service construction, even when the saved access token is valid. Each constructor invocation adds a blocking OAuth network round trip and credential database write before any Salesforce operation, replacing jsforce's existing on-demand refresh behavior. Keep refresh on demand or guard the exchange with a token-expiration check.

The webhook performs a non-atomic findFirst followed by create when no credential exists. Concurrent deliveries for the same user and app can both observe no row and insert duplicates because Credential has no unique userId/appId constraint; subsequent findFirst updates only one duplicate, leaving competing credentials stale. Serialize the lookup/create operation for each user/app pair or introduce an appropriate uniqueness constraint and atomic upsert.

The webhook authenticates a secret using direct string inequality, which is not constant-time and can leak information about the secret through comparison timing. Compare fixed-length representations using a constant-time primitive (such as crypto.timingSafeEqual), handling absent or malformed headers safely, instead of comparing the secret strings directly.

The sync branch returns a raw fetch Response, whereas the Google, HubSpot and Zoho callbacks supplied to this helper return SDK token objects or Axios/Gaxios responses. With sharing enabled, Google reads `res.data` and then `token.access_token`, and Zoho reads `tokenInfo.data.error`, causing undefined-property exceptions; HubSpot similarly consumes token fields directly. Normalize the sync response to each caller's expected representation (or normalize both branches and update consumers) before returning it.
outros: The sync branch returns a native fetch Response even for callers whose original refresh function returns a parsed token object or an Axios/Gaxios response. Google reads res.data.access_token, Zoho CRM/Bigin read response.data.error, and HubSpot reads accessToken/expiresIn directly, so enabling synchronization breaks those refresh paths regardless of the endpoint's JSON payload. Normalize the endpoint response to each caller's expected contract, or make all callers consume a common parsed-token contract.

The sync branch returns a native fetch Response, but the changed Google caller reads res.data, the Zoho callers read tokenInfo.data, and HubSpot expects a decoded HubspotToken. Native Responses satisfy none of those contracts, so enabling sync makes these refresh paths fail or consume undefined token fields. Decode and adapt the sync response to each caller's required shape (or normalize the helper contract and update all callers); preserve Response handling for the existing fetch-based consumers.

Normalize the sync response to the consuming provider's expected shape. This branch returns a native fetch Response, whereas Google reads res.data.access_token, Zoho CRM/Bigin read tokenInfo.data.error, and HubSpot expects a decoded HubspotToken. None of those consumers decode the sync Response, so enabling sync breaks their refresh paths despite a successful endpoint response. Decode and adapt the response or update each of these consumers to handle the native Response explicitly.

The sync branch returns a native fetch Response, but Google reads res.data, Zoho CRM/Bigin read response.data, and HubSpot expects an already-decoded HubspotToken. Consequently these integrations fail or receive undefined tokens whenever sync is enabled. Decode and adapt the sync response to each caller's expected representation (or standardize both branches and consumers).

grupos.texto: The comment says the schema assumes any numeric property is the expiry and allows other token-response properties, but these computed keys are just the string representations of Zod schema objects, not dynamic property matchers. A normal `expires_in` or `expiry_date` field is therefore not recognized by these entries, and `z.object` does not preserve arbitrary extra properties by default. Make the documented contract match the schema (or implement explicit expiry fields and passthrough validation); otherwise integrators following this comment will supply responses that do not behave as advertised.
outros: The computed object keys stringify Zod schema objects rather than matching arbitrary token fields. Zod object parsing strips undeclared fields, so expires_in, expiry_date and actual refresh_token fields are discarded in synchronization mode; Zoom then computes expiry_date from undefined and Google loses required credential fields. Declare the supported expiry fields explicitly and preserve additional response fields with passthrough or catchall.

Computed keys using z.string().toString() do not validate arbitrary response properties: they produce literal object keys (normally '[object Object]'), and the second declaration overwrites the first. Zod object parsing strips unrecognized fields, so ordinary expires_in/expiry_date and refresh_token fields are discarded on the sharing path. Define explicit expiry fields or a schema that preserves and validates the actual response properties; otherwise consumers cannot calculate token expiry.

Computed property names using Zod schemas do not define wildcard fields: both schemas stringify to an object string key. Zod objects also strip unrecognized fields by default. Consequently a normal sync response containing access_token and expiry_date/expires_in parses with its expiry stripped (as well as other token fields). Office365 and Zoom then merge/persist credentials without the new expiry, while Google loses even more credential fields. Define explicit supported expiry fields and preserve/validate additional token properties rather than using schema objects as property names.

grupos.texto: When a refresh response omits refresh_token, this helper manufactures the hardcoded credential "refresh_token". Callers such as Office365 merge this into stored credentials, overwriting the valid existing refresh token and causing subsequent provider refreshes to use a predictable invalid token. Leave the field absent and preserve the existing credential when omission is allowed by the provider, or reject the response when a refresh token is required; do not substitute a literal authentication token.
outros: The parser fabricates the literal refresh token "refresh_token" whenever a successful response omits refresh_token, including when synchronization is disabled. Office365's response schema explicitly permits that omission, and its caller merges parsed data over existing credentials, replacing the valid saved refresh token with this invalid value and breaking the next refresh. Leave the property absent so the existing token survives the merge.

grupos.texto: Persist the parsed credential data, not the safeParse result. Previously googleCredentialSchema.parse returned the credential object directly; parseRefreshTokenResponse returns { success: true, data: ... }. Passing that wrapper as key stores access_token, expiry_date and refresh_token under data rather than at the credential root, so subsequent Google credential parsing fails even with credential sharing disabled. Use the helper result's data.
outros: Google persists the entire safeParse result returned by parseRefreshTokenResponse instead of its data property. Even with credential sharing disabled, the stored key becomes {success:true,data:{...}} rather than the credential object, so the next service construction fails googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key). Persist the successful result's data property.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the Zod safeParse result ({ success: true, data: ... }), not the parsed credential object returned by the previous schema.parse call. Persist key.data instead of key here. Otherwise even with credential sharing disabled, every successful Google refresh replaces the stored credential with an envelope lacking top-level access_token, refresh_token and expiry_date, breaking subsequent credential parsing.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse result ({ success, data }), not the parsed credential object. Persisting this as key replaces the Google credential's top-level access_token, refresh_token and expiry_date with an envelope, breaking subsequent credential parsing even when sharing is disabled. Persist the successful result's data instead.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse result ({ success: true, data: ... }), not the parsed credentials. Persisting this value as `key` on the next lines replaces the credential with that wrapper even with sharing disabled. Subsequent readers expecting top-level access_token/refresh_token cannot use it. Persist the parsed result's data instead.

grupos.texto: The third parameter of refreshOAuthTokens is a user ID and is serialized as calcomUserId, but this call passes credentialId. These IDs are unrelated, so the sync endpoint refreshes the wrong user's credentials or cannot find the user; team credentials also incorrectly enter the user-sync branch. Pass the credential owner's userId (null for team credentials), rather than the credential primary key.
outros: Bigin passes credentialId as the userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens. This value originates from credential.id, so synchronization sends the credential primary key as calcomUserId and requests tokens for the wrong user; team credentials also incorrectly enter the user-sync branch. Thread credential.userId through refreshAccessToken and pass that value instead.

Pass the credential owner's userId rather than credentialId. The new refreshOAuthTokens contract uses its third argument as calcomUserId in the sync request (and to distinguish user credentials). Credential IDs are unrelated to user IDs, so sync requests target the wrong user whenever those IDs differ, potentially refreshing another user's credentials or failing to find the intended account.

The helper's third argument is a userId and is sent as calcomUserId, but credentialId here is credential.id (confirmed at its assignment and refreshAccessToken parameter). When these IDs differ, the sync endpoint requests tokens for the wrong user or cannot find the user. Pass the owning credential.userId separately rather than the credential primary key.

grupos.texto: parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws when parsing fails, so the `tokenResponse.success` check on the next line is dead code and the previous error logging was removed. A failed refresh now throws out of refreshAccessToken instead of keeping the old credentials. Catch the error or restore the previous handling.

The app slug passed to refreshOAuthTokens is "msteams", but this adapter is the office365-video app. The sync endpoint is asked for the wrong app's credentials. Use the correct slug "office365-video".

refreshOAuthTokens is called with credentialId as its third argument, but that argument is `userId`. With credential sync enabled, the sync endpoint receives the credential id as `calcomUserId`, so it looks up the wrong user. Pass the credential's userId instead, which means threading it into refreshAccessToken.
outros: refreshOAuthTokens expects the Cal.com user id as its third argument, but `credentialId` is passed. With credential sync enabled, that id is sent as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint. The endpoint can then return another user's tokens, which get stored on this credential. Pass `credential.userId` instead.

refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter is the Cal.com userId, but this call passes `credentialId`. In sync mode the credential id is sent to the sync endpoint as calcomUserId, so the wrong user's tokens may be fetched. Pass the credential's userId instead.

refreshOAuthTokens expects the Cal.com userId as its third argument, but `credentialId` is passed. In sync mode the credential id is sent as `calcomUserId`, so the endpoint returns tokens for the wrong user, or none. Pass the credential's userId instead.

The third argument of refreshOAuthTokens is `userId`, but `credentialId` is passed here. With credential sync enabled, the sync endpoint receives a credential id as calcomUserId, so the wrong user's tokens are fetched. It also wrongly activates the sync path. Pass the credential's userId.

The third argument of refreshOAuthTokens is documented and named as the Cal.com user id (it is sent as `calcomUserId`), but this call passes `credentialId`. With credential sync enabled, the sync endpoint gets a credential id labelled as a user id. Pass the credential's userId instead.

refreshOAuthTokens expects the Cal.com userId as its third argument, but `credentialId` (credential.id) is passed. When credential sync is enabled, the sync endpoint is called with the credential id as calcomUserId, so it refreshes the wrong user's tokens or fails. Pass the credential's userId.

grupos.texto: parseRefreshTokenResponse now returns a zod SafeParseReturnType ({success, data}), but this caller assigns it directly to `key` and saves it as the credential key. The old code saved the parsed credentials. The stored credential is now wrapped as {success, data}, which breaks later token reads. Use `.data` after checking `.success`.
outros: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a zod SafeParseReturnType (`{success, data}`), not the parsed key, and the code assigns it straight to `key`. The credential is therefore saved as `{success: true, data: ...}` and the token fields are lost. Use `.data` from the parse result.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a zod SafeParse result ({success, data}), not the parsed key. Assigning it to `key` and saving it with prisma.credential.update stores {success:true,data:{...}} as the credential key. Google tokens then can't be read afterwards. Use `.data` from the result as the key.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a zod SafeParse result ({success, data}), not the parsed key. It is stored as `key` in the credential update, so the DB gets {success:true,data:{...}} and the Google credential is corrupted. Use `.data` (e.g. `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data`) as the key.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a safeParse result ({success, data}), not the parsed credential. The result is saved as `key`, so the stored Google credential becomes {success:true,data:{...}} and later reads of refresh_token and access_token fail. Use `.data` of the result as the key.

grupos.texto: The webhook secret is checked with a plain !== comparison, which leaks timing information and lets an attacker recover the secret byte by byte. Compare the header value and the secret with crypto.timingSafeEqual, after checking that both are strings of equal length, so the comparison runs in constant time.
outros: The webhook secret is compared with `!==`, which is not constant-time, and the comparison is not guarded against a missing or array-valued header. This allows timing attacks on the secret, which would let an attacker overwrite any user's app credentials. Use crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers.

grupos.texto: The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]", not a wildcard. The schema therefore requires a numeric property named "[object Object]", so safeParse always fails in credential-sync mode and the function throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Use `.passthrough()` on an object with access_token and optional numeric expiry fields instead.
outros: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to a fixed string key such as "ZodString", so minimumTokenResponseSchema requires a literal numeric property with that name. Every synced token response fails validation and throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Use `z.object({access_token: z.string()}).passthrough()` instead.

The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` evaluate to a literal string like "ZodString" and not to a wildcard. The schema therefore requires a numeric property with that nonsense name and never matches real token responses. In sync mode every refresh throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Use `.passthrough()` and a real expiry check instead.

grupos.texto: In sync mode this returns a raw fetch Response. Callers such as Google (`res?.data`), zohocrm and zoho-bigin (`.data.error`) and hubspot (a token object) expect the shape their refreshFunction returns (axios response, Gaxios response or token). With credential sync on, those callers break because the Response has no `.data` and the body is not parsed. Return the same shape as the refresh function, or have each caller handle the sync response.
outros: When credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response. The refresh callback otherwise returns a gaxios response with `.data`. This caller still reads `res?.data`, which is undefined on a fetch Response, so `token.access_token` throws. The Response body must be parsed with `.json()` and normalised to the old shape.

grupos.texto: WHAT: Missing refresh_token is replaced with literal string "refresh_token". WHY: Stores bogus refresh token in DB, breaking all future refreshes and masking provider errors. HOW: Preserve existing credential refresh_token or throw instead of injecting placeholder.

WHAT: Team branch only checks members.some accepted:true, while non-team path calls throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam. WHY: Any non-admin team member can craft state.teamId to create team-level credentials, privilege escalation vs admin-only intent. HOW: Require admin role check for team branch too.

WHAT: Checks response.statusText !== "OK" instead of response.ok and builds jsforce.Connection from stale credentialKey.access_token/instance_url ignoring accessTokenParsed.data. WHY: Refresh never takes effect (old token reused) and valid refreshes can throw on runtimes where statusText is empty. HOW: Check !response.ok and use parsed access_token/instance_url for connection and DB update.

Direct !== comparison of webhook secret leaks via timing attack. Use constant-time comparison (e.g., crypto.timingSafeEqual on hashed/buffered values with length check) instead of `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

JSDoc documents both appData.type and appData.appId as 'the app slug'. Type is the credential type, not the slug (cf. app-credential.ts uses appMetadata.type for type vs appMetadata.slug for appId). Fix type param doc to e.g. 'the app credential type'.

When sharing is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns fetch Response, but caller types/expects HubspotToken from hubspotClient. Response shape at emit site disagrees with consumption site; downstream token field access gets undefined.

WHAT: Sync branch returns raw fetch Response while callers expect provider-specific shapes (axios .data, Gaxios .res.data, HubspotToken object).
