WHY: Google does res?.data, zoho-bigin/zohocrm do tokenInfo.data, hubspot/zoom/webex parse as token JSON, so sync Response causes TypeError or mis-parsed tokens and broken refresh. HOW: Return normalized token JSON (await response.json()) or branch per caller contract.
outros: When sharing is enabled this returns raw fetch() Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, but consumers (Google .data, Zoho/Bigin axios .data, Hubspot HubspotToken, Office365/Zoom/Webex handleErrorsJson/handleZoomResponse) still expect original provider shape. Parse/map the sync-endpoint payload to the expected shape or update every caller; otherwise enabled path throws/TypeErrors.

grupos.texto: WHAT: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys [z.string().toString()] which are literal garbage keys, not wildcards, and zod strips unknown keys. WHY: With sync enabled validation drops expiry/refresh fields and passes with only access_token, corrupting downstream credential merges. HOW: Define explicit optional fields (expires_in/expiry_date/refresh_token passthrough) instead of computed keys.
outros: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys so real token responses fail validation and throw, and missing refresh_token is replaced with literal placeholder then persisted, corrupting future refreshes. Fix to minimal access_token + passthrough and preserve real refresh_token.

grupos.texto: WHAT: JSON.parse(req.query.state) with no try/catch on attacker-controlled query param. WHY: Malformed state throws SyntaxError, crashing every OAuth callback/add and createOAuthAppCredential path with 500 instead of 400. HOW: Wrap in try/catch and return undefined / 400 on invalid state.
outros: JSON.parse(req.query.state) throws SyntaxError on malformed/tampered state with no try/catch, breaking OAuth callbacks with unhandled 500. Validate and handle parse failure.
Same unguarded JSON.parse(req.query.state): malformed state throws unhandled and breaks the add flow. Guard parse failure.

grupos.texto: refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response when sync is enabled but this caller expects axios shape (tokenInfo.data.error). Also passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects userId (calcomUserId). Map fetch response via .json() to axios shape and pass credential.userId.
outros: WHAT: Passes credentialId as userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens (calcomUserId=credentialId). WHY: Sync endpoint receives wrong identity, returns wrong user's token and leaks/mixes credentials across users. HOW: Pass credential.userId like other services.

When sharing is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns fetch Response which has no .data, but caller uses tokenInfo.data.error (axios shape). Same mismatch in zohocrm. Fetch vs axios shapes must agree; parse sync response or preserve axios shape.

grupos.texto: WHAT: zod parse, symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse throw unhandled (no try/catch) with no method guard. WHY: Invalid body/keys or GET request crashes handler with 500 and leaks stack, instead of 400/405. HOW: Wrap parse/decrypt in try/catch returning 400 and restrict to POST.
outros: schema .parse plus symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse throw unhandled (ZodError, decrypt error, SyntaxError) on invalid body or tampered keys, crashing webhook with 500. Use safeParse and try/catch with 400 responses.

grupos.texto: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns SafeParse result {success,data}, but call site stores that wrapper as credential `key` (previously googleCredentialSchema.parse() returned the plain object). Store `key.data` / handle wrapper, otherwise persisted credential becomes {success,data} shape and subsequent credential reads fail.
outros: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a SafeParse result {success,data}, not the parsed key. Storing it directly as `key` writes the wrapper to the credential. Unwrap like other callers: check .success and use .data.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns SafeParse wrapper {success,data} but code stores the whole wrapper as credential.key. Office365calendar in same PR unwraps via .data. Persisted credential will be {success,data} instead of tokens, so next load fails validation. Unwrap to .data after success check.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

oauth-credential-sync-and-app-integratio.prTitle: OAuth credential sync and app integration enhancements

grupos.texto: WHAT: the deleteMany WHERE now uses `OR` between `(method = SMS AND scheduledDate <= now)` and `retryCount > 1`, but WorkflowReminder has no index on the newly added retryCount column. WHY: Postgres cannot satisfy a two-way OR using the existing (method, scheduled, scheduledDate) index and will fall back to a sequential scan of the entire WorkflowReminder table on every cron invocation, turning a previously indexed delete into a full table scan as the table grows. HOW: add an index on retryCount (or restructure so each branch is index-usable), then re-check the query plan.
The failed-send branch does not increment retryCount on the success path.
The retryCount increment is duplicated in the else-branch and catch.

WHAT: retryCount is incremented with a read-value computed at the start of the run (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`) instead of an atomic increment. WHY: if two cron invocations overlap (or the same reminder is processed twice before the write commits), both read the same retryCount and both write N+1, so failures are undercounted and the reminder can loop forever without ever reaching the `retryCount > 1` deletion threshold. HOW: use `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }` so the increment is atomic (the initial read value is then irrelevant).
outros: `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` is a read-modify-write of the value fetched at the top of the handler, not an atomic increment. Two overlapping cron runs both read the same retryCount and both write the same +1, losing an update, so failed reminders can be retried indefinitely and never reach the `gt: 1` deletion threshold. Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` instead of computing from the stale in-memory value (same issue in the else branch at lines 179-186).

grupos.texto: This new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` sits inside the catch block, which is NOT protected by any try/catch. If this update throws (e.g. the reminder was already removed by the `deleteMany` at the top of the file during a concurrent run -> Prisma P2025, or a transient DB error), the exception escapes the `for` loop and rejects the handler, so all remaining unscheduled reminders are skipped and the cron request fails. Previously the catch only did `console.log`, so a single bad reminder never aborted the batch and the endpoint always returned 200. Wrap this update in its own try/catch (or `updateMany`/catch-and-log) so a failed retry-count write cannot take down the whole scheduling run.
outros: WHAT: the catch block performs an unguarded `prisma.workflowReminder.update` while handling the scheduling error. WHY: if this write itself rejects (e.g. the row was concurrently removed, or a transient DB error), the rejection is not caught and escapes the for-loop, aborting the whole cron run so all remaining reminders go unprocessed. HOW: wrap the retryCount update in its own try/catch (log and continue) so a failure to record the retry does not abort processing of the remaining reminders.

grupos.texto: The `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter was moved from the top-level `where` into only the first arm of the new `OR`, so the second arm `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` now matches reminders of ANY method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, etc.). The statement's own comment says it should "delete all scheduled sms reminders", but this deletion is no longer SMS-scoped: as soon as another workflow method ever increments retryCount (or any non-SMS row with retryCount > 1 exists), the SMS cron job will silently delete those unrelated reminders. Keep the method filter common to both branches, e.g. `where: { method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, OR: [{ scheduledDate: { lte: ... } }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }] }`.
outros: The comment "//delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date" no longer describes the deleteMany below it. After this change the query also deletes reminders with retryCount > 1, and that OR branch has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, so non-SMS (email) reminders with retryCount > 1 are now deleted too. Update the comment (or add the missing SMS filter to the retryCount branch) so the prose matches what the code actually deletes.
The deleteMany OR clause deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of method.

The second OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method` filter, unlike the first branch (`method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`). Because `retryCount` is a generic column on WorkflowReminder used by all reminder methods, this deleteMany now permanently deletes every reminder of ANY method (including EMAIL) whose retryCount exceeds 1, even though this cron is only supposed to clean up SMS reminders. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to this branch (or scope the whole where to SMS) so non-SMS reminders are never destroyed.
The deleteMany OR clause with retryCount > 1 is not scoped to SMS.
The delete guard's second OR branch (`retryCount > 1`) has no method filter, so this SMS cron could delete non-SMS reminders.

grupos.texto: Update the cleanup comment to describe the new retry-exhaustion deletion branch. It currently says this deletes scheduled SMS reminders whose date has passed, but this OR branch also deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1, including future-dated reminders and without an SMS restriction. The comment now misrepresents the scope of this destructive operation.

Restrict retry-limit deletion to unscheduled SMS reminders (or reset retryCount when scheduling succeeds). A reminder can fail twice, enter the next invocation with retryCount = 2, and successfully schedule; the success update does not reset that count. This unconditional OR arm deletes that successfully scheduled future reminder on the following run, losing its tracking/reference before delivery. It also removes the SMS method restriction from this cleanup arm.

The new database update inside catch can itself throw when a reminder has been deleted during scheduling. Booking cancellation deletes reminders through handleCancelBooking and deleteScheduledSMSReminder, so a concurrent cancellation followed by a scheduling error now rejects the entire cron handler and prevents the remaining reminders from being processed. Use an updateMany filtered by the reminder ID to tolerate an already-deleted row, and guard errors from retry bookkeeping so they do not escape the per-reminder error handler.
outros: Keep retry bookkeeping best-effort inside this error handler. Previously a scheduling error was logged and the loop continued; now, if workflowReminder.update rejects (for example because the reminder was concurrently deleted, or the database failure that caused the original error persists), that rejection escapes the catch and aborts the handler, leaving all subsequent reminders unprocessed. Protect this update with its own error handling so recording a failed attempt cannot break the scheduler's continue-on-error contract.

grupos.texto: Retry counts are assigned from the stale findMany snapshot instead of incremented atomically, both here and in the catch branch. Two overlapping cron requests can each fail scheduling the same reminder with retryCount zero and both write one, so two failed attempts do not reach the deletion threshold and additional attempts are scheduled. Use Prisma's atomic retryCount increment operation in both failure branches.
outros: The failure counter uses a stale read-modify-write value. If two cron executions select the same reminder at retryCount 0 and both fail, each writes 1, losing one failure; the reminder survives the > 1 cleanup threshold and can receive extra retries. Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` in both this update and the catch-path update so concurrent failures are not overwritten.

grupos.texto: retryCount is only incremented when message and sendTo are both present and scheduleSMS returns a falsy value. When sendTo is missing (e.g. a missing or invalid phone number), or the message is empty, the if-block is skipped. retryCount is never incremented, so the reminder is retried on every cron run until its date, which is the behavior this PR is meant to stop. Add an else branch that increments retryCount when the message or sendTo check fails.

The prisma.workflowReminder.update inside the catch block is unguarded. If it throws (e.g. the record was deleted concurrently or the DB errors), the exception escapes the for-loop and the handler. The remaining reminders are then skipped and the cron returns a 500. Wrap the update in its own try/catch, or log the error first and then update inside a nested try/catch.
outros: The retryCount update inside the catch block is unguarded. If it throws, the error escapes the catch and aborts the whole loop, so the remaining reminders are never processed. Wrap the update in its own try/catch.

grupos.texto: The comment says this deletes scheduled SMS reminders past their date, but the new OR branch `retryCount > 1` has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter. It therefore also deletes email and WhatsApp reminders in this SMS cron job. Add the SMS method filter to that branch and update the comment to mention the retry-count deletion.
outros: The retry-count delete branch has no method filter, so this SMS cron handler can delete non-SMS WorkflowReminder rows (email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to that OR branch so it matches the original SMS-only scope.

The `retryCount > 1` branch of the deleteMany OR is not restricted to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`. This SMS cron can therefore delete non-SMS reminders (email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to that branch.

The SMS cron's deleteMany was previously scoped to method SMS, but the new OR branch `retryCount > 1` has no method filter. It can delete email or WhatsApp reminders that reach that retry count. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the retryCount branch.

grupos.texto: WHAT: retryCount is only incremented inside if(message?.length && sendTo); when sendTo is missing or message is empty the loop silently skips with no increment. WHY: Reminders with no phone number or empty body retry forever until scheduledDate, leaving the unbounded rescheduling the PR claims to fix. HOW: Add an else that increments retryCount (or deletes/cancels) when message/sendTo is falsy.

WHAT: The catch block unconditionally increments retryCount for any exception (profile/bookerUrl/templating/rate-limit/Twilio outage). WHY: Two consecutive cron runs with a transient global failure increment every pending SMS reminder to 2 and the startup deleteMany then wipes the entire future SMS queue, not just permanently-invalid numbers. HOW: Only increment on permanent scheduleSMS failure, or distinguish transient errors from terminal ones before counting toward deletion.

Stale comment: line 28 says 'delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date' but the new OR clause also deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of method or date. Update the comment to describe both branches.

WHAT: The second OR branch deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount gt 1 without filtering method=SMS, scheduled=false, or scheduledDate. WHY: It deletes EMAIL/WHATSAPP rows if they ever get a count, and deletes successfully-scheduled future SMS rows whose retryCount was left at 2 on success, orphaning Twilio scheduled messages and breaking cancel. HOW: Scope the branch to method SMS and unscheduled, or reset retryCount to 0 on successful schedule.
outros: Second OR branch filters only on retryCount gt 1 with no method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, while the first branch and the findMany query are SMS-only. This deletes non-SMS WorkflowReminders with retryCount>1. Scope it to SMS (e.g. method SMS AND (past date OR retryCount>1)) to match declared intent.

Second OR branch filters only on retryCount gt 1 with no method=SMS, so deleteMany deletes WorkflowReminders of ANY method with retryCount>1. Scope it to SMS (add method: WorkflowMethods.SMS to that branch) to avoid deleting unrelated reminders sharing the retryCount column.

goldens.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

sms-workflow-reminder-retry-count-tracki.prTitle: SMS workflow reminder retry count tracking

grupos.texto: On a successful enable (response.status === 200) the modal no longer calls onEnable(); it only advances to SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes, and onEnable() is now invoked solely from the 'close' button (line 269). If the user dismisses the Dialog via ESC or an overlay click, DialogContent's onOpenChange fires (wired to a plain setEnableModalOpen toggle at apps/web/pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:64 and the conditional render at apps/web/components/security/TwoFactorAuthSection.tsx:36), so onEnable never runs. The parent callbacks (setEnableModalOpen(false) + utils.viewer.me.invalidate() / setEnabled(true)) are skipped, leaving the 2FA Switch unchecked and the UI showing 2FA as disabled even though the server has enabled it. Call onEnable() from the dismiss path (onOpenChange) or when transitioning into DisplayBackupCodes, not only from the Close button.

The new backup-code branch authenticates without guaranteeing the password check ran: password verification at line 121 is gated on `!credentials.totpCode`, and the branch at line 131 triggers on any truthy `credentials.backupCode` regardless of that gate. A POST to the credentials callback supplying a valid backup code together with any non-empty totpCode therefore takes the backup branch (skipping TOTP validation) while line 121 skips password verification — granting a session using only a second-factor backup code, with no account password. Require the password check before the backup branch, or include backupCode in the guard at line 121 (e.g. `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode && !credentials.backupCode)`).

TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable gained a required third parameter `backupCode`, but not every caller was updated. apps/web/components/security/DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:38 still calls `TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable(password, totpCode)` with only two arguments. This is now a type error (missing required argument) and sends `backupCode: undefined` at runtime. Update that consumer to pass the backup code (or make the parameter optional) so the signature change is followed through everywhere it is used.

The default export is named `TwoFactor` but this file (BackupCode.tsx) renders the backup-code field and is imported as `BackupCode` by callers. The copied identifier misstates what the component is; rename the function to `BackupCode` so the name matches the file, the imports and the rendered content.

This 'copy' test does not verify the copy behaviour it names: it clicks backup-codes-copy and then only waits for the toast-success element. The handler (EnableTwoFactorModal) runs navigator.clipboard.writeText(...) without awaiting it and then calls showToast(...) unconditionally, so the toast appears even when the clipboard write is removed or fails. The assertion therefore passes with the backup-code copy feature broken; assert the actual effect (clipboard content, or that the formatted codes reached writeText) instead of the toast.

This assertion cannot fail: page.locator(...).isChecked() returns a Promise<boolean>, and expect(promise).toBeTruthy() is true for any Promise, so it passes whether the switch is checked or not (the PR's own FIXME notes this). Use `await expect(locator).toBeChecked()` so the check actually reflects the switch state.

Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, breaking the stated invariant that each backup code is single-use. Two concurrent login requests with the same backup code both read the same user.backupCodes array and both pass `index !== -1` before either `prisma.user.update` commits; both then persist a stale array (each nulling only its own index), so the code authenticates twice. Make consumption atomic (e.g. compare-and-swap on the encrypted value/updatedAt, a transaction with a conditional update, or an optimistic-locking retry) so exactly one request can claim a given code.
outros: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write: the code is validated with indexOf (line 144) and only then persisted via prisma.user.update (line 149), with no unique constraint or lock. Two concurrent login requests sending the same valid backup code both read the unchanged row, both pass the indexOf check, and both obtain a session, violating the 'each backup code can be used exactly once' invariant. Consume the code atomically (e.g. a conditional update on the raw encrypted value / a dedicated used-backup-codes table with a unique index) so only one request can succeed.

grupos.texto: The submitted backup code is matched against stored codes with `backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`, i.e. ordinary short-circuiting string equality on an authentication credential. String comparison returns early on the first differing byte, so response timing can leak how much of a code the attacker guessed. Compare with a constant-time comparison (e.g. `crypto.timingSafeEqual` over equal-length buffers) instead of `indexOf`/`===`.
outros: The disable endpoint validates the backup code with `backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`, a non-constant-time string comparison of a security credential, leaking correctness via execution time. Use a constant-time comparison (e.g. `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers) rather than `indexOf`/`===`.

grupos.texto: After two-factor authentication completes, consider implementing a clear user journey: either redirect to a dedicated two-factor page or conditionally render the two-factor component based on user state.
Add error handling to clear the polling interval when a 2FA attempt fails, and ensure the interval is cleared on component unmount to avoid memory leaks.
No defect of the assigned class found: every truthiness test is on a value whose only falsy state is the intended "absent" state, and index-existence checks use explicit === -1.

The backup-code branch accepts a valid backup code even when an arbitrary nonempty totpCode has skipped password verification. The preceding guards at lines 113–125 trust the presence of totpCode, but this new branch does not validate it, allowing a holder of a backup code to log in to a password account without knowing its password by submitting both fields. Require password verification for backup-code authentication rather than allowing an unverified totpCode to bypass it.

Successful enablement no longer invokes onEnable until the backup-code screen's explicit Close button is clicked. Dismissing that screen through the dialog's onOpenChange instead only closes it in the parent and does not invalidate viewer.me, leaving the settings switch showing disabled even though the server has enabled 2FA. Ensure dismissal after successful enablement also invokes the completion callback and resets the setup state.

The handler shows “Backup codes copied!” immediately after calling `navigator.clipboard.writeText`, without awaiting its promise. If clipboard access is denied or the write otherwise rejects, the user still receives a success message and may close the dialog believing their recovery codes were saved. Await the clipboard write and show the success toast only after it resolves; handle rejection with an appropriate translated failure message.

The copy test only waits for a success toast, but the implementation emits that toast unconditionally without awaiting navigator.clipboard.writeText. Removing the clipboard write entirely, copying an empty string, or rejecting the write would still pass this test. Read the clipboard after the click and compare its contents with the displayed backup codes so the test verifies the actual copy effect.

The download assertion checks only the static filename from the anchor's download attribute. It still passes if the blob contains empty or incorrect backup codes, leaving the essential recovery-code export behavior unverified. Read the downloaded file and compare its contents to the displayed codes, including their formatting.

Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read/modify/write, so the same code can grant access more than once despite the exactly-once behavior promised by this change. Two concurrent login requests can both read the original backupCodes, pass indexOf, and successfully execute this unconditional update by user ID. Concurrent use of different codes can also overwrite each other's removal, restoring a consumed code. Consume the code atomically (for example, compare-and-swap against the original encrypted backupCodes value and require exactly one affected row before authenticating, with appropriate retry handling).
outros: Backup-code consumption overwrites the encrypted list by user ID without checking that the stored list still matches the value read before verification. Concurrent requests can both authenticate with the same single-use code, and requests using different codes can overwrite each other's removals and restore a consumed code. Use a conditional atomic update matching the original backupCodes ciphertext and reject or retry authentication if no row was updated.

Consume backup codes atomically rather than unconditionally replacing the array read earlier. Two simultaneous login requests can read the same backupCodes value, both find the same code, and both successfully update and authenticate, violating the single-use guarantee. With different codes, the last writer also restores the code consumed by the first writer. Use a conditional update against the original encrypted value and require exactly one affected row (retry validation on contention), or serialize consumption in a transaction with an appropriate row lock.

grupos.texto: Backup codes are authentication secrets, but indexOf compares their plaintext strings using ordinary equality and stops at the first match. This is not a constant-time credential check and can expose comparison-dependent timing. Validate the normalized code's format/length, compare fixed-length buffers with crypto.timingSafeEqual, and scan all stored slots without early termination (including handling consumed null slots) before deciding whether authentication succeeds.
outros: The new backup-code verification uses indexOf on plaintext secrets, so both string comparison and array traversal are non-constant-time. This exposes a timing-dependent credential check on the endpoint that disables 2FA. Use a shared constant-time verifier that validates input length, compares fixed-length buffers with crypto.timingSafeEqual, and traverses every slot without stopping on a match.

grupos.texto: The default export in BackupCode.tsx is named `TwoFactor`, which is the name of the separate TOTP component. It is a copy-paste leftover and misleads readers and stack traces. Rename it to `BackupCode`.
The error log says "cannot proceed with backup code login", but this endpoint disables two-factor authentication and does not log in. Change the message to describe disabling 2FA with a backup code.

The user-supplied backup code is checked against the decrypted codes with Array.indexOf, which compares strings in non-constant time. Compare each stored code with crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers, without short-circuiting across entries. The same comparison in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts should be changed too.

Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write: the codes are decrypted, checked, and then re-encrypted and saved with no guard. Two concurrent logins using the same backup code can both pass the check, so the single-use guarantee is broken, and one request's write can overwrite the other's. Fix it with an optimistic check, for example update with a `where` clause that matches the previously read `backupCodes` value and fail if no row is updated, or run the read and write in a transaction with a row lock.
outros: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write. Two concurrent logins with the same code can both read the list before either write lands, so both pass the check and authenticate. This breaks the 'each code can be used exactly once' guarantee. Make the consume step atomic, for example with a conditional update that matches the previously read encrypted backupCodes value and fails if zero rows were updated, or a transaction with a row lock.

grupos.texto: After a successful enable, `onEnable()` is no longer called and is only called from the backup-codes Close button. If the user dismisses the dialog by Escape or overlay click (`onOpenChange`) while the codes are displayed, the parent is never notified that 2FA is enabled. The modal also keeps its step state and the plaintext backup codes. Call `onEnable` when 2FA is enabled, or make the dialog's `onOpenChange(false)` on the DisplayBackupCodes step run the same handler as Close, which resets state and clears `backupCodes`.
outros: `onEnable()` used to run right after the TOTP code was verified. It now runs only from the backup-codes "close" button. If the user dismisses the dialog another way (escape, an outside click or the X, all via `onOpenChange`), 2FA is already enabled server-side but `onEnable` never fires. The parent's state and UI then stay stale and the switch still shows 2FA as off. Call `onEnable` when verification succeeds, or call it from the dialog's `onOpenChange` close path while on the DisplayBackupCodes step.

grupos.texto: WHAT: The new backup-code login branch authenticates without verifying the password when credentials also contain any totpCode value (password check at line 121 is skipped when totpCode is truthy, and the backup branch never checks it). WHY: An attacker holding only a backup code can add a dummy totpCode to the credentials callback and log in without the password, reducing two factors to one. HOW: Verify the password whenever backupCode is used (or decouple the password check from totpCode presence).

WHAT: resetState() clears only password/error/step and never clears backupCodes, secret, dataUri, nor revokes backupCodesUrl. WHY: Closing the modal after setup leaves TOTP secret and backup codes in memory and leaks the Blob object URL on every setup/close cycle. HOW: Clear those states and call URL.revokeObjectURL in resetState and on unmount.

WHAT: req.body.backupCode.replaceAll assumes a string with no type guard. WHY: A non-string JSON value (number/array) throws TypeError and returns 500 instead of the 400 IncorrectBackupCode contract, breaking error handling and enabling error-probing. HOW: Validate typeof backupCode === 'string' (or String(...)) before replaceAll.

Component in BackupCode.tsx is named `TwoFactor` (`export default function TwoFactor`) while the file is BackupCode.tsx and it is imported as `BackupCode`. The name disagrees with the code's contract and duplicates the real TwoFactor component, misleading callers/readers. Rename to `BackupCode`.

Assertion `expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` never fails: isChecked() returns a Promise which is always truthy. Must be `await expect(locator).toBeChecked()` or `expect(await locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy()`. First enable-2FA test therefore passes even after PR inserts DisplayBackupCodes step it never dismisses.

Download test only asserts suggestedFilename, explicitly TODOing file-content check. Empty/wrong backupCodes blob with correct filename still passes; assert downloaded file lines equal displayed/formatted backup codes.
Copy test only waits for toast-success, explicitly TODOing clipboard check. Broken writeText (wrong format/empty) still passes; assert clipboard content equals formatted backup codes.

WHAT: Backup-code single-use is enforced by non-atomic check-then-write (indexOf, then a separate prisma.user.update that nulls the slot). WHY: Two concurrent logins presenting the same code can both pass the indexOf check before either write lands, so one code grants access twice despite the exactly-once contract. HOW: Consume the code atomically (transaction/conditional update retrying on conflict).
outros: Backup code consumption is non-atomic read-modify-write (decrypt, indexOf, null entry, encrypt+update). Concurrent logins with same code can both succeed, violating single-use invariant. Make it atomic (transaction/conditional update).

goldens.comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

grupos.texto: The rewritten "should combine authorization and filter conditions" test cannot fail if the combination is broken. The fixture creates a single booking that satisfies the auth condition (userId = user.id AND teamId IS NULL) and the filter condition (eventTypeId = eventType.id) independently, so getBaseConditions returning auth-only, filter-only, or the AND combination all yield the same single-row result asserted here. Only a `1=0` result would be caught. Make the data distinguish the two: add a booking that matches the filter but not the auth (e.g. a team booking with the same eventTypeId), then assert the result excludes it, so that dropping either branch changes the returned rows.

This PR removes the public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method and changes `getAuthorizationConditions()`/`getFilterConditions()` to return `Prisma.Sql` instead of `Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput`. Consumers written against the old contract break: a caller doing `service.findMany({ select, where })` now hits an undefined method, and a caller that spread the returned conditions into a Prisma `where` (or passed them to `findMany({ where })`) can no longer use a `Prisma.Sql` fragment there — it is only valid interpolated into `$queryRaw`. The PR updated only the integration test to the new `getBaseConditions()` + `$queryRaw` usage but did not update any other caller; find and migrate any remaining `InsightsBookingService.findMany`/`where: <conditions>` call sites to the new SQL-fragment contract.
outros: WHAT: The public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method was removed and replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns a SQL fragment — the analogous method is still present in the sibling `insightsRouting.ts` (lines 63-76). WHY: Any existing caller of `InsightsBookingService.findMany` (e.g. `service.findMany({ select: {...} })`) now fails to compile or throws `service.findMany is not a function` at runtime; the class's primary data-access contract was dropped without a compatibility shim. HOW: Either retain `findMany` delegating to `getBaseConditions()` (build the raw query with the returned conditions) or confirm/update every consumer of the service; note no production caller exists in this repo, so this is an API-surface regression to verify against downstream consumers.

grupos.texto: WHAT: `getBaseConditions` returns `filterConditions` alone (no authorization predicate) when `authConditions` is falsy (`else if (filterConditions) { return filterConditions; }`). WHY: The WHERE clause returned to consumers then contains no ownership/authorization restriction, so a caller using it would return every booking matching the filters (e.g. all bookings for the given eventTypeId/memberUserId) regardless of the requesting user's org/team membership — an authorization-boundary bypass if `getAuthorizationConditions()` ever yields a falsy value. HOW: Always AND the authorization predicate with the filters and fall back to `NOTHING_CONDITION` when no auth predicate exists, e.g. `return filterConditions ? Prisma.sql`(${authConditions}) AND (${filterConditions})` : authConditions;` (or keep the `NOTHING_CONDITION` default when auth is missing).
outros: Dead branches in getBaseConditions: getAuthorizationConditions() is typed Promise<Prisma.Sql> and buildAuthorizationConditions() always returns a Prisma.Sql (worst case NOTHING_CONDITION), so authConditions is never null/undefined/empty — always a truthy object. The `if (authConditions && filterConditions)` check therefore reduces to `filterConditions`, and both the `else if (filterConditions)` (76-77) and the final `else` (78-79) can never execute. The intended no-authorization fallback to NOTHING_CONDITION is unreachable; the code reads as if auth could be falsy when it cannot.

grupos.texto: I could not construct a failure of my assigned class within the lines this PR added or modified.

getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql, so the `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches (returning NOTHING_CONDITION) in getBaseConditions can never execute. Simplify to: if filterConditions, combine it with authConditions; otherwise return authConditions.

Unreachable branches in getBaseConditions: authConditions is always a truthy Prisma.Sql object (never null, NOTHING is `1=0`), so `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else { return NOTHING }` can never execute. Simplify to if(filter) return auth AND filter else return auth, or make the nothing-case explicit.

Expected Sql is built as a flat Prisma.sql literal with raw values, but service builds nested Sql via Prisma.sql`(${acc}) AND (${condition})` where values are Sql objects. toEqual compares structure, so it always fails even when SQL is semantically identical. Fix validator: do not use toEqual on Prisma.Sql; assert on executed query results or normalized sql/values (e.g., compare baseConditions.sql and flattened values) or build expected with same nesting.

goldens.comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

feat-convert-insightsbookingservice-to-u.prTitle: feat: convert InsightsBookingService to use Prisma.sql raw queries

grupos.texto: WHAT: the new `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` makes `Post#cook` return completely unsanitized HTML, and Jobs::PollFeed stores untrusted feed content this way (poll_feed.rb:35-36 → TopicEmbed.import, unlike import_remote which sanitizes via Readability's tag/attribute whitelist). WHY: the stored `cooked` value is then emitted with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19, and that page is served from the forum's own origin — so a malicious/compromised RSS feed item containing `<script>` or `onerror=` runs attacker JavaScript in the forum origin and can read cookies/session and perform authenticated actions (stored XSS). HOW: sanitize the raw HTML before persisting it (e.g. run the feed content through the same HTML sanitizer used for regular posts, or restrict the raw_html cook path to trusted, pre-sanitized sources only).

The post date uses a hard-coded strftime format `"%e %b %Y"`. `%b` emits English month abbreviations (Jan, Feb, ...) no matter what locale the viewer is in, so the date is frozen to en-US while the surrounding strings in this same view are localized via I18n.t. This is a locale-pinned user-facing format; it should be localized (e.g. via the app's localized date helper / l( ) rather than a literal strftime pattern).

Host identity is compared case-sensitively: `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Hostnames are case-insensitive, so a referer such as `http://EVILTROUT.COM/...` never matches the configured `eviltrout.com` (and the same flaw exists in lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 for `URI(@embed_url).host`). Normalize both sides with downcase before comparing so case variations of the same host are treated identically.

These two tests do not verify the conditions they name. `execute` is guarded by `feed_polling_enabled? && feed_polling_url.present? && embed_by_username.present?`, and feed_polling_enabled defaults to false. Neither test stubs feed_polling_enabled? to true, so the guard short-circuits at the first clause and poll_feed is never called no matter what feed_polling_url/embed_by_username are. Both would still pass if the URL/username checks were deleted entirely. Stub `SiteSetting.stubs(:feed_polling_enabled?).returns(true)` in each so the specific condition under test is actually reached.

The test is named 'is 404 without an embed_url' but passes for the wrong reason: it never sets embeddable_host, which defaults to '' so the before_filter `ensure_embeddable` raises at the blank-host check before `params.require(:embed_url)` is reached. The request is rejected regardless of whether the embed_url requirement exists, so the test would still pass if that requirement were removed. Stub a valid embeddable_host here so the failure is actually attributable to the missing embed_url.

TopicEmbed.import does a check-then-insert on embed_url (where(...).first, then TopicEmbed.create!) with no rescue for the unique index declared on topic_embeds.embed_url. The only guard against concurrent intake is the Redis throttle in TopicRetriever, which is bypassed for staff (retrieve_topic.rb:17 passes no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)) and can expire while a slow retrieval (which may synchronously run a full PollFeed, topic_retriever.rb:41) is still running. Two interleaved retrievals for the same URL both see embed.blank? and both attempt creation; the loser raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, which is unhandled anywhere in the job path, breaking execution. Guard the create against the race (rescue/retry on RecordNotUnique, or use find_or_create_by on embed_url inside the transaction) so concurrent retrievals cannot raise.

The controller enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` and never instantiates `TopicRetriever`, but spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb (lines 40-46, also added by this PR) declares the opposite contract for this action: it sets `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)` and then expects the `best` request to satisfy those mocks. Because the request path only enqueues a Sidekiq job (which is not executed inline here), `TopicRetriever.new` is never called during `get :best`, so the expectation is unmet and the 'tells the topic retriever to work when no previous embed is found' example fails. The two hunks encode two different interfaces for the same retrieval trigger; align them (either have the controller call TopicRetriever directly, or update the spec to stub `Jobs.enqueue`/run the job inline).

WHAT: the if/else block opened on line 2 is closed with `<%- end if %>`, which is not valid Ruby (`if` cannot be a modifier on `end`). WHY: Erubis/ERB compiles this tag into Ruby and the resulting SyntaxError causes every render of the embed 'best' view to raise, so the entire embedded-comments feature fails to load. HOW: change line 6 to `<%- end %>` to match the `if` from line 2.
outros: The `if` opened at line 2 is closed with `<%- end if %>` at line 6. The dangling `if` has no condition, so the compiled ERB (`... else ... end if`) is invalid Ruby and raises SyntaxError when the template is compiled — `embed/best` will fail to render at all rather than showing the comments. Change line 6 to a bare `<%- end %>`.

grupos.texto: The feed item is consumed unconditionally: url = i.link, then i.title, and content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub). SimpleRSS item accessors raise NoMethodError when the element is absent (RSS 2.0 feeds frequently carry only <description>, no <content>, and some items have no <link>/<title>), so a single malformed or content-less item aborts the whole hourly job with an unhandled exception instead of skipping it. The code already anticipates a blank link (line 33 fallback) but reads i.content/i.title without a nil guard; use i.content.to_s (or fall back to i.description/summary) and skip items whose content is blank.
outros: WHAT: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every feed item has a `content` element. WHY: many RSS 2.0 items expose only `<description>` (simple-rss returns nil for `content`), so `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError and, because the job is `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the entire hourly feed import for all items is aborted. HOW: fall back to the available field, e.g. `(i.content || i.description || i.summary).to_s.scrub`, and skip items whose body is blank.

grupos.texto: The message-origin check uses substring matching: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`. Any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl is accepted (e.g. discourseUrl `https://discourse.example.com` accepts origin `https://discourse`), so a malicious page can post `discourse-resize` messages into the embed. Compare against the iframe's actual origin exactly (`e.origin !== expectedOrigin`) instead of a substring test.
The comparison `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` is safe because Discourse's Enum is 1-based.
`present?` is used explicitly rather than raw truthiness, and enum values are >= 1, so :regular is still set.
`if topic_id` is safe because topic ids are >= 1, never 0.
Lines 25-26 use blank?/!=.
`content_sha1` uses string compare and `absolutize_urls` is correct; the port guard and `sub(/^\/+/, '')` indices are correct.
The fallback on nil/empty/non-http is correct and re-guarded in import.
Uses setnx boolean and explicit no_throttle check.
Uses indexOf containment instead of origin equality, but it cannot be bypassed.

Every uncached article retrieval synchronously downloads and processes the complete configured feed before fetching the article. Because the retrieval throttle is keyed by individual embed URL, simultaneous requests for different articles each repeat the feed download and all per-item database lookups/imports, multiplying worker load by the number of requests times feed size. Coalesce feed polling with a feed-wide throttle or lock and reuse its recent results instead of executing a full poll per article.

Use a localized date formatter rather than strftime("%e %b %Y"). %b produces English month abbreviations and the fixed day-month-year order ignores the selected locale, although the neighbouring header and footer labels are translated. Embedded comments therefore show English-formatted dates for users of other locales.

Compare e.origin to the parsed origin of discourseUrl using exact equality, not indexOf. For example, discourseUrl = 'https://forum.example.com/' accepts messages from 'https://forum.example', an unrelated origin, because that origin is a substring of the configured URL. A window on that origin with a reference to the embedding window can consequently send forged discourse-resize messages and control the iframe height. Also verify e.source === iframe.contentWindow to bind accepted messages to the intended frame.

Preserve the Disqus thread creation timestamp when switching to TopicEmbed.import_remote. The previous PostCreator call passed `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`, but this replacement passes only the title, and TopicEmbed.import_remote/import never forward a timestamp to PostCreator. Imported historical topics now get the migration time as their initial post creation date while their replies retain historical dates, losing the importer's chronological fidelity. Extend the import options to forward created_at and pass the thread timestamp here.

Make creation idempotent under concurrent imports. Two workers can both read no embed at line 15 and create posts before attempting the same unique embed_url insert. The unique index correctly rolls back the losing transaction, but its unhandled uniqueness exception aborts that job (and potentially the rest of a feed polling run). This is reachable when scheduled polling overlaps retrieval-triggered polling; the per-URL retrieval throttle does not serialize those paths. Handle the conflict outside the transaction and return the winning embed/post, or serialize imports for the URL.

The missing-embed_url test does not establish a valid embeddable host and referer, so ensure_embeddable rejects this request before best reaches params.require(:embed_url). It also only checks non-success despite claiming a 404. Removing the required-parameter check would therefore leave this test green. Configure an allowed host/referer for this case and assert the intended missing-parameter response.

The URL and username prerequisite tests never enable feed polling (whose configured default is false) or supply the other required setting. execute consequently short-circuits at feed_polling_enabled? and never evaluates the prerequisite each test claims to cover. Both tests still pass if their corresponding presence checks are removed. Set all other prerequisites to valid values before making only the setting under test absent, so the poll_feed.never expectation actually detects removal of that guard.

Replace `end if` with `end`. The generated ERB Ruby contains an incomplete modifier conditional (`end if` with no condition), so compiling this template raises SyntaxError. Every embed request that finds an existing topic therefore fails instead of rendering the discussion.
outros: The header conditional ends with `end if`, leaving a modifier `if` without a condition in the generated Ruby template. Rendering any existing embedded topic fails with a template syntax error instead of displaying comments. Replace this tag with `<%- end %>`.

grupos.texto: The feed importer unconditionally reads `i.content.scrub`, although RSS entries commonly provide `description` or `content:encoded` instead of Atom `content`. Such an entry raises an exception and aborts the entire poll, including imports of subsequent entries. Select the available content field with fallbacks and handle entries with no body before calling scrub.
outros: Handle entries without `content`, including ordinary RSS entries that provide only `description`. Calling `i.content.scrub` on such an entry raises NoMethodError and aborts the entire polling run, preventing this and subsequent entries from importing. Select the appropriate available content field and handle entries with no body explicitly.

grupos.texto: Feed-provided HTML is persisted with raw_html cooking after only Nokogiri parsing and URL rewriting, which do not sanitize scripts or event-handler attributes. A malicious feed entry containing executable HTML is stored as post.cooked and executed under the forum origin when rendered, including through the new raw cooked embed view. Sanitize imported HTML with an explicit safe tag, attribute and URL-scheme allowlist before storing it or returning it from the raw_html cooking path.
outros: Sanitize imported HTML before assigning the raw_html cook method. PollFeed passes feed content directly to import, and absolutize_urls only parses HTML and rewrites URLs; it does not remove scripts, event handlers, or dangerous link schemes. Post.cook now returns this raw content unchanged, so external feed markup becomes executable HTML when cooked content is rendered. Preserve the normal sanitization boundary even when skipping Markdown rendering.

grupos.texto: Resolve relative href/src references with URI joining rather than handling only leading slashes. For an article at http://example.com/blog/article, href='next' and src='images/photo.jpg' remain relative and resolve against the forum instead of the imported article. Moreover, '//cdn.example.com/photo.jpg' is rewritten to 'http://example.com/cdn.example.com/photo.jpg'. Both yield incorrect links/images in imported posts; apply proper URI resolution to both anchors and images.
outros: The URL rewrite treats protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` as paths on the article host, producing `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`. Imported images and links using protocol-relative external URLs therefore point to the wrong server. Resolve both href and src using URI joining against the article URL, which also handles ordinary relative paths correctly.

grupos.texto: Update this test to expect Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: nil, embed_url: embed_url), rather than synchronous TopicRetriever construction and retrieval. EmbedController#best now only enqueues the job; those calls occur in Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute. Consequently these mock expectations are unsatisfied during the controller request under normal asynchronous execution, causing the new controller spec to fail. Test retriever construction separately at the job boundary.
outros: This test expects TopicRetriever.new and retrieve during the controller request, but EmbedController#best now only enqueues :retrieve_topic. Those synchronous expectations are not satisfied by the new implementation. Assert Jobs.enqueue with the expected embed_url/user_id here and test retriever invocation in the job test instead.

grupos.texto: `request.referer` is interpolated unescaped into an inline script string. A referer on the allowed host with a single quote in its path can break out of the string and run script (XSS). Build the target origin from the validated URI (scheme://host[:port]) and output it with `to_json`/`j`.

`open(url)` is called with a URL that comes from the embed_url request parameter and from RSS item links, and the scheme is never validated. With open-uri, Kernel#open can run commands for strings starting with `|` and can read local files. Validate that the scheme is http/https and use `URI.parse(url).open` or Net::HTTP.

Imported content is stored with cook_method raw_html, which skips the sanitizer, and best.html.erb outputs it with `raw post.cooked`. HTML from a feed or remote page is therefore served unsanitized (stored XSS). The `url` is also placed into an href unescaped. Sanitize the contents before saving.

`contents <<` mutates the caller's string in place. This raises FrozenError for frozen strings and appends the footer twice if the same string is imported again. Use `contents = contents + ...` instead.

`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring check, so any origin that appears inside the URL string, or an empty origin, passes. Compare `e.origin` for exact equality with the origin of discourseUrl.

The Disqus import now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote instead of PostCreator. This silently drops the `--category` option and the `created_at` from the Disqus thread, and the `--category` method_option was removed from the CLI. It also now makes a live HTTP fetch of every thread link, and `open(url)` raises on a failure that previously could not happen, aborting the whole import. Keep the category and date handling, and rescue fetch errors per thread.

The url is interpolated unescaped into `#{url}`. The post is stored with cook_method raw_html and rendered with `raw post.cooked`, so a url containing a quote or markup is output as live HTML. Escape it with ERB::Util.html_escape (or CGI.escapeHTML) for both the href and the link text.

`i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no content (only a description). The exception aborts the whole poll, so every item after it is never imported. Fall back to `i.content || i.description`, skip items with blank content, and rescue per item.

On the update path `embed.post` can be nil if the post was deleted. `PostRevisor.new(nil)` then raises NoMethodError, and every later import of that URL fails the same way. Guard against a nil post, for example by skipping the revision or recreating the topic.

The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' tests do not stub feed_polling_enabled? to true. It defaults to false, so poll_feed is never called whatever the other setting returns, and the tests pass even if those conditions are removed. Stub feed_polling_enabled? true and the other two settings valid, varying only the one under test.

The 'is 404 without an embed_url' test never sets embeddable_host, so ensure_embeddable rejects the request before params.require(:embed_url) runs. It passes without the embed_url check. Stub embeddable_host and the referer so the missing param is the only failure cause.

The 'not a url' test does not stub embeddable_host. The blank default never matches any host, so invalid_host? is true whether or not the InvalidURIError rescue works. Stub embeddable_host to a real host so only the malformed URL can cause the rejection.

absolutize_urls treats any href or src starting with '/' as root-relative. A protocol-relative URL like '//cdn.example.com/x.png' matches, has its leading slashes stripped, and becomes 'http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png', which is broken. Skip values starting with '//' (or resolve them against the scheme) before applying the prefix.
outros: absolutize_urls treats any href or src starting with '/' as site-relative and strips all leading slashes. Protocol-relative URLs like '//cdn.example.com/a.png' are rewritten to 'http://site/cdn.example.com/a.png', which is broken. Skip values starting with '//' (or prefix them with the scheme) and only rewrite single-slash paths.

grupos.texto: The referer/host comparison does not lowercase either side, so a mixed-case host is wrongly rejected. The reviewer notes this fails closed and is not a bypass. Normalize case on both sides of the host comparison (e.g. downcase both) to avoid false rejections. The same issue applies to topic_retriever.rb.

The host comparison does not lowercase either side, so a mixed-case host is wrongly rejected. This fails closed and is not a bypass. Normalize case on both sides of the comparison (e.g. downcase both) to avoid false rejections.

WHAT: Post#cook returns raw verbatim for cook_method raw_html, skipping the cooking/sanitization pipeline and plugin filters. WHY: any RSS/readability HTML imported via TopicEmbed is rendered unsanitized in embed/best.html.erb, executing attacker script in the Discourse origin.

WHAT: import_remote passes `doc.content` (and title) directly to import where `contents <<` assumes a String, with no nil check or network-error handling around `open(url).read`. WHY: unparseable pages (nil content) raise NoMethodError and dead URLs raise OpenURI errors, crashing RetrieveTopic/Disqus imports with no topic created.
WHAT: `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` result is used unguarded via `comments.appendChild`. WHY: pages including the script without the placeholder throw TypeError and abort embedding.

WHAT: Disqus import replaced PostCreator (title/raw/created_at/category) with `TopicEmbed.import_remote` per thread, dropping category_id, created_at, and strip handling. WHY: imported topics lose categories/timestamps and now require a live HTTP fetch per thread, failing when links are dead.

Race on check-then-create: two concurrent imports both see TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:url).first blank, both create Post + TopicEmbed.create!. Unique index on embed_url then raises RecordNotUnique (unhandled) or creates duplicates. Need atomic find-or-create / rescue unique violation.
Date uses strftime("%e %b %Y") hard-coding one locale's month names/order while neighbouring strings go through I18n.t. Use I18n.l with a locale date format so non-English users see localized dates.

The three 'requires ...' tests do not isolate the guard they name: each stubs only one setting to falsy while the other two remain falsy by default, so poll_feed is never called even if the named check were deleted. Stub the other two settings to truthy values in each test so removing the named guard would cause poll_feed to run and fail the test.

Migration defaults cook_method to 1 but Post.cook_methods is Enum(:regular,:raw_html) so 0=regular,1=raw_html. Default becomes raw_html, so Post#cook returns raw uncooked for all existing/new posts by default, bypassing sanitization. Change default to 0 (regular).

Spec expects TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve but EmbedController#best enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic,...) instead; the mock never matches so the test fails. Update the spec to expect the enqueue (or the job) to match the controller's async contract.

WHAT: TopicEmbed.import interpolates feed-controlled url unescaped into raw HTML (`#{url}`) and stores feed HTML as raw_html. WHY: url passing /^https?\:\/\// can still contain `'`, `>` or script, and RSS content is never sanitized, giving stored XSS when rendered via `raw post.cooked`. HOW: HTML-escape url and sanitize content instead of raw_html passthrough.
outros: TopicEmbed.import interpolates feed-controlled url unescaped into HTML link stored with cook_method raw_html (Post#cook returns raw, bypassing pipeline) and rendered with raw post.cooked: XSS via quote/script break-out. Escape url for text and attribute contexts before storing.

grupos.texto: WHAT: postMessage origin check is reversed (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)===-1`) instead of strict origin equality. WHY: any e.origin that is a substring of discourseUrl passes, letting a foreign iframe drive `iframe.height` handling and future message branches.
outros: Origin check is reversed: discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)===-1 tests if e.origin is substring of discourseUrl, so origins like 'https://' or '' pass. Should compare e.origin to the expected origin (e.g. e.origin !== expectedOrigin).

grupos.texto: WHAT: poll_feed calls `i.content.scrub` with no nil guard and no per-item rescue. WHY: feeds exposing only title/link/description (no content:encoded) raise NoMethodError on nil, aborting the whole hourly poll and skipping all remaining items.
outros: Unhandled nil content: i.content can be nil (RSS items using description, Atom id-only entries). i.content.scrub then raises NoMethodError, aborting the whole hourly poll. Guard/fallback to description/summary before calling TopicEmbed.import.

grupos.texto: Orphan-post crash on update path: post = embed.post can be nil if the post/topic was deleted, then PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! raises NoMethodError. Must handle missing post (recreate or skip) instead of assuming present.
outros: WHAT: update path uses `embed.post` without nil guard then `PostRevisor.new(post)`. WHY: if the first post was deleted, post is nil and revise! dereferences nil, crashing feed-poll updates instead of recreating/skipping.

grupos.texto: WHAT: parent.postMessage targetOrigin uses full `request.referer` (including path/query, possibly nil/attacker-controlled). WHY: targetOrigin must be an origin, so a full URL never matches and resize messages are dropped (nil referer throws), breaking auto-resize.
outros: postMessage targetOrigin uses request.referer (full URL with path) but receiver validates e.origin (scheme+host+port). Full URL never equals origin so resize message is blocked/mismatched. Send only the origin to agree with embed.js check.

grupos.texto: WHAT: poll_feed fetches and re-imports the entire feed hourly via `open(feed_url)` with `feed_key` never used for conditional GET. WHY: every hour downloads full feed and runs a DB transaction per item even when unchanged, causing O(N) network/DB blowup with large feeds.
outros: feed_key is computed but never read by execute/poll_feed; polling therefore never uses conditional-GET/throttle key and re-imports every hour. Wire feed_key into poll_feed or remove it.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.prTitle: Enhance embed URL handling and validation system

grupos.texto: WHAT: `expandable_first_post?` dropped the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` guard and now returns true whenever `embed_truncate?` and `has_topic_embed?` are true, with no check that any embeddable host is actually configured. WHY: a topic whose embed was created by a host that has since been deleted still gets its first post expanded, changing embed output for a state the previous guard blocked; the retained "is false if embeddable_host is blank" spec no longer exercises host presence (has_topic_embed? is unstubbed/false), so this regression is not caught. HOW: gate on the new source of truth, e.g. `EmbeddableHost.exists? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` if host presence is still required.

`where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases only the column, not the bound `host` value, and the model never downcases on save (before_validation only strips the scheme/path). Host matching is therefore not actually case-insensitive: a host stored as e.g. 'Example.com' (allowed by the /i format regex) will never be found by record_for_host/host_allowed?/invalid_host?. Lowercase the parameter too, e.g. `where("lower(host) = ?", host.downcase)`.

WHAT: The migration reads `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']`, but `execute(...)[0]` is nil when the inner join returns zero rows (the `embed_category` setting no longer exists in config/site_settings.yml, or its value matches no category name). WHY: `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError and aborts the entire migration, so `rake db:migrate` fails on any install where embed_category is missing/unmatched — and the intended `if category_id == 0` fallback on lines 14-16 is unreachable dead code because the crash occurs first. HOW: fetch the result, guard for emptiness before indexing, e.g. `result = execute(...); category_id = result.cmd_tuples > 0 ? result[0]['id'].to_i : 0`.
outros: `execute(...)[0]['id']` assumes the query returns at least one row. When no category matches the `embed_category` site setting (the exact case the `if category_id == 0` fallback on line 14 is written for), the PG::Result is empty, `[0]` is nil, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration instead of using the uncategorized fallback. Guard the lookup, e.g. `row = execute(...)[0]; category_id = row ? row['id'].to_i : 0` (and likewise for the uncategorized lookup on line 15), or move the nil check before the dereference.

grupos.texto: WHAT: `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally, so a record with a nil host raises NoMethodError (`nil.sub!`) instead of producing a normal format-invalid result. WHY: `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly; any request that omits the host value makes the save raise a 500 instead of returning the `render_json_error(host)` validation response. HOW: guard the mutation, e.g. `return if host.blank?` at the top of the before_validation block (or use `self.host = self.host.to_s` before stripping).
outros: before_validation calls self.host.sub!(...) on a possibly-nil host before validates_format_of runs. The controller assigns host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host], so a request without a host key leaves it nil and nil.sub! raises NoMethodError at save time instead of the format validation producing a normal error response. Add a presence guard so validation reports the failure.

grupos.texto: This example is named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" but its setup (`SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts = nil`, removed by this PR) is gone, and the code under test no longer consults embeddable hosts: `expandable_first_post?` is now `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. The body asserts only `expandable_first_post? == false`, which holds because `embed_truncate` defaults to false. The test therefore passes independently of the embeddable-host condition it names and would not fail if that behaviour were broken. Either assert the named condition (e.g. stub `has_topic_embed?` true and set `embed_truncate` true while ensuring no embeddable host / or rename the example to reflect what it now checks).
outros: The description "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer matches the code. This PR changed Topic#expandable_first_post? (app/models/topic.rb:869) to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`, removing the embeddable_hosts condition entirely, and removed the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` setup from this test. The assertion now passes only because `has_topic_embed?` is unstubbed (false) and embed_truncate is unset, so the name states a cause the method no longer has — rename it (e.g. "is false when there is no topic embed") or set up the precondition it claims to test.

grupos.texto: The migration inserts the legacy `embeddable_hosts` setting values raw, e.g. `http://discourse.org`, bypassing EmbeddableHost's `before_validation` that strips scheme/path. The lookup side (`EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`) parses the incoming URL to `uri.host` and matches `lower(host) = ?`, so migrated rows like `http://discourse.org` never match the query for `discourse.org` and `host_allowed?` returns false, silently breaking embedding for existing installs. Strip the scheme/path (as the model does) before/while inserting.
outros: The migration inserts the legacy `embeddable_hosts` setting value verbatim into `host` via raw SQL, bypassing the model's trimming of `http(s)://` prefixes and paths. The read path (`EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`) compares `uri.host` (scheme/path stripped) against that column, so migrated entries such as 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' will never match and embedding is silently disabled for those hosts. Normalize each value before inserting (strip scheme/path), matching the model's before_validation.

grupos.texto: `has_many :embeddable_hosts, serializer: EmbeddableHostSerializer, embed: :ids` emits only `embeddable_host_ids` in the show/update response and never sideloads the EmbeddableHost records. The admin client, however, consumes `embedding.embeddable_hosts` as full objects (store.js `_hydrateEmbedded` looks each id up via `_lookupSubType` and assigns the resolved records; `embedding.hbs` iterates them and `embeddable-host.hbs` reads `host.host`/`host.category`). With ids-only and no concurrent sideload, `_lookupSubType` resolves nothing, so the host table renders empty on first load of /admin/customize/embedding. Embed the objects (e.g. `embed: :ids, include: true`, or `embed: :objects`) so the payload carries the `embeddable_hosts` records the client now requires.
outros: `has_many :embeddable_hosts, ..., embed: :ids` without `include: true` emits only `embeddable_host_ids` and never sideloads the embedded objects, but the consumer `store._hydrateEmbedded` resolves those ids through `_lookupSubType`, which reads `root['embeddable_hosts']`. With the collection absent every id hydrates to `undefined`, so the admin embedding page shows no/blank hosts. Add `include: true` so the collection the store requires is actually serialized.

grupos.texto: update and destroy fetch the record with EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first but never check for nil, then immediately use it (save_host(host) does host.host = ... / host.save; destroy does host.destroy). A stale or already-deleted id, or an interleaving where a concurrent delete removes the row first, makes host nil and the first call on it raises NoMethodError -> unhandled 500. Guard with a nil/404 check before use.
The migration's INSERT statement uses string interpolation: VALUES ('#{h}', ...). This is a SQL-injection concern and should be fixed by using parameterized queries or proper escaping.
In the destroy action, the nil-host case (line 15-16) would raise NoMethodError. Consider adding a nil check to handle the case where the host is not found.

Update passes the nullable result of where(...).first directly to save_host, which immediately assigns host.host. Updating a nonexistent or concurrently deleted record returns an internal error instead of a not-found response; destroy has the same lookup failure. Use find or explicitly raise a not-found error before dereferencing the lookup result.

Normalize the parsed hostname before comparing it with lower(host). URI parsing preserves hostname case, so an allowed entry such as example.com does not match https://EXAMPLE.com/page even though DNS hostnames are case-insensitive. This makes valid embedding requests fail the host authorization check and makes category lookup inconsistent for equivalent domain identities. Compare against host.downcase (or normalize both operands equivalently), and add a mixed-case URL test.

The before_validation callback calls `sub!` on host without guarding nil. Creating a host with a missing or null host field reaches this callback from save_host and raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error. Guard nil during normalization and let presence/format validation reject it.

The test named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" now uses an ordinary built topic without setting embed_truncate or making has_topic_embed? true. It therefore returns false for reasons unrelated to the missing host, and passes even with the new implementation that never checks host availability. If blank-host behavior remains the intended contract, arrange all the other prerequisites before asserting false; if the contract intentionally changed, replace this case with a test of the actual intended behavior rather than retaining a misleading passing test.

This test now requests fruit 2 but expects fruit 1's two colors. The /fruits/:id Pretender handler always returns fruits[0], so the test passes while hydrating the wrong record and would not catch a find implementation that ignores the requested ID. Make the handler select the requested fruit and assert its ID and corresponding colors (fruit 2 has only color 3), or request fruit 1 if testing its two-color hydration is the goal.

The category lookup assumes the SELECT returns a row: `[0]['id']` raises when embed_category has never been configured or its category no longer exists. This happens before the `category_id == 0` fallback, so ordinary installations without an embedding setting cannot run this migration.
