A custom grant implementing the documented three-letter shortcut will issue token IDs that this decoder rejects, so encoding and decoding cannot round-trip for a conforming extension. Specify exactly two characters in this contract and enforce that constraint when registering shortcuts, or change the encoding format to support the documented variable length.
outros: Grant shortcuts are registered without enforcing the two-character length required by the decoder. A custom grant returning a three-character shortcut, which the new OAuth2GrantTypeFactory documentation explicitly suggests, produces a seven-character prefix that getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects, breaking encode/decode round trips for that grant. Validate shortcut length during registration and dynamic refresh, and document the required two-character format.

The new contract describes getShortcut() as usually returning a three-letter shortcut, but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider requires exactly two characters for the grant field (six total prefix characters, decoded with substring(4, 6)). An extension author following this documentation can produce token IDs that the default decoder rejects. Document the required two-character length rather than advertising three letters.

The new shortcut contract recommends three-letter shortcuts, but getTokenContextFromTokenId requires a six-character prefix and consumes exactly two grant characters. A custom grant following this contract produces a seven-character prefix that the decoder rejects. Specify exactly two characters and enforce that constraint when registering shortcuts, or change the encoding/decoding format to support the documented lengths.

Validate that every grant shortcut is exactly two characters before registering it. The new OAuth2GrantTypeFactory contract explicitly describes three-letter shortcuts, and encodeTokenId accepts them unchanged, but getTokenContextFromTokenId requires a six-character prefix and slices only two characters for the grant. A custom grant following that contract therefore produces tokens that this provider cannot decode (IllegalArgumentException). Apply the same validation to lazy registration.

grupos.texto: The rawTokenId null check validates grantType a second time instead of rawTokenId. A context constructed with a null raw ID is accepted and encodeTokenId serializes it as the literal 'null', violating the constructor's non-null invariant and losing the token identifier. Pass rawTokenId to this Objects.requireNonNull call.
outros: The check labelled 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' validates grantType a second time instead of rawTokenId. A null raw ID is accepted and encodeTokenId subsequently emits the literal suffix ':null'. Validate rawTokenId here to enforce the declared invariant.

The rawTokenId null validation checks grantType again. Passing a null rawTokenId therefore creates a context despite the declared non-null constraint, and encodeTokenId silently emits the literal suffix ':null'. Check rawTokenId here so invalid token IDs are rejected at construction.

grupos.texto: The condition `if (items[0].substring(...).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` is inverted. The matcher rejects ids whose grant matches and accepts ids with a different grant. Change it to `if (!...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

isAccessTokenId does not match the ID format produced by DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId. That format is 2 chars session type, 2 chars token type, then 2 chars grant shortcut, so the grant shortcut is at substring(4,6), not substring(3,5). The check is also inverted, because `equals(expected)` returns false on a match. Use `!items[0].substring(4,6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)` to return false on a mismatch; as written, a correct token ID makes the matcher fail.
outros: The matcher isAccessTokenId has an inverted condition and a wrong substring range. It returns false when items[0].substring(3, 5) equals the expected shortcut, and that slice overlaps the token-type chars. The grant shortcut is at indices 4..6. Every valid token id is therefore rejected, or an invalid one is accepted. Use: if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;

The matcher is inverted and reads the wrong characters. It returns false when the shortcut equals the expected one, and substring(3,5) misses the grant shortcut, which is at substring(4,6) in the id 'ssttgg:uuid'. Use `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

The comment says the grant shortcut starts at the 4th character, and substring(3,5) follows it. The token ID format is sessionType(2)+tokenType(2)+grant(2), so the shortcut is at indices 4-6, i.e. substring(4,6). Fix the offset and the comment so they match the encoded format.

isAccessTokenId never checks the grant type. It reads substring(3, 5) when the grant shortcut is at indices 4..6, and it returns false when the shortcut matches instead of when it differs. As written the check never rejects anything, so event assertions pass even with the wrong or an unknown grant shortcut. Use `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

The grant shortcut is extracted with substring(3,5), but the token id layout (2 chars session, 2 chars token type, 2 chars grant) puts it at indices 4-6. This compares the wrong characters, e.g. 'ta' instead of 'ac' for 'onrtac:...'. Use substring(4,6).

The matcher isAccessTokenId is wrong in two ways. The condition is inverted: `equals(expectedGrantShortcut)` returns false when the shortcut matches, so correct IDs are rejected. The substring is also off: the grant shortcut sits at indices 4..6, so use `items[0].substring(4, 6)`, not `substring(3, 5)`. Change the check to `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

grupos.texto: The second null check tests `grantType` again instead of `rawTokenId`, with the message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed'. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted, and encodeTokenId would then produce IDs ending in ':null'. Change line 73 to `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.
outros: The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed"), so grantType is checked twice and rawTokenId is never checked. A null rawTokenId is accepted and later encodes as '...:null' in the token id. Change the argument to rawTokenId.

The null check for rawTokenId actually tests grantType (copy-paste), so a null rawTokenId is accepted and the check for it never runs. Change it to Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed").

The check with message "Null rawTokenId not allowed" tests grantType, not rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId passes validation and the message is wrong. Change it to Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...).

grupos.texto: WHAT: grantType is snapshotted once from formParams in Context ctor but setFormParams() replaces formParams without refreshing it. WHY: Any caller mutating form params after construction leaves getGrantType() stale, so OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse stores the wrong GRANT_TYPE and encodes the wrong token-id prefix. HOW: Update grantType inside setFormParams or make getGrantType() derive from current formParams.
Off-by-one slice: items[0].substring(3,5) extracts indices 3-4 but grant shortcut is at indices 4-5 per encoder/decoder layout. For 'trltcc' it yields 'tc' not 'cc'. Use substring(4,6).
Inverted comparison: if (extracted.equals(expected)) return false rejects correct grants and accepts wrong ones. Negate to if (!extracted.equals(expected)) return false.
Javadoc disagrees with code: says shortcut is usually like 3-letters but all grant shortcuts added are 2 chars. Fix doc to 2-characters to match 6-char format.
Grant offset disagrees with encoder: encoder places grant at indices 4,6 of 6-char prefix but validator reads substring(3,5). Fix to substring(4,6) to match DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider layout.

WHAT: Constructor validates grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId (second check repeats Objects.requireNonNull(grantType,...) instead of rawTokenId). WHY: Null rawTokenId passes construction then encodeTokenId produces 'prefix:null' and decode returns corrupt rawId, causing lookup failures. HOW: Change second check to Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed").
outros: Duplicate null-check checks grantType twice (`requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId...")`) so null rawTokenId is never rejected. Change second check to requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...).

Constructor validates grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId: line 73 is Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of rawTokenId. This leaves AccessTokenContext in an invalid state with null rawTokenId, which later corrupts encodeTokenId (produces 'prefix:null') or causes NPE when rawTokenId is dereferenced.
Constructor error message disagrees with code: line 73 checks grantType again but message says Null rawTokenId not allowed. Should check rawTokenId so message is true.

grupos.texto: WHAT: isAccessTokenId matcher logic is inverted and slices wrong offset: returns false when shortcut equals expected and uses substring(3,5) instead of (4,6) for 6-char prefix on|rt|gt. WHY: Valid token IDs fail the assertion while wrong-grant IDs pass (given UUID suffix), so grant-type coverage is inverted and masks regressions. HOW: Negate the equals check and use items[0].substring(4,6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut).
outros: isAccessTokenId has inverted logic and wrong offset: `if(items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false` should be `if(!items[0].substring(4,6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false`. As written any prefix:uuid passes regardless of grant, so expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh etc pass even if grant encoding is broken.

Inverted result plus wrong slice: `if (items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false` rejects matches. Fix to `if (!items[0].substring(4,6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false` to agree with encoder layout session(0,2)+token(2,4)+grant(4,6).
Matcher name disagrees with code: isAccessTokenId returns false when substring equals expectedGrantShortcut. Inverted condition means expected grants never match.

grupos.texto: WHAT: New interface method getShortcut() has no default implementation. WHY: All existing third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations break at runtime/compile (AbstractMethodError) when upgrading, and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory blindly casts every OAuth2GrantType factory to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory. HOW: Provide a default e.g. default String getShortcut() { return getId(); } or handle missing shortcut.
outros: getShortcut() added as abstract required method breaks existing custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations (old contract had no such method). Make it a default method (e.g. default String getShortcut() { return "na"; } or return getId()) or handle null/missing shortcut in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory so legacy providers keep working.

goldens.comment: In AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth Objects.requireNonNull validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass validation.

In isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut and the equality check look inverted: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4,6)), and a match should return true (combined with UUID check), not false.

Javadoc mentions "usually like 3-letters shortcut" but some implementations use 2-letter shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "rt", "te", "pc", "ci", "ro"). Consider updating documentation to reflect actual usage pattern.
Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.

implement-access-token-context-encoding-.prTitle: Implement access token context encoding framework

grupos.texto: The reader Thread is started but never joined, so the assertion at line 157 can execute before the reader has completed a single groups() read (or while a read that would throw the NPE is still in flight). If the GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount null-model NullPointerException were reintroduced, this test could still pass because caughtExceptions is asserted empty before the racing reader thread has recorded anything. Capture the Thread, then join it (e.g. Thread reader = new Thread(...); reader.start(); ... deletions ...; deletedAll.set(true); reader.join();) before asserting so the test actually waits on the condition it verifies.
outros: WHAT: The reader thread started at line 139-149 is never joined before `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` runs. WHY: The reader can be mid-request when `deletedAll.set(true)` executes; if that request throws (e.g., reading a group deleted concurrently), the exception is appended to `caughtExceptions` AFTER the assertion has already evaluated, so the test can pass even when the NPE regression it targets is present (and is flaky). HOW: after `deletedAll.set(true)`, `thread.join(<timeout>)` (storing the Thread reference) before the assertion.
The test has a thread-join/race weakness.

grupos.texto: WHAT: The reader loop `while (!deletedAll.get())` has no termination guarantee and `deletedAll.set(true)` at line 155 only runs after the delete loop at 152-154 completes. WHY: If any `group(groupUuid).remove()` throws, `deletedAll` is never set, so the non-daemon thread loops forever and the test JVM hangs. HOW: set the thread as daemon and/or wrap deletion in try/finally so `deletedAll.set(true)` always executes.
outros: The test has a mid-loop abort hazard.

grupos.texto: getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when the cached delegate is gone (modelSupplier.get() == null), whereas before this change the method delegate-called getGroupModel().getSubGroupsCount(), which could not yield null (a missing delegate surfaced as an exception instead). The declared type Long is now genuinely nullable in a path that previously always produced a value or threw, so any caller that relies on the old contract — unboxing the result (e.g. `group.getSubGroupsCount() > 0`, `long n = group.getSubGroupsCount()`, or passing it to a primitive-typed parameter) — will now throw a NullPointerException instead of getting a value or the previous exception. Since consumers were not updated for the new nullable contract, either keep the non-null behavior for callers that cannot handle null or audit/update every caller of GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() to null-check before use.
outros: WHAT: `getSubGroupsCount()` now returns `null` when the delegate model is gone, violating the `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount()` contract whose javadoc (GroupModel.java:296) states 'Never returns null'. WHY: In-repo callers happen to tolerate a Long null, but any caller that unboxes the result (`long c = group.getSubGroupsCount()`) or does arithmetic on it will NPE, converting the old NPE into a different one. HOW: return a non-null sentinel such as `0L` (and assert the empty/absent case explicitly), or update the interface contract to document a nullable return.

getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when modelSupplier.get() is null, but the count is consumed as a number by brief-representation building; the sibling cache entity changed in this PR (CachedGroup) handles the same 'model unavailable' case by returning a non-null default (getRoleMappings returns Collections.emptySet(), and the subGroups/attributes loaders are built with non-null empty defaults). grupos.texto: The exception assertion runs without waiting for the reader thread to finish. Setting deletedAll only prevents a subsequent loop iteration; a request already in flight can throw and append to caughtExceptions after assertThat has passed. The reader can also first be scheduled after deletedAll is true and perform no reads at all. Thus this regression test can pass with the original concurrent-deletion null dereference restored. Retain the reader thread, coordinate its startup/read activity with deletion, and join it before asserting the collected failures.
outros: The test asserts caughtExceptions without waiting for the reader thread to finish its in-flight request. A concurrent read can fail and append its exception after the empty assertion has passed, allowing the regression test to pass despite the server error it is intended to detect. Keep a reference to the reader thread, signal it to stop, and join it before asserting the collected exceptions.

Wait for the reader thread to finish before asserting caughtExceptions is empty. Setting deletedAll only prevents another loop iteration; an already-running groups request can fail and append its exception after this assertion, causing the regression test to pass despite a concurrent-read error. Keep the thread reference and join it before inspecting the results.

Wait for the reader thread to finish before asserting caughtExceptions. A reader can enter the groups request before the final deletion, while the main thread completes deletion, sets deletedAll and asserts an empty list. If that in-flight request then fails, its exception is added after the assertion and the test incorrectly passes. Keep the Thread reference and join it before checking the results.

grupos.texto: The reader's stop flag is set only after every deletion succeeds, with no finally block. If any remove() throws, the test exits with a live non-daemon thread that keeps issuing requests and collecting exceptions indefinitely, interfering with teardown and potentially preventing JVM termination. Put stop signaling and reader termination in a finally block around deletion.
outros: Stop the reader in a finally block. If any remove() call throws, execution never reaches deletedAll.set(true), leaving the newly started non-daemon thread continuously issuing requests even after this test fails and the realm is cleaned up. Ensure the flag is set and the worker is awaited on the exceptional path as well.

grupos.texto: The reader thread is started but never synchronized with: the test does not wait for it to complete a read before deleting, and does not join it before asserting caughtExceptions is empty. The deletes can finish before the reader reads at all, or a failing read can land after the assertion, so the test passes even with the bug present. Use a CountDownLatch counted down after the reader's first successful read, start deleting only after it fires, and join the thread (after setting deletedAll) before asserting.

WHAT: getSubGroupsCount returns null when the group was concurrently deleted. WHY: Violates GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount contract documented as Never returns null and diverges from JPA impl which returns 0 count, so callers like GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount propagate null subGroupCount where non-null is expected (unboxing/NPE or wrong output). HOW: Return 0L (or cached empty count) instead of null when model == null.

WHAT: Reader thread is never joined and deletedAll flag is not set in finally before asserting caughtExceptions is empty. WHY: Assertion races with in-flight read requests (misses late NPEs/false pass) and if any delete throws the flag is never set leaving a tight Integer.MAX_VALUE polling loop spinning forever leaking a thread. HOW: Join the thread with timeout before asserting and set deletedAll in finally (with sleep/backoff in loop).
outros: Join the reader thread before asserting (keep Thread reference and join with timeout) instead of asserting immediately after deletedAll.set(true), otherwise exceptions from in-flight concurrent reads are missed and test passes even when the concurrent-delete behavior is broken.

Reader thread is started without join and assertion does not wait for it: store the Thread, join it (with timeout) after deletedAll.set(true) before asserting caughtExceptions is empty, otherwise the check races with an in-flight request and the thread leaks beyond the test.

goldens.comment: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.

For an administrator with global MANAGE but no VIEW, ClientsResource.getClients selects an unpaginated realm-wide client stream and evaluates authorization for clients before applying pagination, instead of fetching the requested database page. The expected ForbiddenException can come from getDefaultClientScopes(), before removeDefaultClientScope() is invoked. Do not short-circuit resource-specific view evaluation on the global fine-grained VIEW grant. With an all-clients VIEW permission allowing an administrator and a client-specific VIEW permission denying that administrator, canView() returns true here and the specific client permission is never evaluated. This differs from the specific-over-global override behavior exercised for users in this PR and exposes the denied client's representation. Keep the administrative-role bypass separate from fine-grained grants and evaluate the client's resource before falling back to the all-clients resource; also ensure the global view result used by client listing cannot bypass those overrides.
outros: The global VIEW check returns true before evaluating client-specific VIEW permissions, bypassing a negative permission on an individual client. An administrator granted VIEW on all clients can therefore read a client explicitly excluded by a client-specific denial; ClientsResource.getClients also bypasses per-client checks when this evaluator's parameterless canView() returns true. Evaluate the specific client resource before falling back to the all-clients permission, and ensure listing does not use a global grant to skip specific denials.

grupos.texto: hasPermission(String scope) looks up the all-clients resource with findByName and returns false when it is null. That call is not guaranteed to find the resource, because it is created lazily through getResourceTypeResource, which the sibling hasPermission(client, scope) uses. As a result, canView(), canManage() and canManageClientScopes() can wrongly deny access when the all-clients resource has not been created yet. Fix: obtain the resource through AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE), as the per-client variant does.

In V2, isPermissionsEnabled, resource and getPermissions now throw UnsupportedOperationException. ClientResource (around lines 710-720) calls these on permissions.clients() with no V2 guard, so the management-permissions endpoint would return a 500 instead of a clean response when V2 is active. Return a safe value (for example isPermissionsEnabled returning false) or guard the callers.

The listener is guarded only by the V1 flag ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ. When V2 is also enabled, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, so clients().setPermissionsEnabled(...) reaches ClientPermissionsV2 and throws UnsupportedOperationException. This aborts client deletion. Skip this cleanup when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, or make the guard V1-only (enabled and V2 disabled).

The Javadoc on void requireViewClientScopes() says it "Returns true if canViewClientScopes() returns true", but the method returns nothing. Change it to "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code false}."
outros: The Javadoc on void requireView() says it "Returns true if canView() returns true", but the method returns nothing. Change it to "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canView()} returns {@code false}."

grupos.texto: WHAT: hasPermission(ClientModel,String) accepts any returned Permission whose scopes contain the expected scope without checking permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId()), unlike UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission which filters by resource id. WHY: An evaluation result granting the scope on a different resource (other client or the all-clients resource when evaluating a per-client resource, or vice-versa) incorrectly authorizes the requested client — privilege escalation across clients. HOW: Filter results by resource id before matching scopes, as UserPermissionsV2 does.

WHAT: getClientsWithPermission iterates every Clients resource via findByType and calls hasGrantedPermission->evaluatePermission separately for each resource. WHY: Listing/filtering clients triggers O(N) full policy evaluations where N is the number of client authorization resources, causing material slowdown and DB/policy-store fanout on realms with many clients. HOW: Batch-evaluate once or query granted resources via a single evaluation / indexed permission lookup instead of per-resource evaluation.

WHAT: ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (and sibling V1 management methods) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AdminPermissions.registerListener still calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled on ClientRemovedEvent and MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now routes to this V2 impl. WHY: Any client removal with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled aborts the provider-event listener with an exception instead of cleaning up permissions, breaking delete flows. HOW: Make V2 setPermissionsEnabled a no-op or implement V2 cleanup, or guard the listener to skip V2 (V2 has no per-client permission objects to disable).
outros: ClientRemovedEvent handler calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled() but MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2 where setPermissionsEnabled() throws UnsupportedOperationException (Not supported in V2). Guard/skip this cleanup for V2 (no-op) so client removal does not fail.

setPermissionsEnabled (and isPermissionsEnabled/resource/getPermissions/manage/configure/view/mapRoles* siblings) unconditionally throw UnsupportedOperationException, but AdminPermissions ClientRemovedEvent handling still calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(). When routed via MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() this turns client deletion into an unhandled exception/rollback. Make V2 lifecycle methods no-ops (or return false/null) instead of throwing, or exempt the cleanup listener from the V2 path.

grupos.texto: Doc says 'Returns true if canViewClientScopes() returns true' but void requireViewClientScopes() returns nothing; should say 'Throws ForbiddenException if canViewClientScopes() returns false'.
outros: Doc says 'Returns true if canView() returns true' but void requireView() returns nothing; should say 'Throws ForbiddenException if canView() returns false' like other require* methods.

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.prTitle: Add Client resource type and scopes to authorization schema

grupos.texto: WHAT: `configuredFor` now returns true via the new clause `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)` even when the user has no password credential at all (only a passkey). WHY: this marks the password execution as configured/required for a passkey-only user, so the flow will execute PasswordForm and render a password page for a user who has no password; if the passkey fails or the browser does not support the conditional UI/passkey, the user is left on a form whose password step can never be satisfied (badPasswordHandler on an empty/absent password), potentially stranding re-authentication/authentication. HOW: keep the passkey clause only for selecting whether to render the passkey UI, and ensure the execution still short-circuits to success when the user is already authenticated via the passwordless credential (the existing `alreadyAuthenticatedUsingPasswordlessCredential` branch), or gate the clause so it does not make PasswordForm a required step for users lacking a password credential.

The new comment says webauthn data is set up "when passkeys enabled", but the guard `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` also requires that a known/already-selected user actually has a passkey credential. With realm passkeys enabled and a selected user without a passkey, `fillContextForm` is skipped (the test `passwordLogin_reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` relies on exactly this), so the comment misdescribes the condition it documents. Rephrase it to match the code, e.g. "setup webauthn data when conditional passkeys can be used (user unknown or user has a passkey)".

The change only widens visibility of the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH constant (a boolean auth-note flag name) and replaces an inlined re-auth form setup with a call to AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context). No password, token, or user identifier is written to a log or returned; the flag is a plain "true"/"false" auth note. No sensitive data exposure issue found. No line numbers were mentioned.

AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError reads the auth note (parseBoolean) and, when set, sets the USERNAME_HIDDEN and REGISTRATION_DISABLED form attributes. It only toggles UI rendering flags; it does not emit the note value or any credential into the response or logs. No sensitive data exposure issue found. No line numbers were mentioned.

The extracted isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() helper and the moved fillContextForm() calls only populate passkey conditional-UI data for the form. This is standard WebAuthn data (public credential options), not secrets, and is unchanged in kind from the pre-existing isPasskeysEnabled()/fillContextForm path. No sensitive data exposure issue found. No line numbers were mentioned.

The added calls only fill context form data / set the same re-auth error attributes. The error path continues to use the fixed "Invalid password." message (as asserted in tests) and does not leak which factor failed or any credential. No sensitive data exposure issue found. No line numbers were mentioned.

The new hidden authn_use_chk inputs emit ${authenticator.credentialId}. This was specifically considered for sensitive data exposure and concluded not to be an issue: the WebAuthn credential ID is a non-secret, public identifier that is already transmitted to the server as part of every WebAuthn assertion, is only emitted for the currently-selected user's own authenticators, and follows the existing pattern used by other WebAuthn login templates. It is not a private key, password, or session secret. No sensitive data exposure issue found. No line numbers were mentioned.

No issue found: the writer sets the auth note at line 102 using USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH and the reader in AuthenticatorUtils.java:126 reads the same constant/session/key; the refactor is behavior-preserving.
No issue found: setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError reads USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH using the same auth session and key string.
No issue found: the new public constant at line 58 keeps its exact value; changing visibility from protected to public does not alter the string.

No issue found: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled is a single definition reused by authenticate, challenge, and PasswordForm methods; call sites pass the expected currentUser argument and the null-safe guard matches intent.
No issue found: authenticate at line 115 uses the shared isConditionalPasskeysEnabled helper and passes context.getUser() as currentUser.
No issue found: challenge at line 137 uses the shared isConditionalPasskeysEnabled helper and passes context.getUser() as currentUser.
No issue found: authenticate at line 52 uses the shared isConditionalPasskeysEnabled helper and passes user as currentUser.
No issue found: configuredFor at line 63 uses the shared isConditionalPasskeysEnabled helper and passes user as currentUser.
No issue found: the action() if/else-if chain has no unreachable branch; authenticate() sets and removes the note symmetrically.
No issue found: the new block in authenticate is guarded by webauthnAuth != null inside the helper before webauthnAuth.fillContextForm is called, so there is no NPE or dead branch.
No issue found: formData, errorCase, and userAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth are each consumed; no computed-then-ignored pattern.
Unverifiable only: the authn_use_chk field name versus the JavaScript that must read it could not be checked; no mismatch is asserted.
所属文件夹的状态管理没有采用统一的状态管理，建议使用 ViewModel + StateFlow 管理 UI 状态。

PasswordForm.configuredFor now accepts passkey-only users even when the active login theme renders the unchanged base login-password.ftl, which contains no passkeys UI. The legacy keycloak theme inherits that template, so a user without a password reaches a password-only challenge with no way to authenticate instead of being able to use the newly accepted passkey credential. Add the passkeys import and conditionalUIData invocation to the base login-password.ftl as well as the keycloak.v2 override.

The comment 'set passwordless policy for discoverable keys' is stale. The updater now only calls setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE), so it disables passkeys for the realm. Change the comment to say that passkeys are disabled for the realm.

The password page now renders the selected user's passkey credential IDs (`authn_use_chk` hidden inputs) before the user has authenticated, since the user is only identified by a typed username. This tells an unauthenticated visitor whether the account has passkeys and discloses the credential IDs. Render the list only when the user is already authenticated, as in the re-authentication case. Otherwise leave it out and rely on discoverable credentials.

WHAT: New isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() per-user gate is applied to display (authenticate/challenge) but UsernamePasswordForm.action() still delegates to webauthnAuth.action() on global isPasskeysEnabled() plus presence of webauthn params without checking the fixed re-auth user owns a passkey. WHY: During re-authentication (context.getUser() fixed) an attacker/other user can POST a discoverable passkey assertion with a different userHandle and have it processed as re-auth for the fixed user, enabling user-substitution/bypass of the re-auth binding if the WebAuthn layer identifies the user from the assertion. HOW: Gate the webauthn branch in action() with isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) or explicitly verify the asserted user equals context.getUser() when USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH is set.

WHAT: PasswordForm.authenticate() reuses UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() whose null-user branch returns true when realm passkeys are enabled, but PasswordForm.requiresUser() is true and expects a resolved user. WHY: On a null/unresolved user (misconfigured flow, alternative execution ordering) it calls webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) without a user scope, producing a challenge/authenticators state inconsistent with the password template that now includes passkeys.ftl, causing wrong output or failed render instead of skipping passkeys. HOW: In PasswordForm use a user-required check (return false when getUser()==null or delegate only when user isConfiguredFor passkeys) rather than the null-tolerant username-form helper.

goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

grupos.texto: WHAT: The new getForLogin cache (keyed by realm+FetchMode via cacheKeyForLogin) is only invalidated from this provider's create/remove/update methods, but linking/unlinking an IDP to/from an organization is performed by InfinispanOrganizationProvider.addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider (model/infinispan/.../organization/InfinispanOrganizationProvider.java:249-270), which only calls registerOrganizationInvalidation(organization) and never registers cacheKeyForLogin invalidation. WHY: After an org-link mutation that does not itself route through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update(), the ORG_ONLY and ALL login caches keep returning the pre-mutation ID set, so the login page shows an IDP linked to (or no longer linked to) an organization until some unrelated update/create/remove happens to invalidate the key. HOW: Register cacheKeyForLogin invalidation for all FetchMode values from the organization provider's addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider (or ensure those paths delegate through the IDP storage provider's update so registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate runs).

getLoginPredicate now also filters on organization link plus the BROKER_PUBLIC config (line 254), but the enum's javadoc directly above (lines 215-217) still states that the enum "contains all fields that are considered when deciding if a provider should be available for login or not", presenting ENABLED/LINK_ONLY/HIDE_ON_LOGIN as the exhaustive criteria. Any reader — or a future LoginFilter constant added against that documented assumption — will believe organization link and BROKER_PUBLIC play no role. Update the javadoc to include the organization-link/public-broker condition, or move the condition into a documented LoginFilter constant.

getForLogin accumulates the login IDPs into `new HashSet<>()` and returns `identityProviders.stream()`. A HashSet provides no iteration-order guarantee, so the cached path returns the IDPs in arbitrary/hash order, unlike the delegate path and the non-cached branch which preserve the delegate's ordering. Any caller of getForLogin that does not re-sort now receives non-deterministic ordering for cached results (and it can differ between cache-hit and cache-miss). Preserve the delegate order (e.g. use a LinkedHashSet and iterate the cached ids in their stored order, or sort the result) so the cached and non-cached paths are consistent.

The new getForLogin override wraps results with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel on every non-cached path (lines 218 and 249) but the cache-hit loop adds the raw model returned by session.identityProviders().getById(id) directly. Any consumer that relies on the organization-aware model (as documented by the 're-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped' comment added in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean) therefore receives a different model shape whenever the list happens to be served from cache. Add .map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel) (or wrap before adding to the set) in this loop so the returned shape is identical on cache hit and cache miss.

The cleanup targets the wrong alias: `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` uses the literal "alias" instead of the provider that was just created ("idp-alias-" + i). No IDP named "alias" exists, so this registered cleanup (and the identical one at line 425 for "idp-alias-20") is a no-op/null-receiver reference and removes nothing — the 21 providers created by the test leak instead of being cleaned up. Build the reference from the actual alias, e.g. `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove)` and `get("idp-alias-20")::remove`.
outros: The cleanup registered here uses the literal alias "alias", but the provider just created has alias "idp-alias-" + i. The same mismatch is repeated at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". The cleanup can never find/remove the created providers (null dereference/404 on remove, or at best a silent no-op), so none of the 21 IDPs this test creates are cleaned up and the realm is left polluted for later tests. Use the actual alias, e.g. `testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove` and `get("idp-alias-20")::remove`.

grupos.texto: getLoginPredicate now declares an org-linked IDP to be a login IDP only when BROKER_PUBLIC is true (`idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`). This predicate is the sole gate for login-cache invalidation: create/remove call registerIDPLoginInvalidation(idp) and update calls registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(original, updated), both of which skip invalidating the `.idp.login.<FetchMode>` caches whenever the predicate says the IDP is not a login IDP. However, FetchMode.ALL/ORG_ONLY for a specific organization are the org's own login view and include the organization's linked IDPs regardless of BROKER_PUBLIC (BROKER_PUBLIC only controls the realm-level page). A non-public, org-linked IDP is therefore treated as non-login and its creation/removal/enable-disable/move-into-org does not invalidate the login caches, so those caches keep serving the stale set of IDPs for the org. The predicate's org/BROKER_PUBLIC condition needs to be scoped to the fetch modes it actually applies to (realm-level membership), or the invalidation must be driven by the full set of IDs each mode can return.
outros: The login-cache invalidation is gated exclusively by getLoginPredicate(), which (newly, server-spi IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254) treats an org-linked IDP as a login IDP only when BROKER_PUBLIC is true. But the cache this method guards, produced by getForLogin() (same file, lines 214-255), stores for ORG_ONLY/ALL the ids of the org's own IDPs (as used with a concrete organizationId in OrganizationCacheTest line 406), which can include org-linked non-public broker IDPs. For such an IDP, both original and updated fail the predicate, so registerIDPLoginInvalidation() and registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() skip invalidation (the latter via its early `!test(original) && !test(updated)` return), leaving the ORG_ONLY/ALL cache entries stale when the IDP's public/hideOnLogin flag is toggled or its org link is directly reassigned; getForLogin()'s null-id self-heal only catches deletions, not these membership changes. The invalidation must cover every IDP the login caches can contain, not only those matching the public-org predicate.

grupos.texto: The early return compares the original IDP's organization-aware enabled state rather than the persisted enabled state used to populate the login cache. If a cached public IDP's organization is disabled and an admin changes BROKER_PUBLIC to false, the original predicate is false because the organization is disabled and the updated predicate is false because the broker is private, so the stale ID remains cached; re-enabling the organization displays the now-private broker because the login bean only rechecks isEnabled. Compare raw persisted models for login-cache invalidation, for example by loading the original through idpDelegate.getById before applying this predicate.

Consume and assert the results of getForLogin, including a repeat query for the same mode/organization to exercise a cache hit. All calls in this test discard the returned stream and assert only IdentityProviderListQuery contents. The implementation populates that query before reconstructing the returned models, so returning an empty stream (or the wrong providers) at line 254 would still pass the entire test. Assert the expected provider identities on both the initial query and the cached query, rather than only the internal cached count.

Do not merge the previously read query into a newly revisioned entry without verifying its revision. A reader can obtain a query containing organization A's IDs, then another transaction disables a provider or changes its organization and invalidates this key. When the reader requests an uncached organization B, this branch obtains a fresh revision but copies the old A results into the new query and publishes it using the current counter. Subsequent A requests receive stale membership indefinitely (a disabled or moved provider still exists, so the null-ID fallback does not repair it). Rebuild rather than copy after invalidation, or ensure the old query's revision is still valid atomically before publishing the merged entry.

The cleanup callback removes the literal IDP alias "alias" instead of the newly created "idp-alias-" + i; the same mistake occurs for idp-alias-20 at line 425. TestCleanup.addCleanup suppresses the resulting deletion exceptions, leaving the created providers in the shared test realm and contaminating subsequent tests or repeated runs. Register cleanup with idpRep.getAlias(), or use getCleanup().addIdentityProviderAlias(idpRep.getAlias()), at both creation sites.
outros: The cleanup targets the literal alias "alias", but this loop creates providers named "idp-alias-" + i. Consequently cleanup attempts to remove a different/nonexistent provider and leaves the created providers behind, potentially failing teardown or contaminating subsequent tests. Capture each actual created alias for its cleanup callback. The same mismatch occurs for the separately created idp-alias-20 at line 425.

grupos.texto: The cleanup is registered for the literal alias "alias" rather than the IDP just created ("idp-alias-" + i). The 20 created IDPs are never removed, and the same applies to the cleanup at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". Use the actual alias, e.g. get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove, so the IDPs don't leak into other tests.

The cleanup registers `identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` inside the loop, and also for idp-alias-20. "alias" is a literal string rather than the actual IDP alias, so none of the created IDPs is ever cleaned up. Use the real alias (e.g. the loop's alias variable / "idp-alias-20") when registering the cleanup. As written, the 21 leaked providers can skew later tests that count IDPs or login caches.

WHAT: Login cache invalidations only fire from IdP create/update/remove, with no invalidation when an IdP is linked/unlinked to an organization via OrganizationProvider.addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider. WHY: getForLogin results depend on organizationId/BROKER_PUBLIC, so linking/unlinking leaves the cached ID sets in IdentityProviderListQuery stale and login pages show/hide the wrong brokers until eviction.

WHAT: getLoginPredicate() dereferences idp.getConfig().get(...) without null-checking getConfig(). WHY: A model with null config throws NPE inside the predicate used by create/remove/update invalidation and cached filtering, crashing the invalidation path.

WHAT: remove() stores idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) in storedIdp and calls registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp) when the alias key is invalid without a null check. WHY: Removing a non-existent alias causes null dereference on idp.getInternalId() instead of a clean false return.

WHAT: Cached getForLogin() resolves every cached internalId with an individual session.identityProviders().getById(id) call in a loop. WHY: Turns one login-broker listing (hot login path) into N per-ID lookups, O(N) growth with broker count with per-miss DB fallback and invalidation retry.

Test fixture never covers the new BROKER_PUBLIC branch: all org-linked IDPs are created public, so reverting the getLoginPredicate public-check leaves all counts unchanged and the test still passes. Add at least one org-linked non-public (BROKER_PUBLIC false/missing) enabled IDP and assert it is excluded from getForLogin counts.

Cache-hit path in getForLogin returns raw getById results without createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel applied on miss/fallback paths, changing the return-shape contract by cache state. Wrap hit-path results the same way before returning.

goldens.comment: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin() recursively calls session.identityProviders().getById() instead of idpDelegate.getById(), causing the cache lookup to re-enter the same caching layer.
Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.

grupos.texto: The new validation-failure warning logs `raw_report`, the full unvalidated report object supplied by the caller. This endpoint is public and unauthenticated (permission_classes = (), @csrf_exempt), so the payload is attacker-controlled, and browser report bodies routinely carry sensitive values (CSP blocked-uri/document-uri/script-sample, sourceFile, plus the full user_agent). Logging the raw payload on every validation failure writes potentially sensitive data into application logs; log only the report `type` (or a sanitized/redacted subset) instead of the entire raw object.

The 'preprod_artifact.api.assemble' analytics event is recorded before the feature-flag check at line 88 (and before any validation). When the organization lacks 'organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble' the endpoint returns 404 without assembling anything, but the assemble event has already been emitted, so this metric/analytics event over-counts requests that never performed the operation. Move the analytics.record call to after the feature check (once assembly is actually attempted/succeeds) so the event reflects the operation it names.

The number-type test's mock matches on `query.query === 'search-query'`, but the hook under test sends the search string as `substringMatch` (see traceItemAttributeValuesQueryKey in useGetTraceItemAttributeValues.tsx, and the correct predicate in the first test in this file). That mock can never be selected, so `expect(searchQueryMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` is satisfied regardless of whether the number-type short-circuit exists — the assertion no longer witnesses the behavior the test names. Fix the predicate to `query.substringMatch === 'search-query'` (and, better, assert the call did occur and returned [] to pin the guard).

WHAT: `zip(error_ids, events.values())` positionally pairs error ids with nodestore results, but `nodestore.backend.get_multi` does not preserve request order — it dedupes ids (`id_list = list(dict.fromkeys(id_list))` in base.py:184) and returns uncached items followed by cached ones (`items.update(cache_items)` at base.py:205), so `events.values()` order can differ from `error_ids`. WHY: when a replay's error set is partially nodestore-cached (or contains duplicate ids), each ErrorEvent gets the title/message/timestamp of a different error, producing a summary that attributes the wrong error text to the wrong id. HOW: map by node id instead of position, e.g. build `node_id -> event_id` and iterate `for node_id, data in events.items(): if data is not None: ErrorEvent(id=node_id_to_event_id[node_id], ...)`, or use `get_many`/per-id lookups to keep the id paired with its data.
outros: `zip(error_ids, events.values())` assumes nodestore `get_multi` returns a mapping whose `.values()` are in the same order as (and cover) the requested `node_ids`. If the backend reorders or omits missing keys, each `event_id` is paired with the wrong node's data, producing incorrect titles/messages/timestamps for errors; the new tests only use a single error id so they cannot catch the misalignment. Key the lookup by node id (e.g. `events.get(Event.generate_node_id(project_id, event_id=id))`) instead of relying on positional zip.

`zip(error_ids, events.values())` pairs each error id with the returned node data positionally, but `nodestore.backend.get_multi` is not guaranteed to return an entry for every requested node id (missing/expired nodes are commonly dropped from the result dict). When any node is absent, the two sequences are offset: every `ErrorEvent` after the missing one is built with an `id` that belongs to a different event and the trailing ids are silently dropped. Iterate over the mapping's items instead of zipping two separately-ordered sequences (e.g. build a node_id -> error_id mapping and use `events.items()`), so identity is preserved when a lookup misses.

grupos.texto: In the new feature-flagged branch, TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with hardcoded empty props: columns={[]} (an empty array, which is truthy for the `columns ?? fallback` logic, so no columns are derived) and tableData={data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}. All the real result data computed above (result.data, result.meta, fields, fieldAliases, eventView) is discarded, so any organization with 'use-table-widget-visualization' enabled gets an empty table instead of the query results. Pass the actual result data/columns into the visualization (or keep the old StyledSimpleTableChart) until the widget is properly wired.
outros: WHAT: the `use-table-widget-visualization` branch renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />`, hardcoding empty rows and no columns instead of the actual query result. WHY: when the feature flag is enabled for an org, every table widget renders an empty table and silently drops `result.data`/`result.meta`/`columns`, a functional regression for all dashboard table widgets. HOW: build `columns`/`tableData` from the existing `result` (and `widget.queries[i].fields`/`fieldAliases`) rather than the empty placeholder objects.

grupos.texto: The cross-spec mutual-exclusion checks use truthiness to decide whether the other field is present: `if self.initial_data.get("age")` and `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. Both fields accept falsy-but-valid integers (`age` has no min_value so `age: 0` is legal; `timestamp` has `min_value=0` so `timestamp: 0` is legal). When a report carries the falsy value, the guard is skipped, so a report containing both `age` and `timestamp` (or with the falsy value) is wrongly accepted instead of rejected. Use explicit key presence (`"age" in self.initial_data`, `"timestamp" in self.initial_data`).
outros: WHAT: `validate_timestamp`/`validate_age` test `self.initial_data.get('age')`/`.get('timestamp')` for truthiness rather than key presence, so a value of `0` is treated as absent. WHY: a report that contains both `timestamp` and `age` where the other field's value is `0` (e.g. `age: 0`) passes the mutual-exclusion check, accepting a report that violates both specs. HOW: check presence instead, e.g. `if 'age' in self.initial_data:` / `if 'timestamp' in self.initial_data:`.

grupos.texto: Zipping error_ids with events.values() assumes nodestore.get_multi preserves request order, but its implementation builds uncached results first and then merges cached results. A batch containing both cached and uncached nodes associates error details with the wrong event IDs. Iterate over zip(error_ids, node_ids) and retrieve each payload by its node ID.

The new Snuba replay lookup executes even when enable_error_context=false. Every opt-out summary request incurs an unnecessary database round trip and can now fail on Snuba availability even though it only needs recording storage. Evaluate the flag first and perform the replay lookup only when error context is enabled.

The mock for the number-type test matches `query.query === 'search-query'`, but `traceItemAttributeValuesQueryKey` sends the search as `substringMatch`. If the numeric early-return guard is removed, the hook will issue a request that does not match this mock, so `expect(searchQueryMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` still passes instead of detecting the forbidden request (and the test may fail only due to an unmatched-request error). Match `substringMatch`, as the string-type test does, so this test directly detects regression of the no-request behavior.

The new shared prop documentation claims the endpoint currently supports only LOGS, but this PR also uses these hooks with TraceItemDataset.SPANS (for example in TransactionNameSearchBar). Update this comment to describe both supported datasets; as written it incorrectly tells callers that a supported and actively used input is unsupported.

Do not attach the complete raw report to the validation warning. Browser reports contain page URLs (potentially including tokens or personal data in query strings) and arbitrary body contents. Any invalid field now causes that entire payload to be emitted at warning level, exposing it in operational logs even where the existing info-level request logging is filtered out. Log the failed field names/report type or a redacted diagnostic instead.

The feature-enabled branch ignores `result.data`, `result.meta`, and the computed fields and instead passes empty columns and empty data. TableWidgetVisualization consumes these props directly, so every dashboard table becomes empty for organizations with `use-table-widget-visualization`, even when the query returned rows. Pass the actual result and corresponding columns rather than placeholder arrays.
outros: The feature-enabled table branch passes empty columns, rows, and metadata instead of the query result. Organizations with use-table-widget-visualization enabled therefore see empty dashboard tables even when result.data contains rows. Pass the actual result data and metadata and derive columns from the selected widget fields.

grupos.texto: The removal of the instance `yAxes` field was not followed through to `static/app/views/explore/savedQueries/exploreParams.tsx:29`, which still computes `visualizes.flatMap(visualize => visualize.yAxes)`. Those accesses now produce undefined rather than the selected aggregate fields, breaking construction of saved Explore parameters. Update that consumer to map `yAxis` (while retaining arrays in the serialized contract).
outros: Replacing Visualize.yAxes with yAxis leaves consumers in savedQueries/exploreParams.tsx:29 and components/seerSearch.tsx:179 reading the removed property. Those consumers now obtain undefined instead of visualization fields, breaking the existing contract and potentially TypeScript compilation. Update those consumers to use yAxis or serialize through toJSON as appropriate.

`static/app/views/explore/components/seerSearch.tsx:179` still constructs its visualization payload with `yAxes: v.yAxes`. With instances now exposing only `yAxis`, that payload loses its aggregate selection instead of supplying the array the Seer consumer expects. Update this consumer to use `[v.yAxis]` or the serialized `toJSON()` representation.

grupos.texto: Include the organization slug in this query key. The new useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys implementation fetches `/organizations/${organization.slug}/trace-items/attributes/`, but makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions contains no organization identity. Two organizations with identical filters (particularly the default all-project selection) therefore share this cache entry. Switching organizations can display the previous organization's attribute names, and concurrently mounted consumers can reuse a request for the wrong organization. Preserve the organization-specific cache identity that the previous endpoint-based key provided.
outros: The new attribute query key omits the organization even though its query function fetches an organization-specific endpoint. Switching organizations with identical project selections such as all projects and the same date range reuses the singleton query client's prior organization's attribute metadata, including while the new request refetches. Include organization.slug or organization.id in the query key.

Include the organization slug or ID in this query key. The query function fetches `/organizations/${organization.slug}/trace-items/attributes/`, but the key contains only query options. Two organizations with the same project selection (especially the all-projects selection), date range and dataset therefore share a cache entry. Switching organizations can display the previous organization's attributes, and overlapping requests can populate the shared entry with the wrong organization's result.

Include the organization slug in this query key. The request function fetches attributes for the current organization, but the cache key only contains dataset/type, date range, and project selection. Switching organizations with the same filters (for example an all-projects selection) reuses the same cache entry and can display the previous organization's custom attribute names in the new organization's Explore UI. The previous endpoint-based key included the organization slug and isolated these results.

The new query key contains only filter options, whereas the query function requests an organization-specific URL. Two organizations with identical project/date/type selections now share one cache entry (especially with the all-projects selection), allowing cached attribute keys from the previous organization to appear in the next one. Include the organization slug in the query key, as the previous URL-based key did.

grupos.texto: Check key presence rather than truthiness when enforcing age/timestamp mutual exclusion. Both fields permit 0, so a report with age=0 and timestamp=0 passes both validators even though both fields are present; a zero-valued counterpart also bypasses the corresponding check. Use `"age" in self.initial_data` and `"timestamp" in self.initial_data` (or object-level validation) and add zero-value tests.
outros: The timestamp/age validators test truthiness and make both fields optional instead of enforcing exactly one field. Reports with both age=0 and timestamp=0, or with neither field, pass validation despite violating the stated mutually exclusive report formats. Enforce field presence and exclusivity in object-level validate using key membership rather than truthiness.

Check field presence rather than truthiness when enforcing timestamp/age exclusivity. A report containing both `timestamp: 0` and `age: 0` passes both validators, despite the declared constraint that they must not coexist; with only one zero value, validation is also asymmetric. Use membership checks on initial_data (or object-level validation) and add zero-value mixed-field tests.

These validators check truthiness rather than field presence. `age=0` is a valid report age and `timestamp=0` is explicitly allowed, so a report containing both fields with zero values passes both validators despite the mutually exclusive contract. Check whether the opposite key is present in initial_data (or enforce exclusivity in object-level validation), and add a both-zero test.

grupos.texto: The documented custom-renderer contract says fallback runs when the callback returns undefined, but `if (cell)` also falls back for valid ReactNode results such as `0`, an empty string, or `null`. A caller trying to render zero or deliberately suppress a cell instead gets the default field rendering. Check `cell !== undefined` here and in the head-cell renderer so the implementation honors the advertised contract.
outros: Use `cell !== undefined` instead of `if (cell)` to select the custom renderer result, and apply the same correction to the header renderer. The API documents undefined as the fallback sentinel, but valid ReactNode results such as numeric 0, an empty string, or null are falsy. A custom renderer returning 0 or intentionally hiding a cell with null therefore unexpectedly renders the default value instead.

grupos.texto: With the 'use-table-widget-visualization' feature enabled, TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with columns=[] and empty data/meta instead of result.data and result.meta. Every table widget therefore renders empty for orgs with the flag. Fix: pass tableData={{data: result.data, meta: result.meta}} and build columns from the fields.

The mutual-exclusion checks use truthiness (`self.initial_data.get("age")` and `.get("timestamp")`), so a legitimate value of 0 is treated as absent. A report with age=0 plus a timestamp, or timestamp=0 plus an age, passes validation despite violating the either/or rule. Use `"age" in self.initial_data` and `"timestamp" in self.initial_data` instead.

The number-type test's mock matcher checks `query.query === 'search-query'`, but the hook sends the search as `substringMatch`. The mock can never match, so `expect(searchQueryMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` passes even if the number short-circuit were removed. Match on `query.substringMatch` as the string-type test does, so the not-called assertion can actually fail.

The log extra 'event_data' now holds workflow_event_data, which wraps the full event object, instead of the ids-only EventRedisData. This writes event payloads that can contain user data (messages, tags, user and request context) to logs. Log only identifiers instead, such as event_id, group_id and workflow ids.

fetch_error_details pairs error_ids with events.values() via zip, but nodestore get_multi returns a dict keyed by node id that omits missing nodes. Any missing node shifts the pairing, so errors get wrong IDs and titles or are dropped from the AI summary logs. Fix: iterate error_ids, compute node_id = Event.generate_node_id(project_id, id), and look up events.get(node_id) for each.
outros: fetch_error_details zips error_ids with events.values(), but nodestore get_multi returns a dict keyed by node_id that omits missing nodes. The ids therefore misalign with the data whenever an event is missing or ordered differently. Iterate over zip(error_ids, node_ids) and look up events.get(node_id) so each id is paired with its own data.

zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes nodestore.get_multi returns values in the order of error_ids with no gaps. It returns a dict keyed by node id that omits missing nodes, so event ids get paired with the wrong event data. Iterate error_ids, look up events.get(Event.generate_node_id(project_id, id)) for each, and skip None.

fetch_error_details zips error_ids with events.values(), but nodestore get_multi returns a dict keyed by node_id that omits missing nodes and does not follow input order. If any event is missing or the order differs, ErrorEvent ids get paired with the wrong event data. Iterate over (event_id, node_id) pairs and look each node up with events.get(node_id) instead of zipping.

grupos.texto: It was not verified whether any caller passes Visualize instances (rather than BaseVisualize) to updateLocationWithAggregateFields. If one does, those instances would be stringified in a shape that the new isBaseVisualize reader rejects, so the values would be lost or ignored when read back. Check all callers of updateLocationWithAggregateFields and make sure they pass BaseVisualize objects, or convert Visualize instances via toJSON() first.

WHAT: update() reads validated_data.get("detector_type") but the field/validate_type stores it as "type", so type updates are silently ignored. WHY: PUT type change never applies, breaking caller assumption and diverging from create() which uses validated_data["type"]. HOW: read validated_data.get("type", instance.group_type).

WHAT: use-table-widget-visualization branch renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns/data/meta, discarding result.data/result.meta/fields. WHY: dashboards show empty tables when flag is on — wrong output/regression. HOW: pass through result data/meta and derived columns instead of empty literals.

WHAT: column fallback uses tableData?.meta.fields without guarding meta, so defined tableData with missing meta throws TypeError. WHY: crashes render on empty/error payloads instead of empty table. HOW: use tableData?.meta?.fields with fallback to [].

WHAT: analytics.record runs before the preprod-artifact-assemble feature check, logging assemble attempts even when disabled/unauthorized. WHY: inflates analytics, leaks usage signal, and does work before guard. HOW: move analytics.record after the feature check (or after validation).

WHAT: attributeKey (tag.key) is interpolated raw into /trace-items/attributes/${attributeKey}/values/ without encodeURIComponent. WHY: keys containing /, brackets or encoded chars break routing or allow path confusion/smuggling to unintended endpoints. HOW: encodeURIComponent(attributeKey).

WHAT: get_environment_info calls issue.get_recommended_event() per issue inside the merged-PR comment loop. WHY: N fetches (DB/Snuba/nodestore) per comment generation amplifies latency on the PR-comment path. HOW: batch/prefetch recommended events or skip environment lookup when unavailable.

WHAT: endpoint loops over unbounded raw_data array validating each report and metrics.incr per report with no size limit. WHY: attacker can POST huge arrays causing CPU/memory blowup and metric spam on unauthenticated endpoint. HOW: enforce max reports per request (e.g. reject >50) before validation.

WHAT: success path dereferences data.summary/numFeedbacksUsed without guarding data undefined (disabled/error-transition states). WHY: throws cannot-read-property crash when query is disabled or returns no data. HOW: guard (data?.summary ?? null) and handle undefined data.

`zip(error_ids, events.values())` assumes `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` values preserve input order and that all keys exist. Dict values give no such guarantee; missing keys shorten/misalign the zip, attaching the wrong event payload to the wrong error_id. Lookup per-id: iterate node_ids/error_ids and do `events.get(node_id)` instead of zipping with `.values()`.
outros: WHAT: fetch_error_details zips error_ids with events.values() instead of mapping by node_id, misaligning ids to payloads and dropping/mismatching on missing keys. WHY: assigns wrong title/message/timestamp to wrong error id and yields incorrect Seer logs. HOW: look up each node_id in the get_multi dict (e.g. dict keyed by node_id) and preserve error_ids order.

fetch_error_details pairs IDs to payloads with zip(error_ids, events.values()) where events is dict from nodestore get_multi. Values order need not match IDs and missing keys misalign, attaching wrong title/message to wrong error. Look up per node_id instead.

grupos.texto: validate_timestamp uses `if self.initial_data.get("age")` and validate_age uses `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")` to test presence. Both fail for falsy-but-valid 0 (timestamp allows 0, age can be 0). A report with timestamp set and age=0 (or vice-versa with timestamp=0) incorrectly passes mutual-exclusion validation. Use explicit existence: `"age" in self.initial_data` / `is not None`.
outros: WHAT: validate_timestamp/validate_age use truthiness (if initial_data.get("age")) so age=0/timestamp=0 bypass mutual-exclusion, and both-absent passes with no error. WHY: accepts invalid spec combinations and rejects/accepts wrong inputs (wrong 200 vs 422). HOW: test key presence ("age" in initial_data) instead of truthiness and require exactly one of age/timestamp.

grupos.texto: WHAT: get_condition_query_groups directly indexes dcg_to_slow_conditions[dcg.id] which KeyErrors if data_condition_groups contains an id absent from the precomputed map. WHY: crashes delayed-workflow task and blocks firing/retries. HOW: use .get(dcg.id, []) or ensure map covers all dcgs.
outros: WHAT: get_groups_to_fire directly indexes dcg_to_slow_conditions[dcg.id] with same missing-key risk as query-groups path. WHY: same task crash during evaluation when DCG sets drift. HOW: use .get with default and handle missing.

goldens.comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.
In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.

Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.

Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.

grupos.texto: WHAT: Splitting the single buffer into per-process SpansBuffer(shards) instances breaks the global 'spans.buffer.max-flush-segments' cap, because SpansBuffer.flush_segments computes max_segments_per_shard = ceil(max_flush_segments / len(self.assigned_shards)) using only the subset of shards given to that sub-buffer. WHY: The option is documented as 'Maximum number of segments to fetch and flush per cycle' (default 500), but with P flusher processes each sub-buffer gets max_flush_segments×(total_shards/P)/total_shards per shard and flushes up to max_flush_segments, so the aggregate cap becomes P×500 per cycle — multiplying memory loaded from Redis by the process count and also making any_shard_at_limit backpressure P× harder to trigger, exactly when the flusher is being scaled up. HOW: Either keep a single shared cap (e.g. compute num per shard from the total shard count, or pass the intended per-shard budget explicitly / divide by the total number of processes) so the per-cycle total is not multiplied by the number of flusher processes.

WHAT: `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard)` is newly added but has no caller anywhere (grep for `_create_process_for_shard(` finds only its definition); the restart path actually used is `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`. WHY: This is dead code that indicates the intended per-shard restart wiring was left incomplete — any future caller relying on restarting only the process owning a given shard will silently do nothing, and it is confusing which restart path is authoritative. HOW: Remove `_create_process_for_shard`, or wire it into `_ensure_processes_alive` if per-shard restart was intended.

The docstring says the flusher "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing," but the code at lines 60-66 shares shards across a capped number of processes (num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards)); each shard assigned via i % self.num_processes). With the new --flusher-processes default of 1, a single process handles every shard, so the documented contract is the opposite of the behaviour this PR introduces (confirmed by test_flusher_processes_limit, which asserts 4 shards served by 2 processes). Update the docstring to say shards are distributed across up to max_processes flusher processes.

The click option declares `default=1` for `flusher_processes`, but the consumer this feeds (SpanFlusher, via ProcessSpansStrategyFactory) is designed around `None` meaning "auto = one process per shard" (`self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`). Because the producer always passes 1, the `or` fallback never fires and the flusher is permanently capped at a single process for all shards, silently disabling the one-process-per-shard parallelism this PR introduces. The default should be `None` (or the flusher sentinel respected) so auto-scaling is actually reachable; as written the advertised behavior is dead in production.

`max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats a falsy value as 'not provided'. The new `--flusher-processes` click option is `type=int`, so a user can pass `0`; that legitimate-but-falsy value is discarded and the flusher silently spawns one process per shard instead of honoring the requested limit. Use an explicit None check, e.g. `self.max_processes = max_processes if max_processes is not None else len(buffer.assigned_shards)` (and validate/reject 0 upstream).

`flusher_processes` is not validated to be >= 1. `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` lets a negative value through (it is truthy), so `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` becomes negative and `range(self.num_processes)` is empty, leaving `process_to_shards_map` as `{}`. The following loop computes `process_index = i % self.num_processes`, which for any negative divisor is 0, so `self.process_to_shards_map[0].append(shard)` raises KeyError and the consumer fails to construct. Since `flusher_processes` is exposed as an int CLI option (`--flusher-processes`), a negative value is reachable from configuration. Guard with `max(1, self.num_processes)` / validate the input.

WHAT: The added synchronization point `time.sleep(0.1)` added after the second `step.poll()` is neutralized by the test's own `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` at line 15 (same `time` module), so it does not actually wait. WHY: The comment says it 'Give[s] flusher threads time to process after drift change', but the call is a no-op, so the test still races the background flusher thread before `step.join()` and is liable to be flaky / to not exercise the intended post-drift flush path. HOW: Use a non-monkeypatched wait (e.g. capture the real sleep before patching, or use the flusher's thread/process join, or poll until `messages` is non-empty with a real timeout).
outros: The added `time.sleep(0.1)` does not wait: line 15 of the same test does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, which replaces `sleep` on the global `time` module, so this call (and the flusher's own `time.sleep`) is a no-op. The comment 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change' is therefore false — the call returns instantly and provides no synchronisation, so the test does not actually wait for the flusher to process after the drift change. Either synchronise on a real condition (e.g. wait until the expected message is produced) or, if the original `time.sleep` is needed here, patch a module-scoped reference instead of the global `time.sleep`.

grupos.texto: The `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` timer is tagged with key `shards` while every sibling metric introduced/updated in the same method (`spans.buffer.flusher.produce`, `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes`) uses the singular key `shard`.
