grupos.texto: The comment/example line names a module path that does not exist: the example app lives at `packages/app-store/_example`, but the comment is written as `// example: import("./example"),` (the previous line referenced `"./_example"`). Because this comment is the copy-paste instruction for re-enabling the example app, uncommenting it verbatim fails to resolve `./example`. Point the path back at `./_example` so the prose matches the actual directory.

WHAT: The reschedule cancellation now runs in `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })`, but `forEach` does not await its async callback. WHY: The `await getCalendar(...)` and the subsequent `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`/`deleteMeeting(...)` become fire-and-forget promises; their rejections are unhandled, and in a serverless handler the response can be returned before the calendar/video deletions complete (now deferred by the dynamic import), so the external events may silently never be deleted. HOW: Replace the forEach+async callback with a sequential `for (const bookingRef of bookingRefsFiltered) { ... await ... }` loop (as done in handleCancelBooking.ts) or collect the promises and await Promise.all.
outros: WHAT: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` — an async callback is passed to forEach, which never awaits it. WHY: The surrounding try/catch can no longer catch failures: before this change getCalendar was synchronous so a throw was caught here, but now exceptions inside the async callback (including from the awaited getCalendar/deleteEvent) become an unhandled promise rejection, and the calendar event deletion may not complete before the flow returns. HOW: Use a `for (const bookingRef of bookingRefsFiltered) { ... await getCalendar(...); await calendar?.deleteEvent(...) }` loop so the awaits are observed and errors are caught.

WHAT: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` — async callbacks passed to forEach are not awaited. WHY: The `await getCalendar(...)` inside the async callback makes the delete fire-and-forget and turns any failure into an unhandled promise rejection that the surrounding try/catch cannot catch, so the calendar event may remain undeleted without any surfaced error. HOW: Convert to a `for...of` loop that awaits getCalendar and deleteEvent, matching the pattern used in handleCancelBooking.ts.

Changing forEach to `forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` makes the callback unawaited: forEach discards the returned Promise. The now-async getCalendar and the deleteEvent inside run fire-and-forget, so the surrounding handler continues before the calendar event is actually deleted, and any rejection (e.g. a failing dynamic import in getCalendar) becomes an unhandled promise rejection that escapes the enclosing try/catch — whereas the previous synchronous callback's throw was caught. Use a for...of loop with await (or Promise.all over a map) so deletions are awaited. Same defect is duplicated in packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts:125 and packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125.

The forEach callback was changed to `async` only to allow `await getCalendar(...)`, but Array.prototype.forEach does not await the callback's returned promise. The `calendar.deleteEvent(...)` call is now scheduled in a later microtask and is effectively fire-and-forget: the reschedule handler can finish/return before the event is deleted, and a rejection here becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Convert this to `for (const bookingRef of bookingRefsFiltered) { ... await ... }` as was done in handleCancelBooking.ts.

The callback passed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach` was made `async` so `await getCalendar(...)` compiles, but forEach ignores the returned promise. The calendar `deleteEvent`/video `deleteMeeting` calls that used to run synchronously inside the loop are now deferred and never awaited by the surrounding code, so the reschedule can complete before (or without) the deletion. Replace the `forEach(async ...)` with a `for...of` loop with `await`, matching handleCancelBooking.ts.

Same defect as the vital adapter: the `forEach` callback was made `async` purely to satisfy `await getCalendar(...)`, but forEach does not await it, so the `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` calls are fire-and-forget and can be dropped if the handler returns first. Use `for (const bookingRef of bookingRefsFiltered) { ... await ... }` instead.

`getCalendar` is now async, but here it is awaited inside `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => …)`. `forEach` ignores the callback's returned Promise, so the deletion is scheduled and the mutation returns without waiting (or ever guaranteeing it runs, errors are swallowed). The sibling hunk in handleCancelBooking.ts:477-483 was changed from exactly this pattern to a sequential `for (const credential of calendarCredentials) { await … }` precisely because forEach does not gate on the awaited call; this hunk assumes the opposite. Convert this to a `for…of` loop (or `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))`) so the awaited getCalendar/deleteEvent actually complete before the handler resolves.

Same disagreement: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { … const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })`. The awaited async getCalendar makes the callback return a Promise that forEach discards, so the calendar deletion is fire-and-forget and the reschedule can finish first. The corrected `for…of` form in handleCancelBooking.ts:477-483 shows the intent; use a sequential loop or `Promise.all(map(...))` here too.

Identical to the vital reschedule: `forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` — forEach does not await the async callback, so the newly-async getCalendar result is never awaited by the caller and the delete may not run before the function returns. Replace the forEach with a sequential for…of loop as done in handleCancelBooking.ts.

This hunk kept `forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); … calendar?.updateEvent(…) })` while the other hunk in the same file (lines 477-483) was rewritten to a sequential for…of for the same operation because forEach discards the async callback's Promise. With getCalendar now async, the awaited updateEvent calls are not waited on and the recurring-event updates may never complete before the handler returns; use the same for…of/await pattern.

grupos.texto: getCalendarCredentials still calls `const calendar = getCalendar(credential)` without awaiting it, but this PR changed getCalendar to be async (`Promise<Calendar | null>`). The `calendar` value placed into each returned `{ integration, credential, calendar }` object is now a Promise rather than a Calendar. Any consumer that assumes it is a Calendar breaks: a `!calendar` presence/null check always passes because a Promise is truthy (so a genuinely missing calendar is never detected), and any direct use (e.g. `calendar.listCalendars()`) fails. Add `await` and make getCalendarCredentials async (or resolve the promise before returning it) so the boundary value matches the type consumers expect.
outros: getCalendar is now async, but getCalendarCredentials is still synchronous and calls `getCalendar(credential)` without await, storing a Promise<Calendar|null> in the returned object's `calendar` field. Only getConnectedCalendars was adapted (await item.calendar); any other consumer of the exported getCalendarCredentials that uses `.calendar` as a Calendar will throw at its own call site (e.g. calendar.listCalendars is not a function). Make getCalendarCredentials async and await getCalendar, or promise-map the credentials.

getCalendarCredentials still calls the now-async getCalendar without awaiting and stores the unresolved value as `calendar` in its returned objects. This changed the shape of the exported function's return type from `{ calendar: Calendar | null }` to `{ calendar: Promise<Calendar | null> }`, but only one downstream consumer (getConnectedCalendars) was patched with `await item.calendar`; any other caller reading `.calendar` as a Calendar now silently receives a Promise. Make getCalendarCredentials async and `await getCalendar(credential)` (or resolve the calendar before building the returned object) so callers receive a Calendar|null as before.

grupos.texto: The new async forEach callback is not awaited. If getCalendar rejects (for example, the dynamically imported calendar module fails to load or its service constructor throws), the callback produces a rejected promise that forEach discards; the surrounding try/catch cannot catch it. Previously a synchronous getCalendar failure reached that catch. Await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) or use an awaited for...of loop so these failures remain handled and calendar cleanup completes before rescheduling continues. Apply the same fix to the equivalent changed loop in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts.
outros: The async forEach callback moves calendar factory exceptions outside the surrounding try/catch because forEach discards its returned promise. An invalid encrypted Exchange credential throws during CalendarService construction, now producing an unhandled rejection while Reschedule continues and returns success instead of logging the error; the identical regression occurs in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts. Await Promise.all over bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...) inside the try block, or use an awaited for...of loop, so factory and deletion failures reach the catch.

grupos.texto: Each `import("./app")` in the object literal runs when the module is first imported, so all apps still load eagerly and nothing is lazy. A module that fails to load also produces an unhandled rejection if nobody awaits that entry. Store thunks instead, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, and have callers do `await appStore[key]?.()`.

getCalendar now returns a Promise, so getCalendarCredentials returns items whose `calendar` field is a Promise<Calendar|null>, not a Calendar. Only getConnectedCalendars awaits it. Other consumers (apps/web/pages/api/availability/calendar.ts and trpc viewer.tsx) that use `.calendar` directly would call methods on a Promise. Make getCalendarCredentials async and await getCalendar, or update every consumer to await `.calendar`.

getCalendar is now async, but it is called inside `forEach(async ...)`, and forEach does not await the callbacks. The calendar deleteEvent calls are fire-and-forget: the handler can return before they finish, and their rejections escape the surrounding try/catch as unhandled rejections. Collect the promises with `map` and `await Promise.all(...)`, or use a `for...of` loop with await. The same pattern appears in vital/lib/reschedule.ts and wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts.
outros: `forEach(async ...)` makes each callback return a promise that nothing awaits. Calendar deletions can still be running after the handler continues, and a rejection from getCalendar or deleteEvent escapes the surrounding try/catch as an unhandled rejection. Replace it with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => {...}))`, or use a `for...of` loop with await. The same pattern appears in vital/lib/reschedule.ts and wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts.

The `forEach(async ...)` callback awaits getCalendar, but forEach ignores the returned promises. Calendar deletions are therefore not awaited, and any rejection escapes the surrounding try/catch as an unhandled rejection. The handler can return before the events are deleted. Replace it with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` or a `for...of` loop with await.

The forEach callback is now async and awaits getCalendar, so the enclosing try/catch no longer catches errors from it. A failed import or a rejected deleteEvent becomes an unhandled promise rejection, and the handler continues before the calendar deletions finish. Collect the promises with map and await them with Promise.all inside the try, or use a for...of loop with await.

The forEach callback is now async and awaits getCalendar, but forEach does not await it. The surrounding try/catch no longer catches errors from getCalendar or deleteEvent, and they become unhandled rejections. Calendar deletions can also still be running when the handler continues. Collect the promises and await them with Promise.all. The same pattern appears in vital/lib/reschedule.ts and wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts.

grupos.texto: WHAT: getVideoAdapters awaits each dynamic appStore import sequentially in for...of. WHY: availability/meeting paths now pay N sequential module-load round-trips per request instead of one parallel fan-out, adding latency on hot getAvailability/createMeeting calls with multiple credentials. HOW: collect promises then await Promise.all, e.g. Promise.all(withCredentials.map(...)).

WHAT: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) never awaits the async callbacks so calendar/video deletions are fire-and-forget. WHY: forEach discards returned promises, the outer flow sends reschedule email and continues before deleteEvent runs, and the surrounding try/catch cannot catch async rejections causing unhandled rejections and missed cancellations. HOW: replace forEach with for...of with await or await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)).
outros: WHAT: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) with await getCalendar inside is never awaited. WHY: the deleteEvent promise returned inside the callback goes nowhere, reschedule email is sent before old events are deleted and errors escape the try/catch as unhandled rejections. HOW: use await Promise.all(...map...) or sequential for...of.

WHAT: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) with await getCalendar inside is never awaited. WHY: same fire-and-forget as vital copy — deletions run in background, try/catch cannot catch them, leaving stale calendar events on reschedule. HOW: await Promise.all with map or for...of.

forEach(async ...) creates floating promises: await getCalendar defers calendar?.deleteEvent and rejections are unhandled while outer flow returns early. Use for...of with await or await Promise.all(map).
forEach(async ...) is fire-and-forget: await getCalendar defers deleteEvent and failures become unhandled rejections. Await via Promise.all or for...of.
forEach(async ...) is fire-and-forget: await getCalendar defers deleteEvent and errors escape try/catch as unhandled rejections. Use await Promise.all or for...of.

Callback was changed to `forEach(async ... await getCalendar ... return calendar?.deleteEvent ...)` but forEach does not await async callbacks, so deleteEvent promises are never awaited. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` or for-of to preserve deletion guarantees.
Same forEach-async gap: `forEach(async (bookingRef) => { await getCalendar ... return calendar?.deleteEvent })` never awaits deletions. Collect with Promise.all(map) or for-of with await.

grupos.texto: WHAT: credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { await getCalendar; apiDeletes.push(...) }) pushes to apiDeletes asynchronously after outer code consumes it. WHY: outer apiDeletes is awaited elsewhere while async callbacks have not yet pushed, so recurring-event deletions are lost/partial and errors are unobserved. HOW: replace with for...of with await or collect promises via map + await Promise.all.
outros: forEach(async ...) around await getCalendar leaves recurring-calendar deletes unawaited; failures unhandled and flow can finish before deletes run. Use for...of with await or collect and await Promise.all.

grupos.texto: WHAT: getCalendar changed to async Promise<Calendar|null> but packages/core/CalendarManager.ts getCalendarCredentials still does const calendar = getCalendar(credential) synchronously without await. WHY: every entry now stores a Promise instead of Calendar, so any consumer not patched to await item.calendar (e.g. callers in viewer.tsx/calendar.ts paths) sees a truthy Promise, breaks null checks and calls listCalendars/createEvent on wrong type. HOW: make getCalendarCredentials async and await getCalendar, updating its callers.
outros: getCalendar is now async but getCalendarCredentials still does `const calendar = getCalendar(credential)` without await in a sync function, so `calendar` is a Promise. Make getCalendarCredentials async and await getCalendar (update callers) so its contract again returns Calendar|null.

goldens.comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

async-import-of-the-appstore-packages-ca.prTitle: Async import of the appStore packages

grupos.texto: `Prisma` is imported as a value (line 9) but is no longer used anywhere in this file. This PR removed the only usages (`Prisma.BatchPayload` in the now-deleted `remindersToDelete` / `deleteReminderPromise` declarations), while the import was kept. WHY: the repo's ESLint `no-unused-vars` rule will fail CI/build for an unused import. HOW: remove `Prisma` from the import list (and keep `import type { PrismaPromise }` as a type-only import).

The new cancel loop performs a sequentially awaited SendGrid HTTP request (`await client.request(...)`) for each reminder returned by an unbounded `findMany` (no `take`), then deletes them. WHY: this is O(N) serial network round-trips per cron run; if many reminders are cancelled at once (e.g. a bulk event-type disable or booking cancellation wave) the cron handler can block for a long time on serial SendGrid latency. HOW: fan the independent SendGrid cancel requests out with `Promise.all`, and/or bound the query with `take` plus pagination, then batch the DB deletes.

The added comment says reminders are cancelled only when 'scheduled within the next hour', but the query uses `scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().add(1, 'hour').toISOString() }` with no lower bound, so it also matches reminders scheduled in the past. The comment overstates what the code does; either add the missing `gte` lower bound to make the stated window true, or reword the comment to describe the actual (open-ended, <= now+1h) selection.

The new cancellation loop calls `client.request(...)` but this module never imports or defines `client` (the diff only adds the Prisma/WorkflowReminder import; the SendGrid client lives inside emailReminderManager.ts and is not exported). This raises a ReferenceError on the first reminder. It is caught by the enclosing try/catch, so the failure is silent: no reminder is ever cancelled or deleted, and the same `cancelled: true` rows are re-fetched and re-failed on every cron run, leaving workflow reminders in an un-cancelled state. Either import/create the SendGrid client in this file or move this cancellation into a helper that has access to it.

This reschedule path calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true) while the equivalent reschedule path in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx calls the same function with the default immediateDelete (marking the reminder `cancelled` so the cron cancels+deletes). The two sites that must tear down a rescheduled booking's email reminders disagree: this one leaves the old reminder row in the DB (and the old booking is not deleted, so no cascade removes it), whereas the dashboard path cleans it up. Align the argument so both reschedule flows use the same cancellation semantics.

The `immediateDelete` branch cancels the email in SendGrid and then `return`s WITHOUT deleting the WorkflowReminder row or marking it `cancelled`. Callers that are not followed by a DB cascade (notably handleNewBooking.ts:968, where the old booking is only marked CANCELLED, not deleted) are left with a reminder row whose `scheduled` is still `true` and whose `referenceId` points at a now-cancelled SendGrid batch. WHY: the DB no longer reflects the actual SendGrid state, and stale `scheduled:true` rows linger until the cron's `scheduledDate <= now` deleteMany eventually clears them; this diverges from the function name/intent ('immediate delete') and from the non-immediate branch which at least flags the row. HOW: in the `immediateDelete` branch also delete the row (or set `cancelled: true` / `scheduled: false`) after the SendGrid cancel, so the DB state matches the cancelled send.
outros: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` no longer deletes in its default path: with no `immediateDelete` (the path used by handleCancelBooking.ts and the event-type-disabled branch in workflows.tsx) it only sets `cancelled = true` and leaves the row; and with `immediateDelete` it posts the provider 'cancel' and returns without removing the row either. The name now disagrees with the behavior a caller reads; rename it (e.g. to reflect cancelling/marking cancelled) or make the delete path actually delete, so the identifier matches what the function does.
The immediateDelete email path returns without deleting or marking the row, which is a concern outside the assigned defect classes and left to other reviewers.

The `immediateDelete` branch cancels the scheduled send and then `return`s without deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row or setting `cancelled: true`. Callers that pass `immediateDelete=true` (handleNewBooking.ts:968, workflows.tsx:214, workflows.tsx:521) expected the row to be removed, so it now lingers — and the new cron in scheduleEmailReminders.ts never reclaims it because it only queries `cancelled: true`. Delete the row (or mark it cancelled) in this branch too.

The branch gated by `immediateDelete` is the only path in this function that deletes nothing at all: it POSTs a cancel to Resend and returns without deleting the DB row and without setting `cancelled: true`. Callers that pass `immediateDelete = true` (e.g. handleNewBooking.ts:968 for a rescheduled booking) removed their own `workflowReminder.deleteMany`, and for a rescheduled (not deleted) booking there is no FK cascade to remove the row, so the WorkflowReminder is left behind with `scheduled=true` and `cancelled` unset — never picked up by the scheduleEmailReminders cleanup, which only selects `cancelled: true`. Either delete the row (or mark it cancelled) in the immediate branch, or drop the flag and let the deferred path handle it.

The `immediateDelete` branch cancels the SendGrid scheduled send and returns without deleting the workflowReminder row or marking it `cancelled: true`, unlike the sibling deleteScheduledSMSReminder (smsReminderManager.ts:177-190) which always deletes the row. Callers in other changed files that pass `immediateDelete=true` (notably handleNewBooking.ts:968 reschedule, where no workflow/step cascade removes the reminder) dropped their own `prisma.workflowReminder.delete`, so the row is left behind; the cron cleanup in scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44-51 only selects rows with `cancelled: true`, so nothing ever removes or cancels it. Delete the row (or set cancelled: true) in this branch.

grupos.texto: The explicit `await Promise.all(remindersToDelete)` (which awaited `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` for every reminder) was removed, but the replacement `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` calls are not awaited. The DB cancellation/deletion now happens inside those floating promises, so the reschedule request proceeds (and on serverless the function may terminate) before the old reminders are actually cancelled/deleted, and any failure is swallowed by the managers' try/catch. Await the returned promises (e.g. collect them and `await Promise.all(...)`).
outros: Same lost guarantee: the `remindersToDelete` Prisma promises were removed from `prismaPromises`/`Promise.all`, so the DB deletion of workflow reminders now lives inside the un-awaited `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` calls. Nothing awaits those promises, so cancellation of cancelled bookings' reminders is no longer guaranteed to complete before the handler returns, and errors are silently swallowed.

grupos.texto: The isSenderIdNeeded branch removal is a concern outside the assigned defect classes and left to other reviewers.

Deferred cancellation includes reminders less than ten minutes from their scheduled send time, when SendGrid no longer permits cancellation. A booking cancelled in that interval is only marked cancelled locally by deleteScheduledEmailReminder, and the cron's POST is rejected, so its email is still delivered. Process cancellation before SendGrid's ten-minute cutoff and explicitly handle cancellations that arrive after that deadline rather than relying on this cron query to stop delivery.

Handle cancellation failures per reminder rather than around the entire batch. If one SendGrid request rejects (for example, for an expired or invalid batch ID), the loop exits before cancelling the remaining reminders, and Promise.all is never reached, so even earlier successfully cancelled reminders remain in the database. The failed record stays eligible for the next run and can repeatedly block other cancellations until their emails are sent. Execute each successful deletion and isolate failures so the worker continues processing the remaining reminders.
outros: Successful cancellation records are only deleted after every SendGrid request in the loop succeeds. If a later request fails, the catch skips all queued Prisma deletions; the next run retries an already-cancelled batch, which SendGrid rejects with 400, and aborts before processing the remaining reminders. Await each reminder's database deletion immediately after its successful cancellation and isolate errors per reminder so one failed batch does not block the others.

grupos.texto: Await the reminder-manager calls as part of the cancellation work (for example, collect their promises and include them in Promise.all). Both changed helpers now perform the database cleanup themselves: email reminders are marked cancelled and SMS/unscheduled reminders are deleted asynchronously. This loop discards those promises, and the previously awaited reminder deletion promises have been removed. The handler can therefore finish before cancellation is persisted; in a serverless deployment that suspends execution after the response, cancelled bookings can retain active reminders. Apply the same awaited-call contract to the other callers that removed their awaited database cleanup.
outros: Cancellation now delegates the database update/deletion to asynchronous reminder helpers without awaiting them, while removing reminder deletes from the awaited promise list. The handler can finish before cancelled flags or unscheduled-reminder deletions are persisted, allowing a subsequent scheduler run to schedule a cancelled booking's reminder and leaving cancellation work unfinished when a serverless invocation terminates. Collect and await the helper promises; apply the same correction to the modified rescheduling and workflow-update callers that discard these promises.

Await the reminder cancellation promises before completing the cancellation request. These helpers now own persistence of cancellation: email awaits a workflowReminder update and SMS awaits Twilio before deleting the row. The forEach discards their promises, and removing remindersToDelete from the awaited promise list removes the previous guarantee that reminder state is cleared before the handler returns. In a serverless request the outstanding operations can be interrupted after the response, leaving reminders active for a cancelled booking. Collect these helper promises and include them in the awaited Promise.all.

Await the reminder cancellation helpers as part of the handler's Promise.all. Previously this handler awaited deletion of every workflowReminder through remindersToDelete; now the only database deletion/marking occurs inside these async helpers, but their promises are discarded by forEach. The request can complete before email reminders are marked cancelled (or SMS/unscheduled reminders are deleted), and a serverless invocation can stop before that cleanup completes, leaving reminders active for a cancelled booking. Collect the helper promises and include them in the awaited work instead of removing the awaited cleanup altogether.

grupos.texto: twilio.cancelSMS and prisma.workflowReminder.delete share one try block. If the Twilio cancel throws, the DB row is never deleted. The reminder row then stays behind for a booking that was cancelled, rescheduled or deleted, because the callers no longer delete rows themselves. Delete the row in a finally block, or handle the cancel failure separately so the delete still runs.

`deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and its `immediateDelete` flag no longer match what the code does. The default path only marks the reminder `cancelled: true`, and the `immediateDelete` path only sends a cancel request to the email provider. Neither path deletes the scheduled send or the row, unlike the SMS counterpart, which still deletes. Rename them (for example `cancelScheduledEmailReminder` and `immediateCancel`) or document the behaviour.

The `immediateDelete` branch is named and called as a delete, but it only posts a cancel to SendGrid and returns. The `WorkflowReminder` row is never deleted, and the old scheduled_sends DELETE call is gone. After the cancel request succeeds, delete the reminder row with `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId } })`.

A single try/catch wraps the whole loop of SendGrid cancel requests. One failed request jumps to the catch block, so the remaining reminders are never cancelled and the queued Prisma deletes never run. Those reminders stay `cancelled: true` and are retried every run, and one persistently failing reminder blocks all later ones. Move the try/catch inside the loop so each reminder is handled on its own, and delete each reminder's row right after its own cancel request succeeds.
outros: One failing SendGrid cancel request aborts the whole loop through the shared try/catch. Prisma deletes are lazy and only run at `Promise.all` after the loop, so reminders processed before the failure are never deleted either. The failing row stays `cancelled:true` and fails again on every cron run, which blocks all later cancellations. Wrap each reminder's request and delete in its own try/catch, and await the delete inside the loop.

grupos.texto: WHAT: remindersToCancel loop awaits SendGrid cancel per-reminder inside one try and only runs Prisma deletes after the loop, with no method filter. WHY: a single throw (e.g. null SMS referenceId sent as batch_id, or one SendGrid error) aborts the loop and skips Promise.all deletes, leaving all other cancelled emails still scheduled so they are still sent.

WHAT: unscheduledReminders query does not exclude cancelled:true reminders. WHY: email reminders marked cancelled:true by deleteScheduledEmailReminder (scheduled=false, future date) still match and get scheduled to SendGrid, so cancelled/rescheduled bookings still receive emails.

WHAT: async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder called inside forEach without collecting/awaiting promises. WHY: handler returns before cancels complete and rejections are unobserved, so cancellations are lost and reminder emails/SMS are still sent (same fire-and-forget pattern repeated in handleNewBooking:966, bookings.tsx:488, workflows.tsx:212/376/519/574).

WHAT: edited/disabled event-type path replaced immediate prisma deleteMany with mark-cancelled-only for EMAIL (deleteScheduledEmailReminder without immediateDelete). WHY: far-future scheduled SendGrid sends stay active until the 1-hour cron window, so edited workflows still send old reminders; combined with missing cancelled filter they can be re-scheduled.

WHAT: SendGrid cancel issued with sequential await inside for loop over remindersToCancel. WHY: cron blocks O(N) sequential network round-trips instead of parallel batch, materially slowing the hourly schedule job as cancelled backlog grows.
Hard-coded placeholder "Verification code" bypasses i18n while surrounding strings use t(). Use translation key e.g. t("verification_code").
Hard-coded button label "Verify" bypasses i18n while surrounding strings use t(). Use translation key e.g. t("verify").

immediateDelete branch cancels the SendGrid scheduled send but returns without deleting the workflowReminder row or setting cancelled:true, disagreeing with deleteScheduledSMSReminder (which deletes) and with the cancelled:true sweeper in scheduleEmailReminders. A reminder cancelled via immediateDelete=true (e.g. handleNewBooking reschedule) leaks a live DB row. Delete the row (or set cancelled) in the immediate path.
outros: WHAT: immediateDelete branch cancels SendGrid then returns without deleting the prisma workflowReminder row. WHY: reschedule/workflow-delete callers leave stale scheduled rows that are never cleaned except by past-date sweep, causing DB bloat and risk of re-processing.

immediateDelete branch cancels SendGrid then returns without deleting or marking the WorkflowReminder row, orphaning the old rescheduled booking's reminder while the SMS path deletes. Delete or mark cancelled before returning.

goldens.comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

comprehensive-workflow-reminder-manageme.prTitle: Comprehensive workflow reminder management for booking lifecycle events

grupos.texto: WHAT: `deleteCacheMutation`'s `onSuccess` only calls `onSuccess?.()` and never invalidates the `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` query, while the sibling `disconnectMutation` explicitly invalidates it in `onSettled`. WHY: the 'Cache Status' row in the dropdown is rendered from the cached `connectedCalendars` result; after deleting the cache the query is not refetched, so the deleted status/last-updated entry stays visible and stale in the UI. HOW: invalidate the query in the cache-deletion mutation as well, e.g. `const utils = trpc.useUtils(); onSuccess: async () => { ...; await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate(); }`.

WHAT: `sed -i '' -E 's|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|...|' "$ENV_FILE"` uses the BSD/macOS `sed -i ''` form. WHY: under GNU sed (typical Linux dev/CI environment) the empty `''` is consumed as the script operand and the command errors, so the existing `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` line is never replaced and the tunnel URL is not written to the env file. HOW: use a portable invocation, e.g. `sed -i.bak -E "s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=$TUNNEL_URL|" "$ENV_FILE"` (or branch on `uname`).

cleanup() always ends in `exit 0`, and both failure paths (rate-limit at lines 46-50 and 'Failed to extract Tunnelmole URL' at lines 56-59) call cleanup. So a script named test-gcal-webhooks that did not actually obtain the tunnel URL / update GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL still exits with status 0, letting any automation treat the run as successful even though the setup it verifies failed. On the failure branches the script should exit non-zero (e.g. `exit 1`) so failure is observable; only the SIGINT/SIGTERM interactive shutdown should exit 0.

The 'Last updated' timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded "en-US" locale (new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)), so every user — regardless of their locale — sees a US-style date/time while the surrounding label is translated. Use the app's locale-aware date formatting helper (the user's current locale) instead of pinning en-US.

Write site and read site disagree on which table carries the cache timestamp. This line bumps `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, but the `cacheUpdatedAt` shown in CredentialActionsDropdown is produced by `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` (connectedCalendars.handler.ts:27-35), which reads `CalendarCache.updatedAt`. Whatever this call sets will never be the value displayed as "Last updated", so the two sides of the feature are inconsistent.

WHAT: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty `data` object, but `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is a Prisma `@updatedAt` field that only updates when the write changes at least one field. WHY: Prisma treats `data: {}` as a no-op (it is accepted syntactically but performs no field change), so the stated intent — 'Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for all calendars under this credential' — never happens and the calendars' timestamps stay stale. HOW: pass an explicit field, e.g. `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, { updatedAt: new Date() })` (or set a real business column), so the timestamp is actually refreshed.
outros: The comment states this call updates SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for the credential's calendars, but the data argument is an empty object `{}`. Prisma's updateMany with empty data does not touch the @updatedAt column, so the field the comment (and the cache-status UI) relies on is never refreshed. The method name/comment therefore disagree with what the code does; pass a real mutation (or document/implement the intended timestamp bump).

The new call passes an empty data object to `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})`. Because `data` contains no field, Prisma writes no column for the rows and the `@updatedAt` timestamp is not refreshed, so the operation declared by the comment ("Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt") does not actually happen — the line is effectively a no-op. Pass a field that genuinely changes (e.g. `{ updatedAt: new Date() }`) or remove the call if it is not meant to write.

`SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an EMPTY update payload. Prisma's `updateMany` is driven by the fields present in `data`; with no fields specified the intended refresh of `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is not guaranteed to be written (the statement degenerates to a no-op / count-only query), so the cache-invalidation this line is meant to trigger silently never happens. If the intent is to bump the timestamp, it must be set explicitly, e.g. `{ updatedAt: new Date() }`, rather than relying on an empty-data side effect.

grupos.texto: Successful cache deletion does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt. The wrapper forwards only an optional parent onChanged callback and disables window-focus refetch, so the deleted cache continues to appear present with its old timestamp and delete action. Invalidate utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars on successful deletion.

The cache timestamp is always formatted with "en-US", even though the surrounding label uses the user's selected translation locale. Users in other locales therefore see US month/day ordering and time conventions inside an otherwise localized message, potentially misreading the last-update date. Use the active application locale for Intl.DateTimeFormat instead of hard-coding en-US.

This warning says updatedAt is added without a default and cannot be added to a nonempty table, but the migration actually supplies DEFAULT NOW(), explicitly handling existing rows. Remove or correct the warning so operators reviewing the migration are not incorrectly told that existing data makes it unsafe to run.

The new call does not actually refresh SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. updateManyByCredentialId in the other changed file forwards `data` unchanged to Prisma, and Prisma does not advance an @updatedAt field when the update data is empty. Consequently successful availability refreshes leave the selected-calendar timestamps unchanged despite this call's stated purpose. Pass an explicit timestamp, e.g. `{ updatedAt: new Date() }`, or make the repository method explicitly perform the timestamp update.
outros: The new timestamp update passes an empty data object to Prisma updateMany, which does not advance @updatedAt. SelectedCalendar.updatedAt therefore remains unchanged after cache repopulation instead of recording the refresh as this new side effect intends. Pass { updatedAt: new Date() } explicitly.

The empty update object does not update Prisma's @updatedAt field (empty updates leave it unchanged), so this call does not perform the timestamp refresh described by the comment. Pass an explicit updatedAt value if successful cache refreshes are intended to advance SelectedCalendar.updatedAt.

grupos.texto: The environment update uses BSD sed's `-i ''` syntax, which fails with GNU sed on Linux. When GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, the script leaves the previous URL unchanged but still prints that it was updated, preventing webhooks from reaching the new tunnel. Use a portable replacement strategy or select the in-place syntax based on the available sed implementation and check its exit status.
outros: When GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, `sed -i ''` uses BSD/macOS syntax and fails under GNU sed on Linux. The script nevertheless prints that the URL was updated and keeps the tunnel running, leaving webhooks configured with the old URL. Use a portable replacement approach (or select the appropriate sed syntax) and only announce success after the edit succeeds.

grupos.texto: `updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {})` passes an empty data object, and Prisma may not set `@updatedAt` when no fields are written. The SelectedCalendar.updatedAt timestamp may then never change, so the intended cache-refresh marker is not recorded. Set an explicit field in the data, for example `{ updatedAt: new Date() }`.

`sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU sed (Linux) it treats '' as the script and fails, so GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never updated. Use a portable form such as `sed -i.bak -E ... && rm -f "$ENV_FILE.bak"`.

The cache 'last updated' timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded "en-US" locale, so users in other languages see US-style dates inside an otherwise translated string. Use the user's locale instead, for example `i18n.language` from useLocale, or pass `undefined`.

`cleanup` always runs `exit 0`, and it is also called on the failure paths (rate limit hit, failed to extract the URL). The script therefore reports success even though the tunnel failed and GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL was never updated. Have `cleanup` take an exit code, and pass 1 from the failure paths.

WHAT: deleteCacheMutation onSuccess only calls onSuccess?.() and never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, unlike disconnectMutation onSettled. WHY: cacheUpdatedAt stays stale after deletion so UI keeps showing old Last updated and delete action until manual refetch. HOW: add onSettled invalidate of connectedCalendars like disconnect does.

WHAT: sed -i '' -E uses BSD/macOS in-place syntax. WHY: on GNU/Linux sed -i '' treats '' as a file argument and fails, so GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never updated on Linux/CI. HOW: branch on OS or use portable sed -i.bak / sed -i without arg.

Date format hard-coded to "en-US" via Intl.DateTimeFormat while surrounding strings use t()/useLocale. Users in other locales see US short date/time. Use the active locale from useLocale/i18n instead of hard-coding "en-US".

Call passes {} as data to updateManyByCredentialId: await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}). Prisma updateMany rejects empty data at runtime, so this always throws (or no-ops and never bumps updatedAt). The previously best-effort availability refresh now fails/blocks. Pass an explicit bump e.g. { updatedAt: new Date() }.
outros: WHAT: updateManyByCredentialId is called with empty data {} to bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. WHY: Prisma updateMany rejects empty data (validation error) or no-ops without touching @updatedAt, so the refresh path throws or silently leaves updatedAt stale. HOW: pass an explicit touch field e.g. { updatedAt: new Date() }.

Comment claims "Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt" but call passes empty object {} as data, so nothing is updated (Prisma updateMany with empty data is a no-op/error). Fix comment or pass { updatedAt: new Date() } to match the stated intent.

updateManyByCredentialId is called with empty data {}. Prisma updateMany throws when data is empty, so this line throws on every resync after the cache write. Pass an explicit touch e.g. { updatedAt: new Date() } instead of {}.

Pass an explicit touch field instead of {} — e.g. updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, { updatedAt: new Date() }) — empty `data` fails Prisma validation (data must not be empty) and does not bump updatedAt, so the stated update never occurs and can throw after caching.

Call passes `{}` as `data` to updateManyByCredentialId expecting it to bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. Prisma updateMany requires non-empty data and will reject/no-op on `{}`. Pass explicit timestamp e.g. `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` so the update succeeds and cache status advances.

goldens.comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems

Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

feat-add-calendar-cache-status-and-actio.prTitle: feat: add calendar cache status and actions (#22532)

grupos.texto: WHAT: `should_block?` mutates state (increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`, calls `record.save`) inside a method that is invoked from the model validation callback, and the signup controller runs validation twice per attempt (`user.valid?` at users_controller.rb:168 then `user.save` at :172). WHY: a single signup attempt increments `match_count` twice and rewrites `last_match_at`, so the per-email block statistics the feature was built to track are wrong. HOW: make the read side non-mutating for validation and record the match separately (e.g. move the increment out of validation, or guard it so it runs once per attempt), keeping the predicate pure.

The message shown for a rejected email disagrees with the reason the code is reacting to. This branch fires when the server rejected the email (result.errors.email), and this PR gives that condition its own server string — user.email.blocked, added in config/locales/server.en.yml as "is not allowed." — but the client re-labels it with the generic I18n.t('user.email.invalid'). A user whose address is perfectly well-formed but blocked/hosted on a blacklisted domain is therefore told their email is invalid, contradicting the reason just returned by the server. Use the blocked/not-allowed message (and add a matching client locale key) instead of user.email.invalid. Notice the same generic string is used at line ~94 for validation failures, so it should not be reused to represent a distinct server-side rejection.

This test is named "returns false if a record with the email doesn't exist," but it cannot verify that. `BlockedEmail.should_block?` returns `record && record.action_type == actions[:block]`, which yields `nil` (not `false`) when no record exists, and under this suite's RSpec 2 semantics `subject.should be_false` is a truthiness matcher that passes for any falsy value including `nil`. The assertion therefore passes on the nil the code actually returns and would only fail on an outright `true`; it does not pin the `false`/`nil` distinction its name asserts. Assert the value exactly (e.g. `subject.should == false`, or `be_falsey`/`be_nil` if nil is intended) so a regression returning a non-false falsy value is caught.

`should_block?` is declared/used as a boolean predicate (its name, its use in the validator's boolean context, and `spec/models/blocked_email_spec.rb:23`'s `be_false`), but the expression `record && record.action_type == actions[:block]` returns `nil` when no record matches instead of `false`. Coerce the result to a real boolean (e.g. `record.present? && record.action_type == actions[:block]`), otherwise the method's return contract as declared by its consumer/spec is violated.

should_block? matches with `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first`, an exact, case-sensitive comparison, and no side is normalised. Email identity is case-insensitive, so an address blocked as bad@spamclub.com is accepted when submitted as Bad@SpamClub.com — the blocklist is bypassable by changing case. Downcase (or otherwise normalise) both the stored value and the lookup value before comparing (e.g. `where(email: email.downcase)` with the record normalised on save), consistent with the case-insensitive domain regexp used in EmailValidator.
outros: WHAT: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` performs an exact, case-sensitive match, unlike the domain blacklist check which is matched case-insensitively (email_validator.rb:20 uses `Regexp.new(..., true)`). WHY: an address stored as `block@spam.com` is not matched by `Block@spam.com`/`BLOCK@SPAM.COM`, so the signup block can be trivially bypassed by varying the case of the email, defeating the spam-prevention control. HOW: normalize case before lookup (e.g. store/compare `email.downcase`) or query case-insensitively.

`this.get('rejectedEmails').contains(email)` is a case-sensitive membership test on an email address. Because the server-side blocklist lookup (BlockedEmail.should_block?) and this client check are both case-sensitive, re-submitting the rejected email with any character's case changed evades the client-side rejection. Normalise the address (e.g. toLowerCase) on both the pushObject at line 275 and this comparison so the rejected set cannot be bypassed by case variation.

grupos.texto: should_block? does a non-atomic read-modify-write on match_count: two concurrent requests for the same blocked email both read the same value, both add 1, and one increment is lost (last_match_at is likewise clobbered by whichever save lands last). Because this method runs on every email validation, collisions are likely under concurrent signups. Use an atomic UPDATE (e.g. BlockedEmail.where(email: email).update_all("match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?", Time.zone.now)) or wrap in with_lock/transaction so the counter is not silently corrupted.
outros: WHAT: `record.match_count += 1; record.last_match_at = ...; record.save` is a non-atomic read-modify-write with no lock or unique constraint protection. WHY: two concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email can both read the same `match_count` and one write overwrites the other, losing counts, so the tracked statistics drift under load. HOW: use an atomic update such as `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all('match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...')` or a database-level counter increment.

grupos.texto: Updating match statistics inside email validation counts a single blocked signup twice. UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, which validates again even when the first validation failed, so both invocations increment match_count. Record the attempt once at the signup boundary rather than as a side effect of each validation.

The match_count update is a read-modify-write operation without synchronization. Concurrent signup attempts for the same blocked email can both read the same count and save the same incremented value, losing matches and potentially overwriting last_match_at with an older timestamp. Use an atomic database increment with the timestamp update, or lock the row before reading and updating its statistics.
outros: The match counter update loses increments under concurrent validations. If two requests load a blocked email with match_count N before either saves, both assign N+1 and save, leaving N+1 despite two matches (and a later save can also overwrite a newer last_match_at). Use an atomic database increment with the timestamp update, or lock and reload the row before modifying the statistics.

The match counter loses increments under concurrent validations. Two calls can both load match_count = N, increment their separate records to N + 1, and save that same value, recording only one of two matches. Use an atomic database increment (or serialize the read/update with a row lock) so match_count measures every matching validation rather than only non-overlapping ones.

grupos.texto: Canonicalize blocked emails consistently with the application's Email.downcase identity handling, both when storing entries and when looking them up. This exact equality query is case-sensitive, and BlockedEmail's validation callback only defaults action_type. A block-list entry such as `Block@SpamFromHome.org` therefore does not block the same identity submitted/stored as `block@spamfromhome.org`. This is particularly relevant to the explicitly supported manually populated block list. Normalize existing/imported entries as well as new ones, and add a test with differing casing between the stored entry and the lookup.
outros: Blocked-email lookup compares the raw email without normalizing its domain. A signup for block@SPAMFROMHOME.ORG does not match a blocked record for block@spamfromhome.org despite identifying the same mailbox, allowing the signup restriction to be bypassed by changing domain capitalization. Normalize domains using Email.downcase both when storing blocked emails and when looking them up.

grupos.texto: should_block? now writes to the database (match_count and last_match_at, via save) and is called from EmailValidator during User validation. Validation used to be side-effect free, so every valid? call, including repeated validations and failed signups, now writes to blocked_emails and inflates match_count. The writes also run inside the validating transaction. Keep the lookup read-only in the validator and record the match statistics only when the block actually rejects a save, or use an atomic update_all increment.

should_block? increments match_count with a non-atomic read-modify-write (`record.match_count += 1; record.save`). Concurrent validations of the same blocked email overwrite each other and lose counts. Use an atomic SQL update instead, e.g. `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now])`.
outros: should_block? looks up the email with an exact, case-sensitive match, so a blocked address such as Bad@spam.org is bypassed by changing the case. Normalize the case on save and on lookup (e.g. downcase both). Its read-modify-write of match_count (+= 1 then save) is also racy and can lose concurrent increments; use an atomic update_all/increment_counter.

should_block? looks up the email with an exact, case-sensitive match, so a blocked address can be bypassed by changing case (e.g. Bad@SpamClub.com). Normalize both sides by downcasing the stored email on save and querying with email.downcase, or compare with LOWER(email) = ?.

grupos.texto: WHAT: EmailValidator.validate_each performs no email syntax/format check, only whitelist/blacklist and blocked lookup. WHY: Any arbitrary string passes validation when no restriction is configured, regressing the moved User#email_validator contract and allowing invalid emails to create accounts. HOW: Restore format validation (e.g. regex / presence of @/domain) before restriction checks.

WHAT: email_in_restriction_setting? builds unanchored Regexp "@(domains)" with only '.' escaped. WHY: Whitelist 'gmail.com' substring-matches 'victim@gmail.com.evil.com', so an attacker registers with an unapproved domain and bypasses the allow-list; blacklist similarly over/under-matches and other regex metachars are unescaped. HOW: Anchor and escape domains (e.g. Regexp.escape per domain split on '|' plus /\A[^@\s]+@(?:domain)\z/i).

WHAT: should_block? mutates match_count/last_match_at via read-modify-write save inside a validator. WHY: Every validation call (including re-validations of the same attempt or attempts failing on unrelated fields like username) inflates stats, and concurrent signups lose increments with no atomic update. HOW: Move stats update out of validation or use atomic increment (update_counters/increment_counter) only on actual blocked rejections.

WHAT: Rejection memory pushes result.values.email (server-side user.attributes value) but checks contains(raw accountEmail). WHY: If server normalizes (strip/case) the email, normalized != raw input so contains() misses and the client-side invalid marker fails to trigger on retry. HOW: Push the attempted raw email (or normalize both sides before compare/push).
Case-sensitivity bypass: BlockedEmail.where(email: email) is exact case-sensitive with no normalization, while sibling checks are case-insensitive. Normalize (downcase/strip) on write and lookup.

WHAT: emailValidation depends on 'rejectedEmails.@each' while rejections are added via pushObject of plain strings. WHY: @each observes properties of array items, not membership, so pushing a string does not invalidate the computed property and the remembered rejection error does not display until accountEmail itself changes. HOW: Depend on 'rejectedEmails.[]' (or 'rejectedEmails.length').
outros: Dependent key 'rejectedEmails.@each' will not invalidate when pushObject(result.values.email) adds a string; use 'rejectedEmails.[]' (or '.length'). As written the cached emailValidation won't recompute after a server email rejection, so the rejected email won't show inline invalid.

goldens.comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.

The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.

add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.prTitle: Add comprehensive email validation for blocked users

grupos.texto: The unsubscribe endpoint mutates notification_level (tu.save!) via a plain GET route (config/routes.rb:440-441) with skip_before_filter :check_xhr, authenticating only through the session cookie. There is no CSRF token (Rails forgery protection does not cover GET) and no capability token, unlike EmailController#unsubscribe which authorizes via DigestUnsubscribeKey. Any third-party page can embed and, when a logged-in user loads it, silently change that user's notification_level for the topic. Require a per-user capability token (like the digest unsubscribe key) in the URL, or perform the state change from an authenticated non-GET request that carries the CSRF token.

The `unsubscribe_url` added to the `message_with_unsubscribe` fixture is never asserted. The two tests only check that the List-Unsubscribe header `be_present` and that the body matches `user_preferences_url`; neither references `unsubscribe_url`. So they would still pass if the topic-specific unsubscribe URL this PR introduces were dropped or wired to the wrong value. Add an assertion (e.g. that `message_with_unsubscribe.body` matches `/t/1234/unsubscribe`, and that the List-Unsubscribe header points at the topic unsubscribe URL) so the new behaviour is actually covered.

This registers a top-level route named `topicUnsubscribe` (dasherizes to `topic-unsubscribe`), but the template added by this PR is at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, i.e. the nested route name `topic/unsubscribe`. The route `topicUnsubscribe` will therefore not find a template. Nest the route under the topic resource (or move the template to `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs`) so the route name, controller and template all resolve to the same name.

tu is not checked for nil before use. TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) returns nil whenever the logged-in user has no topic_users row for that topic (the same lookup TopicUser.get performs), and the next line dereferences tu.notification_level, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500. Because the route is only gated by ensure_logged_in, any logged-in user can hit /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe(.json) for a topic they never opened and trigger the crash. Guard the lookup, e.g. `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...); return render json: {success: false} unless tu` (or build/return early) before reading notification_level.
outros: `TopicUser.find_by(...)` can return nil (e.g. the user clicks the emailed unsubscribe link for a topic for which no TopicUser row was ever created), and the very next line dereferences it (`tu.notification_level > ...`, then `tu.save!`). This raises NoMethodError on nil and the unsubscribe request 500s. Guard the nil case (e.g. return early or use `TopicUser.change`/`find_or_create_by`) before reading/writing notification_level.

`tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (find_by yields nil when no row exists), but the next lines dereference it unconditionally (`tu.notification_level`, `tu.save!`). Since the new unsubscribe routes are public GET endpoints, any logged-in user visiting /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe for a topic they have never tracked will trigger a NoMethodError and a 500 instead of a sane response. Guard the nil case (e.g. create/skip or redirect) before reading notification_level.

grupos.texto: The `unsubscribe_link` translation now contains a required `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation, but only the per-topic notification mailer was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url` (app/mailers/user_notifications.rb:295). Any other caller that sends mail with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` and feeds this string through Email::MessageBuilder (`I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`, lib/email/message_builder.rb:67 and :90) without an `unsubscribe_url` in its opts — e.g. the site-wide digest, which is not topic-scoped — will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` when rendering. Either make the topic-specific line conditional (only emitted when `unsubscribe_url` is present) or add `unsubscribe_url` to every add_unsubscribe_link caller.
outros: The `unsubscribe_link` translation now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}` (config/locales/server.en.yml), but `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` is only given `unsubscribe_url` when the caller supplies it (user_notifications.rb:295). Any other email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but no `unsubscribe_url` will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument inside html_part at send time. Pass a default unsubscribe_url into template_args (or guard the interpolation) so the new placeholder is always satisfiable.

`unsubscribe_link` now unconditionally interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` renders this key for every email with `add_unsubscribe_link` set, using only the opts the caller passed. This PR wires `unsubscribe_url` into just the per-topic notification email (app/mailers/user_notifications.rb:295); any other `add_unsubscribe_link` email that doesn't pass it (e.g. the digest) will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument instead of rendering its unsubscribe footer. Either make the second sentence conditional on the argument being present, or supply `unsubscribe_url` at every `add_unsubscribe_link` call site.

The shared `unsubscribe_link` string now requires `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but that value is only produced in the notification mailer (`user_notifications.rb:295`). `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` (message_builder.rb:67) interpolates this same key for every message built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`; for emails that do not pass `unsubscribe_url` (e.g. digest/mailing-list emails sharing this generic translation) the `%{unsubscribe_url}` placeholder has no matching interpolation key and I18n raises `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument`, breaking those emails. Either supply `unsubscribe_url` in every mailer that sets `add_unsubscribe_link`, or guard the new sentence so the key is only required where the value is set.

grupos.texto: The title is interpolated unescaped and then emitted with triple braces. The controller (topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:6) builds stopNotificiationsText via I18n.t with { title: model.fancyTitle }, which performs no escaping, and this template renders it as {{{stopNotificiationsText}}}. Combined with the locale string "...notifications for {{title}}." (config/locales/client.en.yml:985), any markup in the topic title is injected as raw HTML. Escape the title before interpolation (or render the composed value escaped) so user-authored titles cannot inject HTML.
outros: Unescaped output of user-controlled content in the response. {{{stopNotificiationsText}}} uses a triple stache (no HTML escaping), and the controller builds that string by interpolating the raw topic title (`title: this.get("model.fancyTitle")`, topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:6) into an i18n string containing markup. A topic whose title contains HTML/script is injected verbatim into the unsubscribe page (stored XSS). Escape the title before interpolation, or render with escaped braces and put the <strong> in the template.

grupos.texto: The new GET routes mutate the authenticated user's notification preferences without CSRF verification. An attacker can navigate a logged-in user's browser to a known topic unsubscribe URL and reduce or mute its notifications, because Rails excludes GET from forgery-token checks and unsubscribe explicitly skips check_xhr. Make GET render a confirmation page and perform the preference change through a CSRF-protected POST or PUT.

The confirmation promises that the user will stop receiving notifications for this topic, but TopicsController#unsubscribe sets watching/tracking users to regular, not muted. Regular still allows mention/reply notifications, so this confirmation (and the corresponding promise in the new email link text) overstates what clicking the link accomplished. Describe stopping notifications for every new post, or make the confirmation conditional on the resulting notification level so only muted users are told that all topic notifications have stopped.

Make the unsubscribe URL absolute before passing it to the email builder (for example, prepend Discourse.base_url). Topic#unsubscribe_url appends `/unsubscribe` to the topic's site-relative URL, but the new server translation interpolates unsubscribe_url directly into an email Markdown link and MessageBuilder cooks it without adding the site origin. Unlike the post link in notification.html.erb, which explicitly prepends Discourse.base_url, this produces a `/t/.../unsubscribe` href that email clients cannot resolve to the forum, so the new per-topic unsubscribe link does not work reliably.

The unsubscribe action dereferences the result of TopicUser.find_by without handling a missing record. A logged-in user visiting the unsubscribe URL for a visible topic they have not previously visited gets a NoMethodError instead of being unsubscribed, because TopicView does not create that row. Handle the absent row with the regular default notification level and persist the selection through TopicUser.change, which supports creating missing records.
outros: Handle a missing TopicUser record before dereferencing it. A logged-in user can visit this URL for a topic they have not tracked or visited (for example, an unsubscribe link forwarded by another user); find_by then returns nil and tu.notification_level raises NoMethodError, returning a 500 instead of unsubscribing. Find or initialize the user's topic record, applying the default notification level before updating it.

grupos.texto: Saving the notification level directly leaves notifications_reason_id unchanged instead of recording an explicit user choice. For automatically tracked topics with a null reason, TopicUser.update_last_read promotes the row back to tracking when the reading threshold is exceeded, undoing the unsubscribe on the next read. Persist the change through TopicUser.change so notifications_reason_id and notifications_changed_at are set consistently with set_notifications.
outros: Saving the notification level directly bypasses the explicit-user-change metadata set by TopicUser.change. In particular, a topic_user with notifications_reason_id == nil remains eligible for TopicUser.auto_track, which checks that field and can promote the topic back to tracking after the user unsubscribes. Use the notification-change helper (or set its user-change reason and timestamp consistently) so the unsubscribe is retained as an explicit user preference.

grupos.texto: The client unsubscribe route only loads the ordinary topic view and never performs the unsubscribe operation. When entered through an in-app transition rather than a full server navigation, PostStream.loadTopicView requests /t/:id.json (or consumes preload data), so the page claims notifications will stop while the persisted notification level remains unchanged. Ensure this entry path executes the unsubscribe operation before showing confirmation.
outros: The client route loads the topic but never invokes the unsubscribe action. Notification levels are changed only by TopicsController#unsubscribe, so navigating to this route inside the Ember application can display “You will stop receiving notifications” without changing the subscription. Explicitly perform the unsubscribe operation on client-side entry rather than relying on the initial HTML request to have done it.

grupos.texto: The fixture now passes unsubscribe_url, but no assertion reads it. The tests only check that the List-Unsubscribe header is present and that the body contains user_preferences_url, so they pass if the topic unsubscribe link is removed or broken. Add an assertion that the body includes "/t/1234/unsubscribe".

`TopicUser.find_by` can return nil when the user has no topic_users row for this topic, for example when they were emailed through category watching and never visited the topic. `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError and the unsubscribe link returns a 500. Create the row if it is missing, for example with `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` or `find_or_initialize_by`. Treat a nil notification_level as the regular level.
outros: `TopicUser.find_by` can return nil when the user has no TopicUser row for the topic, and `notification_level` can also be nil. In either case `tu.notification_level > ...` raises NoMethodError and the unsubscribe link returns a 500. Fix: use `TopicUser.find_or_initialize_by(...)` or `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`, and treat a nil level as regular.

`TopicUser.find_by` can return nil when the user has no TopicUser row for the topic, for example an email recipient who never visited it. `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError. The level can also be nil. Use `TopicUser.find_or_initialize_by` and compare `(tu.notification_level || regular)`, or use `TopicUser.change`.

grupos.texto: The English `unsubscribe_link` string now requires `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `Email::MessageBuilder` renders it for every email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`, and `template_args` only carries `unsubscribe_url` when the caller passes it. Only `user_notifications.rb` was updated to pass it, so any other caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link` without `unsubscribe_url` gets a missing-interpolation error or a broken link. The other locale files also still lack the placeholder, so the per-topic link appears only in English. Make the second paragraph conditional on `unsubscribe_url` being present, or have every caller pass it.
outros: The `unsubscribe_link` translation now requires `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but only `UserNotifications#notification_email` was updated to pass it. Any other mailer that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` can fail with a missing interpolation argument when `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` or the text body renders it. Either have MessageBuilder only use the topic-unsubscribe variant when `unsubscribe_url` is present, or update every caller of `add_unsubscribe_link`. I did not confirm whether such callers exist.

grupos.texto: WHAT: The unsubscribe state change (lowering/muting notification_level + save!) runs on a GET route (config/routes.rb GET t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe). WHY: An attacker can forge the URL as an image/prefetch/link to silently change a victim's notification state with no CSRF token since GETs are not CSRF-protected. HOW: Make the mutation a PUT/POST with CSRF protection or require an explicit confirmation parameter/token instead of mutating on page view.

unsubscribe_link now requires %{unsubscribe_url} but not all MessageBuilder callers with add_unsubscribe_link:true supply it; missing arg raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument. Supply unsubscribe_url at all such call sites or provide a fallback/default in MessageBuilder.

outros: TopicUser.find_by can return nil, then tu.notification_level raises NoMethodError. Guard nil and anonymous current_user.

grupos.texto: WHAT: the `elsif` branch treats the last two dot-segments as the registrable domain, so multi-part public suffixes are mis-compared. WHY: for e.g. website_host='example.co.uk' and discourse_host='forum.co.uk' both have 3 segments, the branch compares `'co.uk' == 'co.uk'`, concludes the domains match, and returns `website_host + path`, even though example.co.uk and forum.co.uk are unrelated sites — the display then shows a path that does not belong to the instance domain, defeating the feature's purpose. HOW: compare against a public-suffix-aware registrable domain (e.g. use the PublicSuffix list) or require at least the full suffix before treating hosts as the same domain, instead of blindly taking `split('.')[1..-1]`.

The new `website_name` compares two domain names case-sensitively. `URI(website.to_s).host` preserves the letter case written by the user, whereas `Discourse.current_hostname` is the canonical lower-cased host, and no side is down-cased before the comparison at lines 141, 144-146 and 149 (including the `ends_with?` suffix check). Because DNS host names are case-insensitive identity values, `http://EXAMPLE.com/user` and `http://example.com/user` denote the same host but take different branches, so the same-site check is decided by letter case: the wrong arm is chosen and the full-path form is dropped. Normalise both sides before comparing, e.g. `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host&.downcase` (or use `URI(...).hostname`, which down-cases) and compare against `Discourse.current_hostname.to_s.downcase`.
Branch 2 ('www.example.com == forum.example.com') is not exercised by any test.
The scheme-less-website case (URI(...).host nil) is not exercised by any test.

WHAT: website_name re-exposes the user's website for profiles where it is intentionally hidden — the attribute is added to the public `attributes` list (line 43) but not to `untrusted_attributes`, and `include_website_name` only checks `website.present?` instead of `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. WHY: `website` is an untrusted attribute gated by `restrict_user_fields?` (lib/guardian/user_guardian.rb:58-60), which is true for a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous visitor; `website_name` derives `website_host + path` from the same `object.user_profile.website`, so the URL that `include_website?` suppresses is still disclosed through the new key (the existing spec at spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:11-14 only asserts the listed untrusted keys are absent, so this leak is not covered). HOW: add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (or have `include_website_name` return false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`), mirroring the `website` handling.
outros: `website_name` is derived from the same `object.user_profile.website` value that `:website` protects via `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111), but it is only gated by `include_website_name` -> `website.present?`. Since the untrusted filter removes `website` for some viewers while `website_name` is still emitted, and in the same-domain / subdomain branches it returns host *plus* `URI(website).path` (lines 143/146/149), the user's full website URL still leaves in the response for viewers the filter was supposed to strip it from. Either add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` or gate `include_website_name` with the same trust condition as `website`.

The new `website_name` field is gated only on `website.present?`, ignoring the visibility constraint this file declares for its source attribute: lines 105-111 put `:website` in `untrusted_attributes`, so `website` is omitted for viewers not allowed to see profile fields, but `website_name` is still serialized because `include_website_name` never consults that condition. Those viewers now receive the user's URL host, and when the host equals (lines 141-143) or is a parent of (144-149) the instance host they receive host + path, i.e. the complete URL that `website` was supposed to hide. Fix by adding `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (105-111) — or make the guard reuse `website`'s own inclusion condition instead of a bare presence check.

grupos.texto: The conditional-inclusion guard is named `include_website_name`, but ActiveModelSerializers resolves these guards as `include_<attribute>?` (the sibling in this very file is `include_email?` at line 117). As written the method is never called, so the guard is dead and the `:website_name` attribute declared at line 43 is serialized unconditionally. That defeats the intent of the guard (`website.present?`): the payload now always carries `website_name`, including for the scopes where `website` itself is withheld by the `untrusted_attributes` list (line 109), leaking the user's site host/path to viewers who were never meant to receive the website.
